Tuberous-rooted subshrub native to the southwestern United States and Central and South America. Soft greyish hairs cover its stems and leaves, while its white trumpet-shaped flowers become downward-inclined and its fruit is a spiny capsule. All parts are toxic and may be fatal if swallowed.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are toxic and may be fatal if eaten by people or animals.

stories.summary: A herbaceous perennial native to temperate Asia and Europe, it has deeply divided leaves and upright spikes of blue or purple summer flowers. Ornamental cultivars also include pink, cream and white forms.

A deciduous flowering shrub native to Japan, Deutzia scabra grows naturally along forest edges and rocky openings. It bears clusters of white flowers from May to July, with upper leaves clasping the stem and lower leaves growing on stalks.

A herbaceous perennial native to northern China, Korea, Mongolia and southeastern Russia. Its slender green to grey-green leaves remain on the stems while the basal leaves usually wither during flowering. White, pink or red flowers appear alone or in small clusters from spring to midsummer, often with darker centres and serrated edges.
A moss with a cosmopolitan distribution.

A fast-growing creeping flowering plant distributed disjunctly from the southern United States through Mexico and parts of South America, with extinction reported in Arizona. It has dark green, kidney- or ear-shaped leaves, tiny whitish flowers and hairy capsules with dark seeds.

A perennial creeping herb native to Australia, New Zealand, Mauritius, Réunion and Rodrigues. It roots at the nodes and has soft, greyish-haired, kidney-shaped to round leaves with small, pale greenish-yellow, star-shaped flowers. It is cultivated as an ornamental groundcover or lawn substitute.

A moss found across Europe, parts of Asia, and from North America to northwestern South America. Its bright green to yellow-green mats are especially recognizable in late summer and autumn, when they are strewn with needle-like yellowish shoots; spore capsules are very rare.

Moss occurring in parts of Europe, Asia and North America, with its European range centred on mountainous Central Europe. It forms loose to moderately dense dark-green or yellow-brown carpets and has brittle, weakly sickle-shaped leaves; spore capsules are produced only very rarely.
A moss native to the Northern Hemisphere, including Japan.

A large perennial fern found throughout Asia and Oceania, it has an upright rhizome covered in short reddish-brown scales. Its long brownish leaf stalks have black, scaly bases. Young fronds are stir-fried or used in salads; they may contain mild fern toxins, though no major toxic effects are recorded.
stories.edibilityNote: Young fronds are stir-fried or used in salads; they may contain mild fern toxins, but no major toxic effects are recorded.

stories.summary: A liverwort native to Brazil, Dumortiera hirsuta is the sole species in its genus.

A flowering shrub native from Mexico and the Caribbean south to South America. It bears clusters of blue or lavender flowers followed by yellow or orange berries, while mature plants often develop thorns. Its leaves and unripe berries are toxic, although documented human cases are sparse.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves and unripe berries are toxic; human reports are sparse, including one historical presumed fatal berry poisoning.

stories.summary: Flowering plant endemic to Brazil, also known as sawblade. It has a cultivar called ‘Yellow Glow’ and is a parent of several hybrid cultivars.

A herbaceous perennial native to southern Europe, northwestern Africa and southwestern Asia. It has rough, bristly leaves and hairy fruit resembling tiny cucumbers. When ripe, the fruit detaches and forcefully squirts seed-bearing liquid.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit-juice extract is poisonous when taken by mouth or nose; it was historically used medicinally as a powerful purgative.

stories.summary: Perennial herb native to North America, especially the Great Plains of central Canada and the central United States. Its stems and leaves are hairy, and each long flower stalk ends in a head of pink or purple outer florets surrounding numerous orange florets.

Perennial cactus native to the Chihuahuan Desert and parts of northern Mexico and the southern United States. Young plants are spherical but become cylindrical, growing alone or in clusters with stems largely hidden by dense, variously coloured spines. Its pink or purple flowers each open for only one day, though staggered blooming can continue for a week.

A solitary cactus native to Chihuahua and Sonora in Mexico and Arizona and New Mexico in the United States, it rarely branches or forms offsets. Its new spines are reddish to magenta before fading to yellow or light pink, and its bright-pink flowers have white throats.

A branching perennial herb native to central and eastern Europe, from Germany and Italy east into Russia. It is described as the largest globe thistle and produces nearly spherical flower heads of white or pale blue florets.
A compact, bushy perennial thistle native to southern and eastern Europe and western and central Asia. It has broad prickly leaves and globes of steel-blue flowers in late summer.

An upright biennial found across the western Mediterranean; the supplied source does not explicitly describe this range as native. Its stems and leaves carry stiff bristles, while its funnel-shaped flowers may be reddish-purple, bluish-purple or change from pinkish-red to blue.

sources.title: Echium creticum L.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Deciduous or semi-evergreen shrub or small tree native to China, Korea, Japan and Sakhalin in the Russian Far East. Its leaves are green above and silvery to orange-brown beneath. The juicy fruit is edible when ripe in mid- to late summer, with a sweet but astringent, rhubarb-like taste.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe fruit is eaten in mid- to late summer; it is juicy, sweet but astringent, and has fragile skin.

stories.summary: A dense evergreen shrub native to Asia, including China and Japan, thorny olive has thorn-covered stems and leaves with silvery-white, brown-flecked undersides. Its sweet-scented yellowish or white flowers bloom in autumn, followed by reddish, silver-scaled fruit in spring.
A flowering plant native from the temperate and subtropical Old World to western Malesia, it is introduced in New England, where it occurs mainly around rivers.
A plant native from Europe through the Russian Far East and Nepal, and from subarctic America south to the northern United States.

Orchid with no explicitly stated native origin; it occurs from Florida and the Caribbean through Central America to northern Brazil and the Guyanas. Its flowers usually self-pollinate, sometimes before opening.

A flowering plant found across Britain, Ireland, most of Europe, and central and eastern Asia, while introduced elsewhere. It has mostly opposite, toothed leaves and pale mauve flowers, and commonly grows on disturbed or base-rich ground, in hedges and as a garden weed.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, the Azores and Madeira. It grows in very wet places on siliceous ground, including stream margins, seepage slopes and rocks, and waterlogged meadows.

An evergreen horsetail whose native origin is not specified in the supplied information; its named varieties range across much of Europe, Asia and Africa, with one extending to Indonesia and Papua New Guinea. It can form colonies from underground roots and has untidy lower branches, sometimes with a blue-grey tinge.

A grass native to the Old World tropics, Eragrostis ciliaris has also been introduced across tropical and subtropical parts of the Americas and some Pacific islands. Its small, nutritious seeds are edible but difficult to harvest and handle, so they are usually regarded as famine food.
stories.edibilityNote: The small, nutritious seeds are edible but difficult to harvest and handle, and are usually regarded as famine food.

stories.summary: A strongly branched evergreen shrub native to the Himalayas, western China, India and Nepal. Its vivid gentian-blue flowers emerge from green-and-white veined bracts that remain after flowering, and its large dark-green leaves are hairy.

A warm-season lawn grass native to southern China, centipede grass forms thick sod and spreads by creeping stems. Its coarse, light-to-medium green growth tolerates some shade but has shallow roots and poor drought tolerance.
A perennial subshrub native to western Europe, cross-leaved heath has glandular leaves arranged in groups of four. Small pink, bell-shaped flowers droop in compact clusters during summer and autumn.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

Perennial herb native to the eastern Mediterranean. It forms clumps of spiny, leathery leaves and bears cylindrical summer flower clusters above silvery-blue bracts and branching light-blue to purple stems.

A hairless, spiny perennial with two natural varieties ranging across parts of Europe, North Africa and western Asia. It bears small greenish flower heads surrounded by large spine-like bracts. Its roots were formerly candied as sweets or boiled and roasted as a vegetable, while the plant has long featured in local dishes in Iran’s Mazandaran Province.
stories.edibilityNote: Roots were formerly candied, boiled or roasted; the plant has been used in Mazandaran dishes for centuries.

stories.summary: A coastal perennial flowering plant native to most of Europe and the Mediterranean, sea holly has bluish-grey, stiff, spiny leaves and compact flower heads resembling a thistle. Its roots were formerly candied as sweetmeat, while young shoots may be eaten like asparagus.
stories.edibilityNote: Roots were formerly candied as sweetmeat, and young shoots may be eaten like asparagus.

stories.summary: A herbaceous perennial native to central and southeastern Europe and Central Asia, blue eryngo has branched silvery-blue stems. Numerous small blue, cone-shaped flower heads surrounded by spiky bracts appear in summer.

Flowering tree native to Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, southern Brazil and Paraguay. It has irregular, spiny branches and bright red flowers, and grows wild along watercourses and in swamps and wetlands.

A bulbous perennial native to central and southern Europe, from Portugal to Ukraine. It has paired marbled leaves and solitary pink or lilac flowers, rarely white, whose petals bend backwards. The white bulb resembles a dog’s tooth.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves may be eaten raw in salads or boiled as a vegetable; starch from the bulb is used to make vermicelli.

stories.summary: A spreading flowering shrub native to southern Chile and neighboring Argentina, redclaws has glossy, serrated evergreen leaves and bark that changes from red to gray as it ages. Its pink to crimson trumpet-shaped flowers bloom from July to October in the Northern Hemisphere.

A tree native to southeastern Australia, bangalay has rough bark on its trunk and branches and bears white flowers in summer and autumn. After bushfire, it can resprout from buds beneath its bark or from its swollen woody base.
A small to medium-sized tree native only to south-eastern Australia. It has rough, fibrous bark, often retains rounded blue-grey juvenile leaves, and produces white flowers in groups of three.

A tree, sometimes growing as a multi-stemmed mallee, endemic to southwestern Western Australia. It has rough fibrous trunk bark, elongated horn-tipped flower buds and exceptionally hard, strong timber.

A small to medium-sized tree endemic to eastern Australia, it has thick, deeply furrowed grey-black ironbark extending from its trunk to small branches. Its white flowers are rich in nectar, while its hard, dark-red timber is used in construction.

Large tree native to southwestern Western Australia, mainly along a narrow coastal corridor. It has rough, box-like bark, glossy leaves and white to cream flowers, with major flowering events every five to eight years.
stories.edibilityNote: The flowers are used to produce honey, historically regarded as high quality but an unreliable source.

stories.summary: A tree endemic to New South Wales, grey ironbark has dark, deeply furrowed bark on its trunk and branches. Its glossy curved leaves accompany clusters of mostly seven buds, white flowers and woody cup-shaped to conical fruit.
Tree native to eastern Australia. It grows in swampy or waterlogged ground and has thick, spongy reddish-brown bark, a dense canopy and white to cream flowers in autumn and winter.

A medium-sized to tall tree endemic to eastern Australia, the Sydney blue gum has rough, flaky bark near the trunk’s base and smooth bark above. Its white flowers grow from buds grouped in sevens, nines or elevens, followed by woody cylindrical, conical or cup-shaped fruit.

A moss of the sub-Mediterranean flora, lime-seep eucladium occurs mainly in southern and western Europe, with populations on several other continents. It forms dense olive, pale or bluish-green mats often crusted with lime and favors wet, lime-rich rocks and seepages.
A compact, clump-forming deciduous perennial native to Libya, Turkey, and eastern, middle and southeastern Europe. It bears acid-yellow flower heads at branch tips in spring and summer.

Herbaceous perennial native to central and southern Europe and much of temperate Asia. It has yellow-green flower bracts, explosively opening seed capsules and an extensive root system. All parts contain toxic white milky sap.

A flowering plant whose two named subspecies are native to mainland Portugal; subsp. exigua is also native to Madeira but introduced in the Azores. Both occur in annual grasslands, fallow ground, roadsides and wasteland, often on poor, somewhat disturbed soils. Subsp. exigua has tubercled seeds, while subsp. merinoi has transverse grooves and some tubercles.
A spurge native to most of Europe, northern Africa and Asia, it has two recognised subspecies. One is restricted to Cyprus and western Turkey, while the other occurs throughout the species’ range.
Spurge-family plant native to Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, much of Andean South America, Suriname and French Guiana.

A woody succulent shrub native to Madagascar. It has densely spiny stems and fleshy leaves concentrated on new growth, though its form varies among cultivars. Small flowers framed by conspicuous red, pink or white bracts may appear throughout the year.
stories.edibilityNote: Its moderately poisonous sap causes severe stomach pain, mouth and throat irritation, and vomiting if ingested.

stories.summary: An annual herb whose native origin is not stated in the supplied information. It is self-supporting with simple broad leaves, and its flowers are visited by Plagiolepis pygmaea, Polistes and nomad bees.

A perennial herb native to Europe, serrated spurge has mostly long, narrow leaves, with more oval leaves near the stem tips. Its leaves are finely toothed, and its spherical fruits contain tiny grey seeds.

A shrub or small tree native to Africa, especially widespread in its northeastern, central and southern regions. Its smooth, succulent green branches resemble pencils, and its milky sap is toxic and corrosive, causing severe irritation and potentially temporary blindness.
stories.edibilityNote: The milky latex is toxic; ingestion can burn the mouth, lips and tongue.

stories.summary: A small evergreen shrub native to southern Africa, it is compact, densely branched and leafy. It grows in varied settings including forest edges, riverine bush, ravines, coastal scrub and grassland.

A deciduous shrub of unstated native origin, pearl bush is found mostly in China and Japan. It has a loose, upright form and clusters of round-petalled white flowers in late April to early May, followed by brown seed capsules.

A large evergreen fig tree native to southeastern Asia and many Pacific islands. It often begins life on another tree, sending roots to the ground and eventually overwhelming its host. Pollinated flowers develop inside orange-red, many-seeded figs.

A woody evergreen climber native to East Asia, including southern China, southern Japan, southern Korea and Vietnam. Its juvenile leaves are much smaller and thinner than its mature foliage, and it creeps over ground or climbs trees and walls.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit of var. awkeotsang is inverted and dried; seed-surface gel is extracted with water and set as aiyu or ice jelly.

stories.summary: A North American moss also widespread through Northern Hemisphere forests, maidenhair pocketmoss forms robust dark green to brown-green mats. Its wavy, finely toothed leaves tend to curl downward at their tips when dry.

A moss of unstated native origin with a broad global distribution. It forms green mats chiefly on shaded, lime-rich rocks and soils, and has leaves with coarse teeth and a pale border of thick-walled cells.
A terrestrial moss with a cosmopolitan distribution. It has been recorded rarely at La Bouzaréah and Aït Idjer in Algeria.

sources.title: Fissidens exilis Hedw.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A moss with no native origin stated in the supplied information. It is the largest member of its family and grows in turbulent water; its fronds were likened to phoenix feathers in China.

A moss with a nearly worldwide distribution, especially common in the Northern Hemisphere, though it is introduced in New Zealand. It forms dense green tufts with flattened leaves in two rows, resembling tiny fern fronds, and usually grows on soil or soil-covered rocks in wet, shaded places.

A deciduous flowering shrub native to China, golden-bell produces golden-yellow flowers in early spring. Its weeping form can grow along stream banks, and it also occurs naturally in thickets and grassy areas on slopes and in valleys.
Liverwort native to Europe and America.
A tree native to eastern and northeastern Mexico and the south-central United States, it produces male and female flowers on separate trees.
A liverwort with a cosmopolitan distribution. In Europe it occurs on rocks and tree trunks, especially beech, while Algerian records describe it as rare.

sources.title: Frullania tamarisci (L.) Dumort.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A flowering sub-shrub native to the lower Southern Cone of South America. Its long arching stems bear many small, hanging tubular flowers over a long period, commonly in vivid red and purple. It is relatively cold-hardy, becoming deciduous in light frost and dying back above ground in harder frost.
A tall shrub or small tree native to Central America, it usually has smooth, upright branches. Its nearly round fruit is bluish-purple with a whitish waxy coating.

A flowering subshrub native to the Caribbean and northern South America, it is generally stemless and bears sword-shaped leaves ending in sharp tips. Its strongly scented, greenish to creamy-white flowers grow on a very tall stalk, after which the flowering section dies back and usually leaves young plants around its base.

An annual flowering herb native only to Texas in the south-central United States. It grows in sunny, sandy places and bears red or purple rays, rarely yellow, around yellow disc flowers with purple tips.

An annual herb native to much of Europe, white bedstraw has mostly upright, slightly ridged square stems and shiny, nearly hairless leaves. Its flowers are white or yellowish, and its fruits are hairless.
Plant native to Europe from Portugal to Ukraine. Known as waxy bedstraw, it is only sparingly naturalized in a few locations in Quebec, Ontario, Connecticut and New Jersey.

A herbaceous annual native to virtually all of Europe and parts of North Africa, Asia, Greenland and eastern North America. In Britain it grows on poorly drained neutral or acidic soils, while several northeastern US states classify it as a noxious weed.
An annual grass native to Europe, North Africa and southwestern Asia, nit grass bears a long, thin, smooth flower head of spikelets. It has become naturalized in scattered locations elsewhere.

Evergreen flowering shrub native to La Palma and Tenerife in the Canary Islands. Its narrow leaves have fine, silky silver hairs, and its strongly scented yellow flowers appear in late winter or early spring.

A deciduous shrub native to meadows and pastures in Europe and Turkey, dyer’s greenweed bears golden-yellow, pea-like flowers and shiny bean-shaped pods. Since ancient times it has been used to produce yellow dye, or green when combined with woad.
Herbaceous perennial of unstated native origin, it is found mainly in the eastern United States. Its clustered autumn flowers are white with distinctive purple stripes, and its seeds are wingless.
A herbaceous perennial native to Texas and Mexico, it behaves as an annual in temperate climates. It has a tuberous root and red, strawberry-like flower heads.

An erect shrub or slender tree endemic to Queensland, with divided leaves bearing narrow lobes. Its clustered flowers range from creamy white to bright scarlet or crimson, while its flowers and seed pods contain toxic hydrogen cyanide.
stories.edibilityNote: Flowers and seed pods contain toxic hydrogen cyanide.

stories.summary: A moss with no explicitly documented native origin. It forms loose yellow-green to dark-green mats that shimmer grey from their hair points. Its leaves lie loosely against the stem and twist when dry, but spread outward when wet; it fruits quite rarely.

An annual herb native to Ethiopia, Eritrea and Malawi, Niger has yellow flower heads and small black seeds resembling sunflower seeds. The seeds are eaten in southern India in chutney or curries, and their clear, nutty oil can be used directly for cooking.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds are eaten in southern India in chutney or curries; their oil is edible and may be used directly for cooking.

stories.summary: A moss with a cosmopolitan distribution. It is recorded as common across numerous Algerian localities, including Tlemcen, Constantine, the Djurdjura region and El-Kala National Park.

sources.title: Gymnostomum calcareum Nees & Hornsch.
sources.attribution: Ros R M, Olaf S R, Eloy O W, Cerón E, plazi (2024). Revisiting the Bryophyte Checklist of Algeria: Exploring Diversity and Distribution. Cryptogamie, Bryologie. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/6xu7ry accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An evergreen flowering perennial native to Southeast Asia, purple passion plant is widely grown as a houseplant. Its dark-green leaves, stems and flower bracts are covered in soft purple hairs, giving it a velvety appearance, while its yellow, orange or red flowers have a strong smell.

A mat-forming herbaceous perennial native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, where it grows on dry, chalky slopes. Through much of summer it bears masses of star-shaped white, lilac or light-purple flowers.

A flowering tree native to southern Mexico and introduced to the Caribbean, northern Central America and elsewhere. Its wood was extensively exported to Europe for fabric dyeing from the 17th through 19th centuries and remains a source of haematoxylin stain.
A bromeliad native to southern Texas, Mexico and Guatemala.

An evergreen climbing plant native to the Middle East, Persian ivy clings to trees, cliffs and walls with aerial rootlets. Its five-lobed juvenile leaves give way to unlobed adult leaves, and it has the largest leaves of any ivy.

An evergreen climber native to Europe’s Atlantic coast, it clings to trees, cliffs and walls with aerial rootlets or spreads as ground cover. The whole plant, including its blue-black berries, is slightly poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: The whole plant and its berries are slightly poisonous.

stories.summary: A moss with a cosmopolitan distribution. It has been recorded rarely at several Algerian localities, including the Djurdjura region, Blida Atlas and Akfadou.

sources.title: Hedwigia ciliata (Hedw.) P. Beauv.
sources.attribution: Ros R M, Olaf S R, Eloy O W, Cerón E, plazi (2024). Revisiting the Bryophyte Checklist of Algeria: Exploring Diversity and Distribution. Cryptogamie, Bryologie. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/6xu7ry accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed around the Mediterranean. It grows in dry grasslands on siliceous, limestone or sometimes sandy ground. Its upper leaves are lance-shaped, while its small petals may be no longer than the sepals or entirely absent.

sources.title: Helianthemum salicifolium (L.) Mill.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An annual herb endemic to Texas, the Texas sunflower grows mainly in sandy coastal prairies along the Gulf Coast and in the Río Grande Valley. It usually carries one to three flower heads with yellow outer florets surrounding red or purple centres.
A flowering plant of unstated native origin, introduced in mainland Portugal and Madeira. In Portugal it occurs in gardens and has escaped onto coastal cliffs, dunes and woodland clearings.
An erect herb native to northern South America and the West Indies. Its upward-facing flowers collect rainwater for birds and insects, and bats and hummingbirds typically pollinate it.

An herbaceous perennial native to southern Mexico, Central America and northern South America, and naturalized in Florida and Jamaica. Its banana-like leaves accompany an upright flower cluster with red or orange bracts surrounding green, yellow or orange flowers.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in dry watercourse beds on somewhat moist sandy soils, which may be slightly salty or nutrient-enriched.

sources.title: Heliotropium supinum L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A semi-evergreen flowering perennial native to central and western Europe, including southern England. It bears green flowers in spring. All parts are poisonous; eating any part can cause severe vomiting and seizures.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous; consumption can cause severe vomiting and seizures.

stories.summary: A clump-forming daylily found in China, northeastern Italy and Slovenia, yellow daylily bears sweetly scented, lemon-yellow flowers. Its flowers are edible and are used in Chinese and Japanese cuisine.
stories.edibilityNote: The flowers are edible and used in Chinese and Japanese cuisine.

stories.summary: Roughly hairy perennial herb native to most of Europe, western Asia and northern Africa. Its sap may cause burns or rashes in sensitive people when contaminated skin meets sunlight. Pickled stems, leaves and flower clusters were historically used in an early form of borscht; young shoots are foraged and dried seeds used as a spice.
stories.edibilityNote: Historically, pickled stems, leaves and flower clusters made an early borscht; young shoots are foraged, and dried seeds are used as a spice.

stories.summary: A flowering plant whose recorded varieties glaberrima and setulosa are native to mainland Portugal. Both occur in sparse plant communities in paving cracks, along paths and in disturbed places, on clay-rich or stony soils.

A flowering plant with no stated native origin, it is found in North America. It is believed extinct in Connecticut and is listed as endangered in Illinois and Ohio. The Cherokee apply a hot root poultice to inflamed wounds and sores.
A semi-deciduous shrub or small tree native to southern China. Its single or double flowers open white or pink and deepen to red by evening, while its stems and leaf stalks are densely hairy.

A flowering plant native to most of Europe, common hawkweed has pale yellow flowers throughout summer. Its flower heads lack central florets, while the stalks below them bear scattered black hairs and contain a milky substance.

A hawkweed native to Europe, it has become naturalized in parts of North America and is considered a noxious weed in Washington state. It grows in fields, roadsides and forests, usually in well-drained soil.
A bulbous perennial native to tropical South America, though naturalized elsewhere. Its orange-red flowers appear before the bright green, strap-shaped leaves are fully developed.

An evergreen, sprawling shrub from the Himalayas through India and Nepal to Myanmar. Its red to orange-red flowers have broad, saucer-like calyces and long curved floral tubes; some varieties flower yellow or bronze.

A hardy deciduous tree found across Asia from eastern China and Korea to the Himalayas. It has glossy pointed leaves and clusters of small cream flowers. Its sweet, fragrant fleshy fruit stalk is edible raw or cooked and resembles raisins when dried.
stories.edibilityNote: The fleshy fruit stalk is eaten raw or cooked; when dried, it looks and tastes like raisins.

stories.summary: Aquatic plant native to South America, Central America, Puerto Rico, Trinidad and the Netherlands Antilles. Known as water poppy, it is grown in decorative ponds and has naturalized in several warmer regions worldwide.

Hairless creeping perennial native to parts of tropical Africa, the western Indian Ocean, the southeastern and south-central United States, Central America, the Caribbean and South America. It roots where its stems touch the ground and bears numerous white to creamy-yellow flowers.
A moss with a cosmopolitan distribution. It can grow under artificial light in places without natural light, including Niagara Cave.
An aquatic flowering plant native to Bangladesh, India, China and Malaysia. Popular in tropical aquariums, it grows and reproduces rapidly, and leaves near strong light may turn pink or orange.
A herbaceous perennial native to China and Korea. It has upright succulent stems, frosted-blue leaves, and flat clusters of star-shaped pink flowers from summer until the first frost.

A small, fragile perennial fern most frequent in western Europe’s oceanic regions, especially the British Isles. Its translucent leaves are only a single cell thick, and creeping underground stems produce dense colonies of overlapping leaves.

A plant native to Southern Europe, North Africa, West Asia and Macaronesia, white henbane is sticky and covered in woolly, glandular hairs. Its mostly yellowish-white flowers have green or purple throats, and the plant is described as slightly poisonous.

Black henbane is a poisonous plant native to temperate Europe and Siberia. Its foliage and seeds contain psychoactive chemicals, and ingestion can cause hallucinations, delirium, coma or death; historically, it was used to flavour beer before hops replaced it between the 11th and 16th centuries.
stories.edibilityNote: Historically, henbane was used to flavour beer, but it fell from use when hops replaced it between the 11th and 16th centuries.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Hyoscyamus niger
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Most current Portuguese records come from sparse grasslands on sandy river beaches or flood deposits of the Tagus and Douro, though it is also reported from field grasslands and roadsides, preferably on basic soils.

A flowering plant with no native origin stated, claspingleaf St. John’s wort occurs from Florida to New York and in Guatemala. It favors wet habitats and has yellow, five-petalled flowers, with upper leaves much larger than lower ones.

A low-growing perennial flowering plant found in Western Europe. Its thin trailing stems carry pale green leaves with tiny translucent glands and black-edged dots, while its yellow flowers often have a few black spots.

Perennial flowering herb native to Europe and Western Asia, where it grows in moist meadows. Its square stems bear opposite leaves with few or no translucent glands, while black dots may mark the leaves, petals and sepals. The flowers are yellow.

A widespread moss found on every continent except Antarctica, growing on trunks, logs, walls and rocks. Its creeping stems form dense mats of overlapping, curved leaves resembling miniature cypress branches.

Moss of unspecified native origin, widely distributed in Europe and the Aleutian Islands and also found elsewhere. It showed intermediate sensitivity to the herbicide Asulam in a study of moss growth.

An evergreen shrub native to South Africa, Madagascar and Southeast Asia, it forms compact growth with green leaves heavily spotted in pink or white, as if sprayed with paint. The spots may merge into larger colored areas, and cultivated forms range from white through pink to red.

A shrub native to Southern Europe, the Middle East and the region around the Caspian Sea. It has upright branches with dark-green leaves and fragrant summer flowers that may be pink, blue or, more rarely, white.
stories.edibilityNote: According to Chaeremon, Egyptian priests ate hyssop with bread for ritual purification; its essential oil can cause seizures, even at low doses in children.

stories.summary: An annual flowering plant native to Belgium, France, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, Spain and Switzerland. It has four prominently unequal petals; wild plants have white or pale violet flowers, while cultivated varieties may be deeper pink, violet or fuchsia.

A flowering evergreen subshrub native to southern Europe. It forms spreading mounds of glossy foliage and fragrant white flower clusters in spring and early summer, often cascading over rocks and walls.

Holly-family shrub native to coastal areas of the United States from Virginia to Texas. It grows mainly beneath pine forests and in moist or wet sandy habitats, resprouts from underground stems after controlled burning, and provides important nectar for beekeepers.

A slow-growing evergreen shrub native to eastern China and Korea. Its glossy rectangular leaves usually have four or five marginal spines, while dull white spring flowers are followed by large red berries ripening in early autumn.

Perennial grass native to tropical and subtropical Asia, Micronesia, Melanesia, Australia, Africa and southern Europe, cogon grass forms dense stands linked by extensive underground stems. Its sharp-pointed, finely toothed leaves have an off-centre pale main vein, and it is highly flammable even when apparently green.
stories.edibilityNote: Young flower clusters and shoots may be eaten cooked; the roots contain starch and sugars.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to coastal Portugal from Nazaré to Sagres, violet cress mainly inhabits wet sand in clearings among junipers, pine forests and dry scrub.

A flowering bush of unspecified native origin, it has rich green, heart-shaped leaves. Its hollow stems were historically used in Brazil to make tobacco-pipe tubes, while its seeds and leaves are toxic when eaten.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds and leaves are toxic when eaten.

stories.summary: A twining or trailing perennial climber probably originating in tropical Africa and now cultivated throughout the tropics. It has heart-based leaves and pale-yellow, funnel-shaped flowers with purple inside the base; its slender stems are hairy.

sources.title: Ipomoea ochracea G.Don
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.title: Ipomoea ochracea (Lindl.) G.Don
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A flowering perennial native to Japan, China, Korea and Russia, Japanese iris is widely grown as an ornamental. It has strap-shaped leaves and purple midsummer flowers with a flash of yellow.

A rhizomatous perennial native to Asia Minor, this iris forms large clumps and has white flowers marked with a prominent egg-yolk-yellow area. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental and has naturalized in several countries.
stories.edibilityNote: Most parts, particularly the rhizomes and leaves, are poisonous if eaten and may cause stomach pain and vomiting.

stories.summary: A hardy flowering perennial native to Croatia's Dalmatian coast, sweet iris grows from a rhizome and bears bluish-green sword-shaped leaves with pale purple to whitish flowers. Oil extracted from its rhizome, called orris root, is used to flavor foods, drinks and gin as well as perfumes.
stories.edibilityNote: Orris oil extracted from the rhizome is used to flavor foods, drinks and gin.

stories.summary: A rhizomatous flowering plant native to temperate eastern Asia, it has grey-green leaves, unbranched stems and early-summer flowers ranging from blue to red-violet, with rare white forms. Most parts, including the rhizome and leaves, are poisonous if eaten and may cause stomach pain and vomiting.
stories.edibilityNote: Most parts, particularly the rhizome and leaves, are poisonous if eaten and can cause stomach pain and vomiting.

stories.summary: A bulbous iris native to Spain and Portugal. It bears blue, violet, white or yellow flowers, typically but not always in May and June, while its grey-green leaves emerge in autumn and die after flowering. Florists value its striking colour combinations.

Evergreen flowering shrub native to Vietnam and southern China. It has fragrant yellow flowers from spring into summer, potentially year-round in warmer climates, and a scrambling habit that can be trained as a slender climber.
Shrub native to India, Nepal, Bhutan, Laos, Burma, Thailand and Vietnam. Unlike many jasmines, its attractive white flowers have no scent and are used in worship in Manipur.

A slender deciduous shrub native to China, winter jasmine has arching green shoots and a trailing, vine-like form. In the Northern Hemisphere, its bright yellow or white flowers appear from November to March, often on bare stems.
A deciduous flowering climber native to parts of Asia, though its exact country of origin is uncertain. It bears clusters of star-shaped white summer flowers with an intense fragrance.
stories.edibilityNote: Jasmine is recognized as safe as a food ingredient by the US Food and Drug Administration.

stories.summary: Flowering shrub or small tree native to Cuba and Hispaniola. It has a swollen trunk and three-lobed leaves whose middle lobe is much larger than the others. Male and female flowers occur separately.
A garden plant native to Mexico and the Caribbean, coralbush has been introduced across several tropical and subtropical regions. It is mildly toxic, and consumption causes gastrointestinal distress.
stories.edibilityNote: Consumption is mildly toxic and causes gastrointestinal distress.

stories.summary: Flowering rush native to temperate Eurasia. It has flat or slightly grooved leaves and brown seed capsules, and often grows in limestone-rich wetlands or disturbed places such as ditches, roadsides and canal banks.

Perennial flowering rush native to Europe, Asia and Africa. It forms tufts of stiff, blue-grey, wiry, ridged stems with shiny reddish-black basal sheaths, and bears loose clusters of tiny reddish-brown flowers from late spring to midsummer.
A coastal rush distributed across Europe, western Asia and the Maghreb; its native origin is not stated. Ancient Egyptians reportedly cut and chewed its fibres into chisel-shaped writing brushes.

A rush native from the Mediterranean region across temperate Europe, though not far into Scandinavia, it has been introduced to New Zealand and North America. It is particularly common on disturbed ridges in a human-created Western European fen-meadow habitat.

An evergreen succulent native to Madagascar, flaming Katy grows naturally in humus soil on the relatively cool Tsarantanana plateaus. It has glossy, scallop-edged leaves and produces red, pink, orange, gold or white flowers from late autumn into early winter; parts are poisonous if swallowed.
stories.edibilityNote: Unspecified parts are poisonous if ingested.

stories.summary: A succulent native to southwestern Madagascar, the alligator plant produces new plantlets along its leaf margins. Its fleshy leaves are green above and purple-blotched underneath, and all parts contain a very toxic steroid.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts contain daigremontianin, described as a very toxic steroid.

stories.summary: A succulent native to Madagascar, mother of millions produces numerous plantlets along the tips of its narrow, spotted leaves. It can become invasive and contains cardiac glycosides associated with fatal poisoning in grazing animals.

A frost-tender perennial succulent native to Madagascar. It has fleshy blue-green leaves with scalloped edges that may turn pink or red in strong sunlight or drought. Its lax stems often root where they touch the ground, producing new plants.

Succulent perennial native to parts of central and East Africa. Its fleshy leaves have irregular purple or brown blotches, creating a marbled appearance, while upright clusters of white, four-petalled, star-shaped flowers appear from late winter to spring.
stories.edibilityNote: It may be toxic if ingested, but species-specific data are limited and cited adverse effects concern livestock and pets.

stories.summary: Succulent native to Madagascar and naturalized across many tropical and subtropical regions. Miniature plantlets develop along its fleshy leaf margins, while its hanging flowers are red-orange.
stories.edibilityNote: Contains cardiac glycosides that can cause cardiac poisoning, particularly in grazing animals.

stories.summary: A deciduous tree whose two subspecies are endemic respectively to Fiji and Taiwan. It flowers in autumn with butter-yellow, red-based petals, followed by inflated capsules that change from red or green to brown before splitting open.

An annual herb native to northeastern Mexico and the southeastern and south-central United States, it generally produces one flower head per stalk. Each head has 12–35 yellow ray flowers and no central disc flowers.
A vigorous annual climber native to Africa and India, with large, softly hairy leaves and tendrils that help it climb. Its fruits are used to make bowls and other gourd vessels.

A fast-growing trailing flowering plant endemic to South Africa’s Western Cape, red brightfig has small fleshy leaves and glossy bright-red flowers that open only on sunny days. It blooms in spring, and only five small subpopulations are reported to remain.
A perennial woody shrub in the verbena family.

Perennial tropical shrub with no native origin identified in the source; it is common in Central and South America, the Caribbean and Hawaii, and also occurs in Africa and Madagascar. It usually bears three leaves at each node, with orange glands beneath, dense cylindrical flower spikes and juicy lilac-to-purple ripe fruit.

A perennial legume native to Europe and parts of Asia, growing in broad-leaved woods, clearings and woodland margins. Its leaves have paired leaflets but no tendrils, its red flowers turn bluer with age, and the foliage blackens as it withers.
stories.edibilityNote: The source warns that its seeds are toxic and should not be confused with edible black peas of Pisum sativum.

stories.summary: A cultivated legume with no undisputed native origin supplied, grass pea is grown for food and livestock feed in Asia and East Africa. It yields reliably in drought- and famine-prone areas. Its seeds contain a neurotoxin: immature seeds may be eaten like peas, but mature seeds need soaking and thorough cooking, and prolonged heavy reliance can cause lathyrism.
stories.edibilityNote: Immature seeds are eaten like peas; mature seeds require soaking and thorough cooking. Leaves and stems are cooked in parts of Odisha.

stories.summary: A perennial hawkbit native to Europe and introduced across North America. In a recent British study, it produced the most nectar among examined non-weed perennials, nearly twice that of the leading non-weed annual.
An annual herb with no supplied native origin, tall pepperwort is self-supporting, with simple, broad leaves. It can grow to 51 cm tall.

stories.summary: A flowering plant in the mustard family native to temperate Asia and northern and eastern Europe. It has naturalized in southwestern Europe and North America.
Annual herb native to Egypt and western Asia. It grows quickly and has a mildly spicy, aromatic taste; mainly the leaves of young shoots are eaten in salads, soups, sautés and purées.
stories.edibilityNote: Mainly young-shoot leaves are used in salads, soups, sautés and purées.

stories.summary: Moss with a cosmopolitan distribution, reported absent only from Australia and the Pacific Islands. Its pointed oval leaves grow in two rows, and it can tolerate extremely acidic water and grow under artificial light where natural light is absent.

Moss native to Eurasia and North America, many-fruited leskea usually grows on tree trunks and branches near water, though it also occurs in drier areas. It has creeping stems with spreading branches and curved brown to yellowish spore capsules on red to brownish-orange stalks.

A moss native to and prolific in the eastern and midwestern United States, it also has a wide distribution across both hemispheres. It occurs less commonly in Ontario and is common through Europe into Asia.
Evergreen shrub native to the southeastern United States. It has glossy, laurel-like leaves and hanging clusters of urn-shaped flowers in spring.

A sand-loving grass native to the coasts of northern and western Europe, lyme grass has an extensive root network historically used to stabilize coastal sand. Its seeds were formerly eaten, including as a wild grain in Iceland from at least the 12th century.
stories.edibilityNote: The seeds were historically eaten; Icelanders harvested the grass as a wild grain from at least the 12th century.

stories.summary: A cool-season perennial grass native to Europe, western Asia and North Africa. Its emerging leaves are rolled rather than folded, a key identification feature, and it is widely cultivated for forage and turf. Some plants carry a seed-transmitted fungus whose alkaloids can harm grazing livestock.

An annual grass native to southern Europe, northern Africa, the Middle East and the Indian subcontinent. It grows in open tufts and is cultivated as forage, especially in Australia, where it is also a serious crop weed; infected flower spikes can become dangerously toxic to livestock.
stories.edibilityNote: Ergot-infected plants can cause ergotism in humans, but no human food use is documented.

stories.summary: Annual grass with a cosmopolitan distribution. It closely resembles wheat until the ear appears, but has more slender spikes and ripens black rather than brown. When infected by an endophytic fungus, eating it causes drunken nausea and can be fatal.
stories.edibilityNote: Eating fungus-infected darnel causes drunken nausea and may be fatal.

stories.summary: A shrub native to China, winter honeysuckle forms a tangled mass of slender, spreading branches. Its paired creamy-white flowers have a strong lemony fragrance, followed by red berries.

A liverwort of unstated native origin, it has pale-green translucent leaves that are two-lobed low on the stem but become notched or smooth higher up. It has a strong scent and grows mainly at tree bases, but also on fallen wood, soil, leaf litter and roots.
A climbing or sprawling perennial native to Mexico's Sierra Madre Oriental mountains. It climbs with twisting leaf stalks and bears pink-and-white tubular flowers in the wild.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira, small-flower trefoil is introduced in the Azores. It grows in annual pastures, meadows and fallow ground on temporarily wet soils.

A herbaceous perennial growing throughout Europe in damp, open places. It has golden-yellow flower clusters on upright stems; the always-hollow stem and the turned-back sepals forming a green star on each bud distinguish it from related species.

A flowering rush whose native origin is unsettled. Its grasslike leaves have long white hairs, and its terminal flower spikes develop into round capsules from late spring; unlike most rushes, it favors upland woodland habitats.

A deciduous woody shrub whose native origin is not stated in the supplied information. It has highly branched, often curved or drooping stems with thorns and produces bright orange-red berries. The fruits may be infused with hot water to make goji tea.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruits may be infused with hot water to make goji tea.

stories.summary: A fern native to eastern Asia, from Pakistan and India to Japan, southeastern Asia and New Guinea. Its extremely long, vine-like leaves climb other vegetation, while fertile leaflets bear spores along their fringed edges.

A biennial flowering plant native to coastal eastern Asia and islands of the Indian and Pacific oceans. It grows along beaches and in maritime rock crevices, with fleshy spoon-shaped leaves and white flower clusters in late spring and early summer.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Lythrum thymifolia has narrow, lance-shaped leaves, mostly alternating but opposite at the base. Its solitary, four-petalled flowers grow from the leaf joints and have two stamens.

sources.title: Lythrum thymifolia L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A deciduous tree native to the southeastern United States, bigleaf magnolia has the largest simple leaves and single flowers of any native North American woody plant. Its heavy foliage often bends the branches, while mature orange-coated seeds hang from cone-like fruits on silky threads.

An annual garden plant native to Greece and Albania, and possibly naturalized elsewhere in Mediterranean Europe. It forms masses of fragrant, four-petalled flowers in pink, purple and white, with cultivated plants varying especially in height and flower colour.

An apple tree native to Russia, Mongolia, China, Korea, Bhutan, India and Nepal, it bears fragrant white spring flowers. Its small red-to-yellow fruits grow in dense clusters and are eaten fresh or dried.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruits are edible and eaten fresh or dried.

stories.summary: A crabapple tree native to the United States. Its common variety is concentrated in the upper Mississippi Valley prairies, while the Texas variety is confined to a small part of central Texas. It bears white or pink summer flowers and small, apple-like autumn fruit.
An annual or perennial herb or shrub native to North and South America, three-lobe false mallow has been introduced to Australia, Africa, and southern and eastern Asia.
A perennial shrub of unknown native origin, though Mexico has been suggested. It has hanging red tubular flowers with protruding stamens, pointed oval leaves and hairy stems.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant is described as edible, but no part or preparation is specified.

stories.summary: A succulent cactus native to Texas, northeastern Mexico, Cuba and Hispaniola. Its round or slightly elongated stems usually form dense clusters, and their appearance varies considerably among subspecies. Flowers commonly appear alongside edible fruit.
stories.edibilityNote: The cylindrical fruit is edible, with juice confined to its outer walls.

stories.summary: A fast-growing shrub or small tree native to southern Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay and Argentina. It has striking hand-shaped leaves and pale green, bell-shaped flowers in summer.
A liverwort with no explicitly documented native origin, Marchantia paleacea is found in North America, Europe and eastern Asia. It is used as a model organism to study plant–fungus partnerships.

A moss found across circumboreal regions, with separate tropical mountain populations in Africa, Mexico and Colombia. It forms green, reddish-brown or blackish mats on wet, lime-free rocks in and beside streams, and its rounded leaves are distinctly notched.
A moss with no stated native origin, it occurs in Europe and North America. It forms dense black-green mats of branched stems, with spreading, boat-shaped leaves divided into two triangular lobes.
An annual herb native across the Mediterranean Basin, from Macaronesia to the Caucasus. It usually grows along the ground, sometimes with ascending stems, and is used as livestock forage.

An annual herb with no supplied native origin, star-fruited medick is self-supporting and has compound, broad leaves. It grows on dry, stony, usually alkaline soils in places such as pastures, field edges, banks and walls.

A small tree endemic to eastern Australia, it has white or creamy-white papery bark and a dense canopy. Its perfumed, creamy-white flowers briefly cover the tree between October and February, followed by woody capsules scattered along the stems.
A plant whose native origin is not supplied, tall melilot is a preferred food plant of three short-tongued bumblebee species found in the UK.

An annual flowering herb native to mainland Portugal and Madeira, elegant melilot grows upright and branched, becoming nearly hairless. It bears loose clusters of many fragrant flowers, followed by yellowish fruits with sharply marked crosswise folds and a prominent seam.

sources.title: Melilotus elegans Salzm.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Annual legume with no explicitly stated native origin, distributed in southern Europe. It has grooved stem leaves, tiny flowers from June to August, and pods marked with curved veins.

A perennial grass native to parts of Africa, with fragrant foliage and long, slender stems that layer into thick mats. It can lean on other plants for support and has become invasive in places including Hawaii and parts of South America.

A liverwort, forked veilwort grows on many kinds of tree and shrub bark and occasionally on rocks. It forms slim, translucent yellow-green mats whose branches and central ribs characteristically fork at their tips; spore-bearing structures are rare.
A small annual grass native to western and southwestern Europe. It grows in open vegetation on moist sand, forming tufts of hair-thin stems with two or three leaves clustered at or near the base.

A perennial grass native to much of East and Southeast Asia. It forms dense clumps from underground stems, with purplish flowers held above the foliage, and is widely grown as an ornamental in temperate regions.

A moss native to Europe and eastern North America. It has upright stems, toothed leaves and pointed-lid capsules, and commonly grows in damp, acidic woodland on soil, logs, rocks, tree bases and stream banks.
A perennial grass native to Europe, western Asia and northern Africa. It forms dense tussocks of coarse, pointed leaves, with long, narrow purple flower spikes that are a key identifying feature.

A tree-like perennial shrub native to Central America and southern Mexico. Its young leaves are deeply divided but become palmately lobed, while abundant white-and-yellow daisy-like flowers appear from late autumn to winter. It can form dense invasive stands where introduced.

A flowering plant broadly distributed across the western Mediterranean, Moricandia arvensis ranges from the Canary Islands and northern Africa to southern Europe, but was introduced to France, Corsica and Sardinia. Its photosynthesis uses an intermediate carbon-fixation system.

Fast-growing, drought-resistant tree native to northern India. It has feathery foliage and hanging three-sided pods, and its young pods and leaves are widely cultivated as vegetables, although Australia prohibits their retail food use because safety evidence was insufficient.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves, immature pods, seeds, flowers, roots and seed oil are used as food; excess root compounds may harm, and Australia prohibits retail food use.

stories.summary: A large climbing vine native to tropical Central and South America and the West Indies, it climbs into the forest canopy. Its ridged pods bear orange-brown stinging hairs that cause intense itching, while its seeds have been used as famine food.
stories.edibilityNote: The seeds have been used as famine food.

stories.summary: Perennial warm-season grass native to eastern North America. It forms clumps topped by feathery purple-pink flowers with a cloudlike appearance, while its green leaves turn copper in autumn.
A fast-growing tree originating in the Americas, especially Mexico and Peru. It bears small, round, very sweet edible fruits, while its weak wood breaks easily in strong winds and storms.
stories.edibilityNote: The small, very sweet fruit is edible and nutritious.

stories.summary: A perennial bulb native to the Mediterranean region and naturalized elsewhere. A tassel of bright blue to violet sterile flowers rises above brownish-green fertile flowers. In Italy and Greece, its bulbs are eaten as a delicacy, traditionally boiled repeatedly or served pickled in olive oil.
stories.edibilityNote: Bulbs are a delicacy in Italy and Greece; historically seasoned, and today often boiled repeatedly, pickled and kept in olive oil.

stories.summary: A highly variable tree or shrub native to the Hawaiian Islands and ʻEua in Tonga, naio ranges from a dwarf shrub at the tree line to a large tree. Its fragrant white or pink flowers occur year-round, followed by juicy, bitter, waxy-white fruit that often dries while still attached.

A perennial herb endemic to the western Azores, it was reported only from Flores and Corvo, with the last wild populations on Flores described as recently extinct. Its deep blue-purple flowers have yellow centres and grow on spirally curved stems. It inhabits waterfalls, wet rocks and high wet meadows.

Aquatic plant native to Europe and Asia, inhabiting ponds, streams and other waters. Its whorled leaves occur both underwater and above the surface, with the exposed leaves smaller than the submerged ones. The flowers emerge above the water and are reported to bloom in August.

An annual submerged aquatic herb native to Europe, Asia and North Africa, it grows in dense clusters in calm water. Its highly branched stems break easily, while its strap-shaped leaves have clearly visible serrations.

A leafy liverwort with no native origin specified, distributed across Europe, Macaronesia, Japan and North America. It forms dense green-to-brown carpets, sometimes reddish in sunny places, and produces dark-brown oval spore capsules that mature in spring.
A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal and the Azores. It is the predominant herbaceous cover in the Serra da Estrela, where it is commonly called servum.

A grass native to Argentina, Chilean needle grass has strong colonising potential and is considered a serious threat to native species and habitats. Its release, possession, transport and trade are prohibited in the Canary Islands.

A grass native to the southwestern United States, northern Mexico and Argentina, Mexican feathergrass is cultivated ornamentally but readily escapes. In Australia it is considered a major potential threat to native grasslands, eucalypt woodlands and agricultural production.

A herbaceous perennial native to the Caucasus, Turkey and northern Iran, it has aromatic leaves and violet or lilac-blue summer flowers. Like other catmints, it can produce a euphoric effect in some domestic cats.

A tropical fern native to Florida, Mexico, the West Indies, Central and South America, Africa and Southeast Asia, this is the largest sword fern and can develop exceptionally long fronds. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, its young leaves are cooked and eaten as a condiment or leafy vegetable.
stories.edibilityNote: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, young leaves are cooked and eaten as a condiment or leafy vegetable.

stories.summary: An ornamental plant with a broad, possibly cultivation-influenced distribution around the Pacific, it is notable for its bright orange berries. Of 21 children reported to have ingested the plant, five developed mild poisoning symptoms including tiredness, stomach pain and vomiting.
stories.edibilityNote: Of 21 children reported to have ingested the plant, five developed mild poisoning symptoms including tiredness, stomach pain and vomiting.

stories.summary: An ornamental tobacco plant whose commonly grown varieties open their flowers in the late afternoon or evening and release a floral scent through the night. Flower colours include white, pink, yellow and lime green.

A rainforest plant native to South America, Aztec tobacco is exceptionally potent, with leaves containing up to nine times more nicotine than common tobacco. Its nicotine-rich leaves are used to produce pesticides and in varied cultural preparations.
stories.edibilityNote: In Peru it is drunk as juice for entheogenic purposes; no human food use is documented.

stories.summary: A flowering plant with no supplied native origin, red monk's-wort occurs around the western Mediterranean, including North Africa, the Iberian Peninsula and Sicily. It favors arable meadows, pasture, fields and roadsides, usually on alkaline soil but sometimes acidic soil, with some preference for disturbed, nitrogen-rich ground.

A small liverwort found on rotting forest logs across northern temperate and subarctic regions. Its leaves grow in two rows and each forms a tiny water-holding pocket; plants often turn reddish-purple in autumn and winter.

An aquatic plant native to Louisiana, Florida, Texas, Mexico and the Bahamas. Its leaves are green above and purple beneath, while its fragrant flowers function as female on their first day and male during the following two days.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant is used for food, but the source does not specify parts, preparation or historical context.

stories.summary: A small shrub indigenous to South Africa, it has fragrant yellow spring flowers followed by bright-red sepals and fruitlets that turn black when ripe. Cultivated as an ornamental, it is invasive in Australia and New Zealand.

A basil species native to Africa, including Madagascar, and southern Asia, African basil has leaves used in Nigeria to prepare pepper soup, rice, beans, plantains and other dishes. Its seeds seem to need strong sunlight to germinate, although they have germinated during an average UK summer.
stories.edibilityNote: In Nigeria, the leaves are used in pepper soup, rice, beans, plantains and other dishes.

stories.summary: Wildflower native to Europe and Asia. It bears pinkish-red flowers from June to September and is partly parasitic on grass roots, commonly growing in low-fertility soils.
A flowering plant native from central and southern Mexico through Honduras to Panama. It grows mainly in humid tropical environments.

A liverwort found in temperate, ocean-influenced parts of Europe and North America, as well as northern Mexico. It grows horizontally in dense mats, ranging from pale yellow-green to reddish-brown, particularly in bogs and other moist settings.

An aquatic flowering herb native from Ireland to central Siberia and from southern Scandinavia to the Mediterranean, it favours reedbeds and pools with fluctuating water levels. Its finely divided lower leaves are threadlike underwater but have flat, oval segments when emerging above water.
stories.edibilityNote: Not widely used because of poisoning danger; its fruits are reputed to cause vertigo, drunkenness and narcotic symptoms.

stories.summary: Flowering plant native to Mexico and the southeastern United States. Beach evening-primrose grows on coastal dunes and other disturbed sandy areas and has been introduced to many places worldwide.

Perennial herb widespread across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, throughout North America and Eurasia. Its pointed leaves are smooth above and woolly beneath, while its pale brown flower heads have green-centred bracts with papery brown edges.
A cactus that may have been endemic to Mexico but has been widely introduced. Unlike most Opuntia species, it is pollinated by hummingbirds.

A succulent, thorny shrub native to Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, it develops a broad, almost tree-like crown. It has shiny green flattened shoots, dark yellow flowers and spineless, pear-shaped red fruit.

A tree-like cactus native to San Luis Potosí and Hidalgo in Mexico and to Nicaragua. Its flattened green stem segments are finely velvety and bear irritating short bristles, while its fleshy, seed-filled ripe fruits are edible.
stories.edibilityNote: The fleshy ripe fruits are edible but full of seeds and protected by irritating bristles.

stories.summary: A flowering plant whose young flower shoots are eaten as a vegetable, similarly to asparagus. It was once abundant near Bath in England.
stories.edibilityNote: Young flower shoots are eaten as an asparagus-like vegetable.

stories.summary: A moss widespread across the Northern Hemisphere, with separate occurrences in southern South America. Often growing on tree bark and stone near settlements, it is distinguished by transparent, glass-like leaf tips and capsules almost buried among the leaves.

A perennial grass of obscure native origin, with sources proposing widely different regions. Its thick, pointed, branching underground stems spread repeatedly and can form dense colonies or floating mats. Introduced across many tropical and subtropical areas, it is often a serious invasive weed.

A deciduous woody vine native to Korea, Japan and northern and eastern China. It climbs using branched tendrils tipped with sticky disks, and its usually three-lobed leaves turn orange-yellow to intense scarlet in autumn.
stories.edibilityNote: Traditionally used as a culinary sweetener in Japan, although its dark blue fruit is inedible.

stories.summary: A tropical to subtropical perennial grass native to Mexico and South America, bahiagrass is remembered for its prominent V-shaped flower head. Its creeping stems root along the ground and form dense turf.

Evergreen climbing shrub native to Central and northwestern South America, sweet granadilla climbs surrounding vegetation using coiling tendrils. Its aromatic, sweet-musky flowers last only one day. Ripe yellowish-orange fruits contain hard black seeds surrounded by translucent, sweet, edible pulp.
stories.edibilityNote: The translucent pulp surrounding the hard black seeds is the edible part of the ripe fruit and tastes sweet.

stories.summary: A fast-growing flowering vine native to Mexico, Guatemala and parts of South America. Its white-and-purple flowers are followed by blue or purple fruit containing edible orange pulp, though the pulp is not especially flavourful and the plant is not cultivated for fruit.
stories.edibilityNote: The orange fruit pulp is edible but not particularly flavourful; the vine is not cultivated for its fruit.

stories.summary: A vining passionflower with three-lobed leaves and ornate flowers followed by yellow-green fruits. It is grown as an ornamental and can be a minor pest in some areas.

A densely branching shrub native to South Africa, oak-leaved geranium has sticky, aromatic leaves divided into stiff, coarsely toothed, oak-like lobes. Its flowers are pink with darker pink markings, and its stems become woody with age.

A thallose liverwort occurring in North America, Europe, North Africa and parts of Asia, common pellia forms patches in damp, sheltered places. Its irregularly branched green body may have a red or purple tinge, and it produces spherical greenish-black capsules on pale green stalks.

A bristly perennial native to southwestern Europe, particularly northwest Iberia and France. It can retain green leaves through winter, and its pink buds open into vivid blue flowers with white centres. Its leaves and stems can irritate skin.
stories.edibilityNote: Blue flowers garnish salads or drinks; roots remain liver-toxic after cooking, and leaves are toxic in large quantities.

stories.summary: An evergreen flowering perennial native to tropical America. It has cupped, leathery leaves and shiny, winding spikes of white flowers, while cultivated plants may have variegated foliage. It is often confused with Peperomia magnoliifolia, although living plants differ in their waxy rather than fleshy leaves.

A scrambling cactus shrub native to South America, it has spiny, non-succulent stems and large leaves. Its leaves and fruits are edible, and the leaves are a popular vegetable in parts of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves and fruits are edible; the leaves are traditionally eaten as a vegetable in parts of Minas Gerais, Brazil.

stories.summary: A cactus native to eastern and southern Brazil, the rose cactus grows as a shrub or small tree. Unlike most cacti, it keeps its leaves and bears showy, rose-like flowers ranging from pale pink to purplish pink.
stories.edibilityNote: The leaves can be eaten as a salad or used in stews.

stories.summary: A small green liverwort found from the Mediterranean region east to Turkey and along Atlantic Europe to north-western Scotland. Its flat body has a central rib, two wings and upright leaf-like ridges, and it grows chiefly in open, damp dune hollows.

Shrub native to North America, Central America, the Antilles and tropical South America. Its crushed leaves smell of garlic, and flowering occurs year-round toward the south but from spring through autumn toward the north.

An evergreen flowering vine native to tropical America, it has rough leaves and showy violet flower clusters. Depending on the climate, it may bloom twice a year, and its nectar-rich flowers attract butterflies.

A wetland biennial with hollow, often purplish stems and finely divided leaves, found beside rivers, estuaries and ditches. Its young parts contain a thin milky latex, and it is an important food plant for Old World swallowtail caterpillars.
stories.edibilityNote: Roots have been used as a ginger substitute in southeastern Europe and Russia.

stories.summary: A hornwort whose native origin is not stated, found worldwide in damp, shaded places. It forms flat, dark green rosettes on bare soil or rock and produces upright horn-like spore capsules. In temporary habitats it often grows annually, while tuber-like structures help it survive dry periods.
A perennial shrub native to the eastern United States, hoary mock orange can grow tall and bears white flowers.

Annual flowering grass native to Europe, Morocco and the Levant. It typically grows in coastal dunes and other sandy areas; in mainland Portugal, it occurs at only a few unstable dune sites along the northern coast and was assessed as Endangered in 2020.

stories.summary: A perennial flowering plant native to the eastern United States, wild sweetwilliam forms upright clumps. It produces fragrant clusters of deep pink summer flowers on stiff, red-spotted stems.

A clumping palm native to tropical Africa, the Arabian Peninsula and Madagascar, with multiple stems and long, recurved green leaves armed with sharp basal spines. Its ripe orange fruit and palm heart are edible; in KwaZulu-Natal and Botswana’s Okavango Delta, sap tapped shortly before flowering is made into palm wine.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe fruit and palm heart are eaten; sap tapped before flowering makes palm wine in KwaZulu-Natal and Botswana’s Okavango Delta.

stories.summary: Shrub or tree native to parts of Asia, from central and southern China to northern Vietnam, Taiwan, northern Sumatra and Mount Kinabalu on Borneo. It has closely clustered white flowers followed by small fruits and is grown as an ornamental plant.

An evergreen flowering shrub or tree found in mixed forests from China and Taiwan to Japan, the Philippines, Indonesia and India; its three recognized varieties are native to Taiwan. White spring flowers appear with red leaves and have a strong semen-like odor, while red fruits ripen in autumn and persist through winter.
stories.edibilityNote: The leaves are toxic.

stories.summary: A perennial flowering grass native to West Africa, tall reed is a fast-growing aquatic plant often found in swamps, along riverbanks and in standing water. Its young shoots can be cooked and eaten like bamboo or asparagus.
stories.edibilityNote: Young shoots can be cooked and eaten like bamboo or asparagus.

stories.summary: A herbaceous plant native to the Mascarene Islands and possibly also eastern Africa, other western Indian Ocean islands and the Arabian Peninsula. Its main stem bears scales rather than leaves, while secondary stems carry its leaves and tiny male and female flowers.

A running bamboo native to Zhejiang Province in China, yellow groove bamboo typically has dark green stems marked by a yellow groove, with occasional zigzag bends near the base. Its shoots are edible and lack an acrid taste even when raw.
stories.edibilityNote: The shoots are eaten and are described as free of acrid flavour even when raw.

stories.summary: A bamboo native to Hunan Province, China, it forms clumps of slender, arching canes that turn black after two or three seasons. Its plants flower together at long intervals and die after flowering.
stories.edibilityNote: It is used as food in its native Chinese range and worldwide; the source does not specify the part or preparation.

stories.summary: Flowering plant native to Europe and Asia. Its narrow leaves resemble an ox’s tongue, while its summer flowers are small, yellow and dandelion-like; it is invasive in Africa, Australia and North America.
A perennial evergreen herb native to the Caribbean, including Florida, and northern South America. Its creeping growth suits indoor hanging pots.

A herbaceous perennial whose native origin is not specified in the supplied information. It is widespread in central Europe and the Caucasus and naturalized in North America, with hollow, deeply grooved stems and white to pink flowers in rounded clusters.

A plant in the carrot family native to the British Isles, temperate Europe and Western Asia, burnet-saxifrage has leaves resembling those of burnet. It forms much of the turf on some southern English chalk downs and was formerly grown on lime-rich soils as livestock fodder.

A flowering tree native to the Pacific Coast and adjacent highlands of Mexico, Central America and northern South America, Madras thorn has a spiny trunk and fragrant greenish-white flowers. Its ripe pods turn pink and split open to reveal pink or white pulp, which is eaten raw in several countries and used in drinks.
stories.edibilityNote: Sweet-and-sour pod pulp is eaten raw, served with meat dishes, or mixed with sugar and water for drinks.

stories.summary: A rhizomatous plant native to Mexico and tropical America that grows in soil or on rocks. It occurs mainly in subtropical regions and has been widely introduced across Asia, Africa and Pacific islands.

A moss distributed almost worldwide, including from lowlands to the high Alps in Central Europe. It forms bright green, slightly glossy, flattened mats, often on tree bases or rotting wood, and produces reddish-yellow capsules whose spores mature in spring.
A small tree native to the West Indies and parts of Mexico and Central America, with glossy, blunt-tipped leaves. Its fragrant white flowers have yellow centres and grow in clusters.
An evergreen vining shrub native to South Africa. It has fragrant, bell-shaped pink flowers with darker markings and long capsules that release numerous winged seeds.
A moss with no stated native origin, urn hair moss is found across Europe, North America and parts of Asia. Its robust, upright growth may look bluish-green when moist, and its stems are wine red.

A leafy moss recorded across Europe, Asia, Africa, the Americas, Australia, New Zealand and Antarctica, it forms loose to moderately dense patches. Young growth is whitish to bluish-green, becoming reddish or brownish with age, while its capsules lean or hang from curved yellow-red stalks.

A perennial herb native to Europe, including European Russia, and Turkey. It has branching stems woody at the base and usually bears blue or violet flowers from May through July, with purple forms occurring rarely.

An evergreen shrub native to the paleotropics and neotropics, it has upright branches and variable, coarsely toothed leaves often edged in white or pale yellow. Small green flower clusters may be followed by black berries.

A tropical shrub or small tree native to eastern Malesia and the southwest Pacific islands, shield aralia has strong, bowl-shaped leaves historically used in Indonesia as dishes. Its shredded leaves can be mixed with meat or fish for their aroma.
stories.edibilityNote: Shredded leaves are used in Indonesian cuisine with meat or fish; historically, whole leaves served as bowls rather than food.

stories.summary: A widely distributed moss found across Europe, Asia, Africa, the Americas, Australia, New Zealand and Antarctica. It forms loose muddy-green, bluish-green or brownish growth, and its serrated leaves fit together when dry but bend back when wet.

A succulent annual flowering plant native to southern Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay. It has fleshy leaves and flowers in red, orange, pink, white or yellow. Unlike some related purslanes, it is described as inedible because of its bitter taste.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant is described as inedible because of its bitter taste.

stories.summary: Annual or short-lived perennial succulent native to the New World. Its unusually small, broad foliage accompanies flowers ranging from yellow and pink to orange.
stories.edibilityNote: The stems, leaves, flowers and roots are all described as edible.

stories.summary: A perennial aquatic plant of unspecified native origin, perfoliate pondweed is widely distributed across standing and flowing fresh waters on every continent except South America and Antarctica. Its translucent submerged leaves have no stalk and clasp the stem; it produces no floating leaves.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Potamogeton perfoliatus
