A medium-sized red marine alga whose native origin is not specified; it occurs from Norway and the Faroes to Senegal, the Mediterranean and the Canary Islands. Its flattened branches alternate between long and short forms, with curved side branches creating a comb-like pattern.

A small, uncommon seaweed found around Great Britain and Ireland, the Azores, and the Atlantic coast from Massachusetts to Virginia, Gymnogongrus griffithsiae grows in lower-shore rock pools and just below the shore. It is dark purplish brown, with erect, stiff fronds that fork in one plane and have slightly flattened tips.

Small red marine alga of unstated native origin, recorded around the British Isles and from Norway and the Mediterranean to the Indian and Pacific oceans. It grows in shaded upper-shore sites as dark brown, creeping, moss-like branches visibly pinched at intervals.
A multicellular red marine alga with no stated native origin, found across Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia, as well as islands in the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans.

A red alga with no specific native origin stated, Amphiroa beauvoisii is widely distributed, mainly in tropical and subtropical waters. It attaches to intertidal rocks by a calcified base and produces flat, branching, fan-like growth whose form varies with location.
Perennial herb native to the mountains of Southern Europe, with a fuzzy woody stem and paired leaves. Its generally violet flowers appear between May and August depending on altitude.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant can be brewed and served as tea.

stories.summary: A wild banana plant originally from Assam and the eastern Himalayas. It bears fuzzy pink fruits on upright flower stalks, and the ripe fruits peel themselves back. Their soft, sweet flesh is edible, but the tough seeds can chip a tooth.
stories.edibilityNote: The soft, sweet fruit flesh can be eaten, but the tough seeds can chip a tooth.

stories.summary: A bulbous perennial native to South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province, silver squill is often cultivated and grows well with minimal care.
Flowering plant endemic to Brazil. Its centre turns red shortly before flowering, creating its characteristic blushing appearance.
Evergreen flowering climber native to Colombia, with red stems and large heart-shaped leaves. Its deep-red, fragrant flower structures appear in summer and autumn.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are toxic because they contain calcium oxalate and should be kept away from young children.

stories.summary: Wetland plant native to Japan, Korea and eastern Asia. Its long, narrow, slightly curved leaves grow in very moist soil or partly or fully submerged, while its rhizomes can spread aggressively into dense groundcover.

A hornwort whose native origin is not stated. It grows in moist soil and waterways, forming a nearly flat, dark green, slightly glossy body. When numerous, its slender green spore capsules resemble tufts of grass.

A seaweed with no native origin specified, Ulva clathrata occurs across parts of Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, as well as several oceans, gulfs and seas. It is light green and forms thin, cylindrical threads.
A green seaweed found worldwide, Flexuous Gutweed is a large, tubular and highly variable alga. Its branches have cells arranged lengthwise and sometimes crosswise.

A tree-like cactus from southern South America, probably including Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina. Its branching, segmented stems are usually spineless, while large white flowers open on summer nights and are followed by red-to-yellow fruits with white pulp.
stories.edibilityNote: In Rio Grande do Sul, the fruits are appreciated by local people.

stories.summary: Small flowering tree native to the Caribbean, including Jamaica, Hispaniola, Puerto Rico, and the Leeward and Windward Islands. Its showy flowers make it a popular ornamental.

Fast-growing perennial vine endemic to Rio de Janeiro state in Brazil. Its long woody stems twine around supports, while pink-red funnel-shaped flowers appear over a long period from spring into autumn.

Perennial plant native to several countries in southern South America. Purple cultivars have three-part leaves that fold down at night, when disturbed or in harsh sunlight; white or pale pink flowers also close at night.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves and flowers are edible in moderation, but large quantities may cause toxicity from soluble calcium oxalates.

stories.summary: A tender trailing perennial native to southern Africa, it has aromatic, glossy, rounded leaves that sometimes show deep purple centres and undersides. White, pale violet or pale pink flowers may appear sporadically year-round, especially in spring and late autumn.
Fruit tree native to the Amazon rainforest in Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Ecuador. It bears pale green fruits that turn bright yellow when ripe, with juicy, aromatic and strongly acidic pulp.
stories.edibilityNote: The acidic fruit is eaten fresh, preferably with sugar, or processed into juices, nectars, marmalades, ice creams and other foods.

stories.summary: Creeping evergreen flowering perennial native to rainforests of Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador and northern Brazil. Its dark green leaves are marked by strongly contrasting veins, from white to deep pink or red, while its stems are lightly fuzzy and its flowers small and pale.

A perennial flowering plant native to eastern Brazil's Atlantic Forest, northeastern Argentina and Paraguay. It is cultivated as a decorative potted or landscape feature plant in warm temperate and subtropical climates.
Herbaceous plant native to Venezuela, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru. It has been introduced to places including Hawaii and the Galápagos Islands.

A rhizomatous flowering plant native to the eastern Himalayas from southern Bhutan to northern Myanmar. It is prized for dark leaves marked with prominent silvery-grey bands and is usually grown for foliage rather than flowers.

Evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand. Its leaves usually have seven sharply toothed leaflets, with young leaves shiny and purplish underneath. Māori used its timber to make fire by friction and its fruit juice as a dye.

Soft-wooded shrub native to eastern Australia; in New Zealand it is reported as indigenous, though some authorities consider it introduced. It has blue-purple flowers and orange-red to scarlet fruit. Ripe berries were traditional Māori food and were stewed or made into pies and jam by early European settlers; using leaves in hāngī is now discouraged because they contain poisonous alkaloids.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe berries were traditional Māori food and early settlers stewed them or made pies and jam; leaf use in hāngī is now discouraged.

stories.summary: A climbing cactus native to Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela, yellow dragonfruit has exceptionally large night-blooming flowers. Its spiny yellow fruit has edible white flesh with a pleasant, mildly sweet flavour; hybrids may have differently coloured skin or flesh.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit’s white interior is edible and mildly sweet; hybrid fruit may have pink flesh.

stories.summary: Salt-tolerant flowering plant native to Portugal. It grows in estuary and lagoon salt marshes, with fleshy stems and scale-like leaves that are green in spring and summer but reddish in autumn.

A woody evergreen vine native to southern tropical India, it bears long hanging clusters of strongly curved flowers. The flowers are rich yellow with maroon to brownish-red tips and appear from spring to autumn.

A densely branching flowering subshrub found from Mediterranean Europe and northern and central Africa through western Asia, Cressa cretica also occurs in Southeast Asia and Australia, where its native status is unclear. It has silky-haired leaves and white flowers and grows in salty, seasonally wet places.
A perennial herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa. It grows on rocky ground and slopes, with a woody base, profusely branching stems and broadly arrow-shaped leaves.

A fast-growing tropical tree native to tropical South America. Its edible fruit ripens from green to yellow and has a soft-spined surface that bruises and blackens easily, contributing to a shelf life of under a week. The very soft, sweet pulp is usually eaten fresh, though it is also cooked and made into wine in Brazil.
stories.edibilityNote: The sweet fruit pulp is usually eaten fresh; chefs sometimes cook it, and it has been made into wine in Brazil.

stories.summary: A perennial shrub or subshrub native to South America, lemon verbena has glossy, pointed leaves that release a strong lemon scent when bruised. Its leaves flavour foods and drinks, including fish, poultry, jams and herbal tea, and are also used to flavour liqueurs.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves are used to flavour cooked dishes, marinades, dressings, jams, puddings, yogurt and beverages, and to make herbal tea and flavour liqueurs.

stories.summary: An aromatic, spiny deciduous shrub or small tree native to Japan and Korea; its natural range also includes mainland China. Its scarlet berries burst open in autumn to scatter black seeds. Young leaves and ground or prepared fruits are used as flavorings in Japanese and Korean cooking.
stories.edibilityNote: Mature fruits are ground as spice; immature berries are blanched, salted or simmered, while young leaves, shoots and male flowers are eaten in Japan and Korea.

stories.summary: A stemless evergreen shrub native to south-central and southeastern North America. Its sharply pointed, sword-like leaves often fold under their own weight, and tall summer flower clusters rise above them with creamy white, bell-shaped blooms.

A deciduous tree native to tropical Southeast Asia and northern Australasia, it produces masses of golden summer flowers. Its pods change from red to black as they ripen, and the tree is widely planted as an ornamental.

A creeping wetland perennial native to Western and Central Europe, creeping marshwort is rare throughout its range. Its trailing stems root at their joints and can form mats where flooding, mowing or grazing keeps taller vegetation in check.
stories.edibilityNote: Its leaves taste mild and parsley-like, but the source only speculates about edibility and documents no clear human food use.

stories.summary: A low-growing, hairless perennial flowering plant native to western Europe, found in ditches, streams, and fresh or brackish wetlands. Its hollow stems root where nodes touch the ground, and crushed leaves smell of carrot. Traditionally harvested in several Mediterranean countries, its young leaves and tender shoots are eaten raw, boiled, or as a condiment, though it can be confused with allegedly poisonous lesser water parsnip.
stories.edibilityNote: Young leaves and tender shoots are traditionally eaten in several Mediterranean countries, raw in salads, boiled, or used as a condiment.

stories.summary: A small marine red alga recorded from Great Britain and Ireland south to Portugal and the Mediterranean. Its flattened, fan-shaped fronds grow from a disc-like anchor and divide into blades with rounded tips.

Flowering herbaceous perennial native to southern China, the Himalayas, India and Indochina. It grows along forest edges and in mountain grasslands, producing flowers from red and orange to almost yellow.

A perennial flowering herb native mainly to Missouri and Arkansas, with additional populations in Louisiana and Illinois, Drummond's goldenrod spreads through underground stems. A single plant can bear 200 or more small yellow flower heads in a large, sometimes drooping, branched display.

A small bulb-growing species of garlic native to the Mediterranean region, Allium chamaemoly has an extremely short or absent flower stalk, so its flowers appear at ground level. Its white flowers usually have a purple stripe, while its flat, grass-like leaves often bear long white hairs.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Allium chamaemoly
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A bulb-forming perennial wild onion native to southern Iberia, the Balearic Islands, Sicily and North Africa; it might be introduced in the Azores. Its narrow leaves bear conspicuous long white hairs, and its white flowers have yellow anthers.

A tall herbaceous perennial of unstated native origin, giant fennel has hollow stalks and produces resin from its root or lower stalk. Its young stems and flower clusters were eaten in ancient Rome and remain eaten in Morocco, though culinary use can cause poisoning.
stories.edibilityNote: Young stems and inflorescences were eaten in ancient Rome and remain eaten in Morocco; poisoning can occur, and Sardinia has poisonous and non-poisonous chemotypes.

stories.summary: A Mediterranean-endemic perennial found in dry grassland, rocky places, roadsides and waste ground. Its many rigid, twisting stems form a tangled bush, while a large fleshy root is wrapped near the top in brown fibres left by old leaves.

Clump-forming, fleshy-leaved plant endemic to South Africa's Eastern Cape Province. Its small light-green rosettes usually have slightly bristly leaf margins and transparent streaks or tips; in the wild, the plant is mostly buried in sand with only these tips showing.
A flowering-plant species native to mainland Portugal and introduced in the Azores.

An aromatic perennial of the western Mediterranean and southern Atlantic coast of the Iberian Peninsula. It grows on coastal sand, dunes and rocky shores, bearing solitary daisy-like flower heads with white rays and yellow centres.

sources.title: Anthemis maritima L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A herbaceous perennial native to the Mediterranean. Its nearly leafless upright stalks carry yellow flower heads ringed by thorny bracts, including stiff golden inner bracts, and it flowers from June through August.
A low, trailing succulent endemic to New Zealand. Its fleshy, three-sided leaves and white-to-deep-pink daisy-like flowers distinguish it on cliffs, gravel beaches, salt meadows and estuaries.
stories.edibilityNote: European settlers ate its bland, fleshy capsules and pickled its leaves.

stories.summary: A tree fern native to New Zealand.

A deciduous flowering climber native to mountainous Asia from Afghanistan to Taiwan. In late spring it produces masses of scented white or pink flowers for about four weeks, each with four petals and prominent yellow anthers.

A perennial plant distributed along the southern Atlantic coast of the Iberian Peninsula and through the western Mediterranean to Italy. It grows in sand, dunes and pine scrub, with purple flower heads surrounded by scales bearing hooked reddish-brown spines.

sources.title: Centaurea sphaerocephala L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A culinary herb in the buckwheat family, French sorrel has a tart, slightly lemony taste from oxalic acid and may become bitter later in the season. It is eaten in salads, soups and sauces, especially sauces for fish.
stories.edibilityNote: Used as a culinary herb in salads, soups and sauces, especially with fish; tart from oxalic acid and sometimes bitter later in the season.

stories.summary: A low woody flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and occurring across southwestern Europe and North Africa. It grows in scrub and uncultivated ground, flowering from May to July.

A herb found only on the Iberian Peninsula, mainly at inland sites in Spain and a small neighbouring area of Portugal. Its recognised subspecies and varieties are largely geographically separate, and the plant blooms from April to October in habitats including woodland edges, scrub and roadsides.
An ascending legume recorded in the Iberian Peninsula and northern Morocco. It has hairy stems, purple-and-white flowers and very hairy pods edged with several spines.

A rhizomatous perennial herb native to temperate Europe. It grows in wet places and bears solitary white flowers tinged with yellow and purple. All parts are poisonous, and some historical medicinal use resulted in fatal poisoning.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous; historical medicinal use caused some fatal poisonings, and the plant is no longer used because of the poisoning risk.

stories.summary: A flowering rush native to northwestern Africa, many Mediterranean islands, warmer parts of southern, central and eastern Europe, and western Asia, sand rush favours wet, nutrient-poor rock, sand or clay soils. It often occurs in clay pits, old brickyards and along roads.

A sedge native in Wallonia, sweet galingale is also widespread across Africa, southern Europe, the Indian subcontinent and western Asia. It has creeping underground stems and upright triangular stalks, and grows in shallow water or damp ground such as pond edges. Its thick yellowish underground stems are traditionally harvested to distil sweet-scented oil for perfume.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits wet meadows, marshes and temporarily flooded pasture around lagoons, springs and permanent waterways, particularly on siliceous ground.

A flowering plant in the daisy family, Leucanthemopsis pulverulenta includes a subspecies endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. This subspecies occurs in mainland Portugal and is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

An annual herb occurring across southern Europe, North Africa and parts of Asia. It may grow upright or trail along the ground, with usually yellow flowers and hairy, glandular pods containing several brown seeds.

sources.title: Ononis viscosa L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Annual flowering plant native to the Palearctic, from the western Mediterranean to Central Asia. It grows in sandy, well-drained ground, particularly coastal and desert dunes.
A perennial, thistle-like plant occurring in southern Europe and North Africa. It has spiny leaves that partly dry by flowering time and solitary flower heads filled with yellow flowers.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Within Portugal it is characteristic of major-river floodplains, occurs at only three known locations along the Douro and Tagus, and was assessed as Endangered with an estimated population of about 500 mature plants.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Andryala ragusina
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An annual lupine endemic to the western half of the Iberian Peninsula. Its pinkish-blue flowers form neat rings along a spike, while its leaves have several leaflets radiating from one point. The whole plant feels soft and has a particularly strong smell.

A herbaceous plant endemic to Mediterranean areas of southwestern Europe, Spanish birthwort occurs from the Iberian Peninsula through southern France to Corsica and Sardinia. It inhabits rocky places, fallows and clearings among heaths, scrub or holm oak groves.
A perennial plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it has several smooth or nearly smooth stems and narrow leaves. It grows in open scrub and uncultivated ground, usually on dry, often stony soils.
A flowering plant whose nominate subspecies, Linaria viscosa subsp. viscosa, is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in meadows, pasture, fallow and uncultivated land, often on sandy soils.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It occurs in open grassland, scrub clearings, olive groves, fields, roadsides and embankments. Possible identification features needing confirmation include persistent sepals and two distinct kinds of hairs on the fruits.

A biennial rose-family plant recorded around the Mediterranean and on the Iberian Peninsula. Its club-shaped flower heads place female flowers at the top and bisexual flowers below, while its large, roughly pyramidal or egg-shaped fruit has conspicuous warts.
A flowering grass native to Europe, North Africa and temperate Asia. It is a tufted perennial with spreading underground stems, stiff flat leaves and a narrow flower cluster.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it grows in shady, waterside herb communities beneath riverside woodland, often under alder trees.
An annual thistle found across the Mediterranean region, it occurs mainly in non-alpine, non-saline wetlands and grasslands. It is spiny and slender, with simple broad leaves.
A hardy, clump-forming perennial native to the Iberian Peninsula and the Atlas Mountains of Morocco and Algeria. It grows on rocky slopes, and its numerous stems were formerly used to make brooms.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula in Spain and Portugal. It grows up to four metres tall and bears very small leaves.
A flowering grass whose album and erianthum varieties are native to mainland Portugal. No habitat information is supplied.

Annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed across the Mediterranean region. It grows on stony, alkaline soils around cliffs, scree and roadsides. A 2020 mainland Portuguese assessment classified its small, scattered national population as Vulnerable.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Arabis verna
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An annual herb with no native origin stated in the supplied information. It is self-supporting and has simple, broad leaves.
A shrubby flowering plant of unstated native origin. It belongs to a group of Cistus species with white or whitish-pink flowers.

A rush with no native origin stated, it has sharp-looking flowers in warm brown and maroon shades, appearing from July to September. Its hollow, smooth leaves have cross-walls that make them feel jointed.

An evergreen shrub native to southern Europe, including the western Iberian Peninsula, and northwestern Africa, including Morocco. It has tiny needle-like leaves and pink to purple bell-shaped flowers in late spring.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Veronica anagalloides subsp. anagalloides is native to mainland Portugal.

A perennial herb found from European mountain ranges into western, central and southern Asia, it has lilac flowers from July through October. It typically grows in rocky, lime-rich places, woodland edges and subalpine meadows, but also occurs beside marshes and lakes.

An evergreen shrub or small tree of Mediterranean forests, growing wild in Algeria, Morocco, Sardinia and Spain. Its glossy oval leaves are larger than those of common boxwood and may develop reddish or yellowish colouring.

A cinquefoil native to France and the northern half of the Iberian Peninsula, it grows in rocky places, banks, meadows and edges. In Portugal, the 2020 assessment classified it as Endangered, with fewer than 1,000 mature plants concentrated in one declining subpopulation.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Potentilla montana
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A branching subshrub of Eurasia, it is widespread from Portugal to Pakistan. Its deeply lobed basal leaves contrast with the narrow, unlobed stem leaves, while its flower heads have four or five yellow ray flowers but no disc flowers.

A deciduous tree native to Europe, it has rough, scaly bark and birch-like, double-toothed leaves. Its nuts hang in clusters, each enclosed in a bladder-like covering, while its very hard wood was historically used for plane soles, cogs and gears.

An evergreen, woolly perennial subshrub naturally found on coasts from Western Europe and the Mediterranean to parts of the Black Sea and Caucasus, cottonweed forms dense silver-white mounds. Its small fleshy leaves smell strongly aromatic when bruised, while its clustered yellow flower heads lack the usual daisy-like outer petals.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows on dry, stony roadsides, path banks and scrub edges, sometimes in disturbed places; current Portuguese records are confined to the Algarve, where known populations are small.

sources.title: Plumbago europaea L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A perennial herb native to mainland Portugal. Its showy flowers occur among shaded limestone rocks, cliffs and scree, and it is very rare in concentrated populations in west-central Portugal's limestone hills.

A flowering plant native to South Africa, including the Northern Cape, Eastern Cape and Free State. This highly variable species has velvety flowers of various shapes and colours, produced intermittently in late summer and autumn. The flowers smell of carrion and attract flies.

A succulent tree native to dry areas of southern Africa, the candelabra tree has thick, ridged green stems and small greenish-yellow flowers. Its milky latex is extremely poisonous and can cause blindness, severe skin irritation or poisoning if swallowed.
stories.edibilityNote: The milky latex is extremely poisonous and can poison humans and animals when ingested.

stories.summary: A deciduous shrub or small tree indigenous to southern Africa. Its purple, mauve, pink or rarely white flowers form an unusual double-star shape, followed by four-lobed reddish-brown fruits that remain after ripening. The fruits are locally eaten raw, fermented with traditional beer or mixed with goat’s milk to make berry yoghurt.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruits are locally eaten raw, fermented with traditional beer, or mixed with goat’s milk to make berry yoghurt.

stories.summary: A hardy perennial present in northern Africa and southern Europe, it has long stems with divided, fern-like leaves. White or pale lemon flowers appear from July to November.

A sedge native to Mediterranean coasts and nearby areas, capitate galingale grows in coastal sands and spreads through scaly underground roots. Its thick blue-grey leaves are U-shaped, while its flowers form a single crowded head.
Rosette-forming succulent perennial native to the Alps, Apennines and Carpathians of Europe. Its furry central rosettes resemble spider webs, and raised stems bear pink flowers in July.

A small annual spurge native to southern and western Europe, northern Africa and southwestern Asia, usually growing on coastal sand and shingle. It lies low against the ground and has fleshy grey-green leaves with reddish-purple veins. At its northern range edge in England, it was always rare and is now extinct.

An annual climbing herb whose native origin is not supplied. It has broad leaves and is associated with freshwater habitats; in Portugal it also grows along field edges, paths, banks and waterways, favouring somewhat shady or moist places.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal but introduced in the Azores and Madeira. It grows in moist meadows, hedges, agricultural floodplains and traditional orchards.

A flowering plant whose mollis and reclinata subspecies are native to mainland Portugal. It bears hanging pink flowers and hairy pods; both subspecies grow in annual grasslands on rocks and stony ground, generally over alkaline material.

sources.title: Ononis reclinata L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira but introduced in the Azores. It has yellow flowers and strongly flattened, segmented pods, and grows in annual grasslands, open woodlands, fallow ground and pastures, usually on silica-rich ground.

sources.title: Ornithopus compressus L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to the Canary Islands, Mediterranean and Middle East as far east as Iran, cupped clover has been introduced to Australia as forage. Three cultivars have been developed there.

A usually annual herb of Mediterranean distribution, though its native origin is not explicitly supplied. Its low or climbing stems bear leaves ending in simple tendrils and small pale-purple or pale-blue flowers, usually singly or in small groups; in Portugal it inhabits moist meadows, field grasslands and woodland or scrub edges.

sources.title: Vicia parviflora Cav.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.title: Vicia parviflora Cav.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A tall tree native only to north-eastern Australia, with smooth bark ranging from white to pink or coppery tones. Its narrow, glossy leaves are often lemon-scented when crushed, and its flowers are white.

An aquatic perennial native to northern and eastern Australia, and possibly New Guinea, the blue waterlily has large floating leaves and blue or lilac flowers that fade almost white. After fertilisation, its fruit is drawn underwater to ripen. Indigenous Australians traditionally ate roasted tubers, raw peeled stalks and flower buds, and roasted seeds or seed flour.
stories.edibilityNote: Indigenous Australians ate roasted tubers, raw peeled stalks and flower buds, and seeds roasted or pounded into flour.

stories.summary: A slender tree endemic to eastern Australia. Its drooping branchlets bear leaves reduced to tiny scales, while its warty, barrel-shaped cones contain brown winged seeds.
A perennial plant native to Europe, North Africa and western Asia. One specimen was recorded as collected at Salem, Oregon, in 1910.

Aquatic annual or perennial native to Europe, southwestern Asia and northern Africa. It has broad, rounded floating leaves and finely divided, thread-like submerged leaves. Its flowers are white with yellow centres.

A perennial aquatic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed in Europe. It lives submerged in shallow, temperate rivers and streams, with brush-like underwater leaves and usually no floating leaves.

sources.title: Ranunculus penicillatus (Dumort.) Bab.
sources.attribution: Info Flora, plazi (2021). Info Flora Schweiz - Ranunculaceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/kxyxpm accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A flowering herb found mainly in Europe, with reports extending to Morocco and Turkey, though its range is uncertain. It grows in shallow water or exposed mud and may carry both thread-like submerged leaves and flat, deeply three-lobed surface leaves. Its small white flowers have a yellow patch near the base.
A flowering water plant native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits cold, very shallow, nutrient-poor standing water or very slow streams, including bogs, springs, ponds and lagoons.

Dwarf amphibious annual or perennial herb of unstated native origin. It grows directly in water or very damp places, often forming dense stands, with rounded leaves along the stem and a flower-like leaf bundle at the top. Broken fragments can develop into new plants.

An aquatic perennial restricted to Europe, Turkey and extreme North Africa, it inhabits shallow, peaty, calcium-rich waters. Its thin, translucent, net-veined leaves are often reddish or brownish and may sit just below the surface, creating a distinctive drowned appearance.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Potamogeton coloratus
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An aquatic perennial native to the western Palearctic and Africa, hairlike pondweed grows mainly in standing or slow-flowing water. It survives winter as numerous resting bodies and has stiff, very narrow submerged leaves but no floating leaves.

A succulent subshrub endemic to east-central Madagascar, the panda plant has thick, velvety silver-green leaves edged or spotted with dark brown to rusty red. In its natural habitat it flowers from March to June, but indoor plants rarely bloom.
stories.edibilityNote: Mildly toxic to humans if ingested.

stories.summary: A bulbous daffodil native to the southwest Iberian Peninsula and northwest Africa. Unlike other daffodils, its central floral cup is almost completely absent. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment classified it as Critically Endangered, with only two known subpopulations there.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Narcissus cavanillesii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A tropical tree native to southeastern Brazil. It bears yellow flowers intermittently throughout the year and long, four-sided seedpods that rattle; its glossy leaflets form thin green foliage.
stories.edibilityNote: The seeds and other unspecified plant parts are poisonous if eaten.

stories.summary: A bushy perennial flowering shrub native to parts of the Mediterranean and Middle East. Its golden-yellow flowers have conspicuously long stamens, and its leaves usually produce a goat-like smell, though one subspecies lacks it.

An evergreen flowering climber native to southern southwestern mainland Portugal. It climbs using its leaf stalks and has variable leaves. Its whitish, bell-shaped flowers have a honey-like fragrance and appear from October to December.

sources.title: Clematis cirrhosa L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An evergreen or semi-evergreen ground fern native to New Zealand, the Chatham Islands, several New Zealand subantarctic islands and Australia’s Macquarie Island, prickly shield fern has an erect, scaly underground stem that may form a short trunk. Round spore clusters occur beneath its fronds.
A grass-like herb native to southern Europe, Lebanon and Syria.

Deciduous climbing plant native to southern Europe and northern Africa. It forms dense tangles covered with white flowers during warmer months; newly opened flowers have a strong sweet-almond fragrance.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows chiefly on coastal sands, especially primary and secondary dunes, and occurs less often on coastal rocks.

sources.title: Crucianella maritima L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An erect perennial native to the Mediterranean region from Portugal and Morocco to Greece, extending north into Germany. It has narrow leaves arranged in rings around the stem and a large terminal cluster of many small white to cream flowers.

A small perennial shrub with no explicitly stated native origin, Osyris alba is widespread across the Mediterranean basin, western Asia and North Africa. It is semiparasitic, with leaves produced in winter but almost entirely absent in summer, and bears small red, fleshy fruits.
Annual plant native to Southern Europe and parts of the Middle East and Northwest Africa. It flowers from May to June and grows in dry, sunny grasslands, often on carbonate ground.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, where it is assessed as Regionally Extinct. It was collected at Foz Tua in July 1905 but has not been observed there since, despite repeated searches.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Plantago sempervirens
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Its narrow, grasslike leaves and several long-stalked yellow flowers distinguish it; it grows in rocky meadows and rock cracks, particularly on limestone.

sources.title: Ranunculus gramineus L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An erect, deciduous shrub found in central and southern Europe, particularly in woods, scrub and rocky slopes. Its many smooth, thorny branches carry clustered leaves, and it produces greenish fruits with two or three stones.

A stemless flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It spreads through short, mostly underground runners and bears fragrant pale-violet flowers with dark lines and white centres; occasional plants in Portugal have white flowers.

sources.title: Viola suavis M.Bieb.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A semi-evergreen trailing perennial native to the Dinaric Alps in the former Yugoslavia. It has lavender-blue, star-shaped flowers from mid-spring to early autumn and readily seeds into cracks in walls and paving. Its leaves are edible year-round and may be added to salads.
stories.edibilityNote: The leaves are edible year-round and can be used in salads.

stories.summary: A woolly flowering plant native to northern South America and introduced to the Dominican Republic. It is grown as a hothouse ornamental.

sources.title: Kohleria hirsuta (Kunth) Regel
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A low-growing flowering perennial occurring in western Europe, English stonecrop grows on dry rocks, walls, dunes and cliffs, often near the sea. Its stubby succulent leaves may turn pink in dry conditions, and its star-like flowers are white, sometimes tinged pink.

A perennial herb with no explicitly stated native origin, it grows in wet woodland or heath in northern Iberia, southwestern France and Ireland. Its rounded, heart-based leaves form a rosette at ground level, while its small white flowers are dotted yellow.
A hemiparasitic flowering plant found in western Europe and north-western Africa. It usually grows flat along the ground, with yellowish-green strap-shaped leaves and tiny yellowish flowers.

Perennial flowering plant native to Turkey and the Caucasus. It produces large, cone-shaped clusters of open, star-shaped flowers in summer, usually white or pale blue, though cultivated forms come in other colours.
Clump-forming perennial native to the Caucasus and Turkey. It has heart-shaped, toothed, gray-hairy basal leaves and white, tubular bell-shaped flowers with pointed petals.
Evergreen flowering perennial native to the Dalmatian Mountains in Croatia. It forms vigorous, low-growing mounds and produces abundant deep purple or blue flowers from mid- to late summer.

A mostly hairless perennial flowering plant predominantly native to western Europe, heath lobelia also occurs in northern Morocco and Madeira. It has shiny, toothed dark-green leaves and blue-purple flowers from May to September. It favours seasonally waterlogged, acidic ground in grassy heaths, rough pastures and open woodland.

An annual flower native to Portugal and scattered regions eastward through Europe and Asia, French speedwell has an upright, gland-covered form and small, bright blue flowers. Its broad lower leaves have weak, blunt teeth or none, becoming smaller and narrower upward, while its fruit has two deeply separated lobes.

Aquatic carnivorous perennial bladderwort of unspecified native origin, with a broad range across Europe, Asia, central and southern Africa, Australia and New Zealand. In mainland Portugal it occurs sparsely from Minho to Baixo Alentejo and was assessed as Vulnerable because of its limited occupied area, ten known locations and continuing declines.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Utricularia australis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering herbaceous perennial native to southern Europe from Italy to western Turkey, spiny bear's-breeches has deeply cut leaves with spiny edges. In early summer it bears upright clusters of white flowers with maroon bracts.

A perennial herb occurring in western, southern and central Europe. Its roots unite into a spindle-shaped tuber, while its upright stems carry deeply divided, spiny-edged leaves and usually purple flower heads. It grows in damp meadows, marshes, banks and ditch margins.

sources.title: Cirsium tuberosum (L.) All.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.title: Cirsium tuberosum (L.) All.
sources.attribution: Info Flora, plazi (2021). Info Flora Schweiz - Asteraceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/qmbbhk accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula, reticulate thistle has received the Royal Horticultural Society’s Award of Garden Merit.

A perennial plant, viper's-grass is rare in Britain and restricted there to moist meadows in parts of England and South Wales. It has deep-yellow flower heads from May to July and exudes milky juice from its stem.

Flowering plant with two documented subspecies in Portugal: subsp. atlantica is native to mainland Portugal and Madeira but possibly introduced to the Azores, while subsp. lutescens is native to mainland Portugal.
An annual flowering plant native from Europe to western Siberia, the Himalayas and northern Africa, it grows in temperate climates.
A sunflower-family plant widespread across much of Eurasia. It is strongly aromatic, spreads mainly through creeping stems to form thick groups, and flowers very late in summer.
A perennial herb native to Europe. It has broad, divided leaves and pale-pink to purple flower rays, and grows in open forests, rocky woodland edges, scrub, meadows and fertile ground.

sources.title: Achillea distans Willd.
sources.attribution: Konrad Lauber, Gerhart Wagner, Andreas Gygax, plazi (2018). Flora Helvetica - Asteraceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/e3932j accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Upright, short-lived perennial herb native to the western and eastern Cape Provinces of South Africa, within a relatively small coastal range. Its green leaves resemble holly and have irregular prickly teeth. Daisy-like heads usually carry bright-pink outer flowers, and a plant may produce several hundred heads that cover the foliage.
A flowering plant, Senecio doria includes the variety subsp. legionensis, which is native only to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.

A perennial herb native to southeastern Europe from Greece and Italy to Ukraine and the Czech Republic, it has roundish leaves and produces its yellow flower heads one at a time. It is reportedly naturalized in Oregon.
A small perennial fern confined to western Europe and Macaronesia. It is fragile and forms large, dense colonies from creeping underground stems.
A Fuchsia species found in Brazil.
A perennial rush native to Southwestern and Central Europe, including the Alps and Pyrenees. It is grown as an ornamental grass and can escape gardens and become invasive in some climates.
A flowering plant represented in Portugal by two subspecies, both native to mainland Portugal; the nominate subspecies is introduced in the Azores. It is an annual.

A flowering plant native to South America and introduced in mainland Portugal and the Azores. Its branches and narrow, smooth-edged leaves are densely covered with close-lying hairs, while its ripe fruit is dull, dark black-purple. In Portugal it grows in shady, disturbed field margins and streamside woodland.

sources.title: Solanum chenopodioides Lam.
sources.attribution: Info Flora, plazi (2021). Info Flora Schweiz - Solanaceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/jb8k33 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A biennial or perennial flowering plant, it includes two subspecies in mainland Portugal that are native only to the Iberian Peninsula. Its rough, hairy foliage has strongly wavy or curled leaf edges, while its dark purple flowers turn deep blue and bloom in spring.

A small evergreen tree native to and found only in the Azores, Azores laurel is a major part of the islands’ laurel and high-elevation juniper forests. It also occurs on lava flows, in coastal and mountain scrub, and in forested peat bogs.
A large evergreen tree native to humid uplands on Madeira and the Canary Islands. It has been introduced to several nearby Azorean islands and is threatened by habitat loss.

A succulent flowering plant endemic to the Canary Islands, the candle-plant has jointed branches resembling rows of sausages. Thick elongated leaves cluster at branch tips and fall at the start of the dry season, while fragrant grey-white flowers may appear from March through October.

A succulent shrub endemic to the Canary Islands, it grows in a narrow coastal belt. Its fleshy four- or five-sided trunks resemble cacti and bear spines instead of leaves; it also produces reddish-green flowers and poisonous latex.
A flowering plant endemic to the Drakensberg in Southern Africa. It grows in moist grassland and on rocky slopes, and both of its subspecies are classified as least concern.

A low-branching evergreen tropical shrub native to tropical South America. Its leaves close and droop from dusk until morning, while its showy powder-puff flower heads gain their colour from numerous long stamens that are white below and pink above.

A herbaceous perennial whose native range depends on classification: it is treated either as widespread around the Mediterranean or native only to the Levant. It forms a ground-level leaf rosette around a large, sometimes human-shaped taproot, with usually purple flowers and yellow or orange berries. The root and leaves are poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: The root and leaves are poisonous; reported consumption has caused severe atropine-like symptoms, including hallucinations and rapid heartbeat.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Mandragora autumnalis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It parasitises the roots of Cistus albidus, with its vegetative body hidden inside the host as filaments. It is rare in Portugal, where widely scattered populations occur in dry scrub and open woodland.

Perennial herb native to the Spanish Mediterranean coast. Its varieties differ in silkiness and Mediterranean distribution, while the plant bears yellow flowers and fleshy leaflets. It grows in habitats ranging from sand to heavy saline soils.

Cactus-like succulent tree native to central India, Odisha and southern India’s Deccan. It has spreading, nearly five-sided branches, thorns and thick, spoon-shaped leaves. The leaves are eaten raw or cooked, including boiled with syrup or chopped as stuffing in parts of the Philippines, while the latex is irritating and toxic.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves are eaten raw or cooked, including boiled with syrup, made into sweets or used as stuffing in parts of the Philippines.

stories.summary: Subtropical succulent tree native to Pakistan, India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Myanmar. Its thick branches bear clusters of sharp spines and fleshy leaves, with reddish flower-like structures grouped near the branch ends.

A shrub native to Morocco’s Atlas Mountain slopes, resin spurge forms broad, cushion-shaped clumps. Its upright, cactus-like succulent stems are four-angled and lined with short, sharp pairs of spines.
A shrub or thick-trunked tree native to southern Africa. Its short, horizontal branches form rosettes at the top of the main trunk and are succulent and triangular in cross-section.

Succulent shrub native to Mozambique, Eswatini and parts of South Africa. It has deeply segmented, three-angled stems with pairs of bull-horn-like spines, and small leaves that later fall off. Its showy fruit pops open when ripe.

A small, branching flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Berlengas archipelago, it grows in open areas near coastal cliffs. Its yellow flowers appear between March and July, and the species is endangered.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Pulicaria microcephala
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A perennial flowering plant endemic to western Iberia, including Portugal, Galicia and the Sierra Morena; one subspecies is native to the Berlengas archipelago. It generally has several low or rising stems, rosette-forming basal leaves and loose clusters of hairy, funnel-shaped flowers.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal. It is protected under Annex V of the Habitats Directive.
Herbaceous perennial native to northwestern Spain and western Portugal. Its glossy dark-green foliage and hollow stems smell faintly of aniseed, while its pale flowers form broad, flat clusters.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Angelica pachycarpa
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A deciduous tree native to eastern China, Taiwan and Japan, it usually has glossy, three-lobed leaves, though unlobed leaves sometimes occur. Its paired winged seeds point forward and often overlap.

A flowering shrub or small tree endemic to the Andes from Colombia to northern Chile, red angel's trumpet has hanging, trumpet-shaped flowers in vivid red, yellow, orange and green. All parts are poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous and contain tropane alkaloids in varying proportions.

stories.summary: A shrub or small tree native from Uganda to South Africa, forest num-num grows in woodland and forest. It has fragrant white flowers and fruit that turns red when ripe.

An evergreen tree native to low-elevation Himalayan woodlands in China, India, Pakistan, Nepal and Bhutan, it has grey-green leaves with pale, fuzzy undersides. White bracts surround its small greenish flowers, while several fruits fuse into a red body that is edible but usually bitter.
stories.edibilityNote: The fused red fruit is edible but usually bitter.

stories.summary: An evergreen to semi-evergreen shrub native to mountains, mixed forests and open places in western China, willow-leaved cotoneaster has arching branches and narrow, willow-like leaves with grey hairs beneath. Its small red fruits ripen in autumn and can persist into winter.

A deciduous shrub native to Japan, it is common throughout the country on forest edges and cliffs. It has opposite, thick, toothed leaves and flowers from May to July in Japan; a double-flowered form is popular in gardens.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation through Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.
A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation, including Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.
A flowering plant whose two listed subspecies are endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Both grow on coastal dunes and sands, including primary dunes and hollows between dunes.
A flowering plant whose two listed varieties are native to mainland Portugal. It grows on coastal sands, mainly secondary dunes and sometimes ancient dunes.

An often-climbing shrub occurring around the Mediterranean except France, and on Madeira and the Canary Islands. It has glossy dark-green, toothed leaves, white or pale lilac flowers, and black fruit. It grows in scrub and evergreen woodland, especially near coasts, and in Portugal also occupies limestone rock crevices and scree.

sources.title: Prasium majus L.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.title: Prasium majus L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Flowering plant whose subspecies have different documented origins: subsp. cabezudoi is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, while subsp. grandiflorus is native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal. It grows in ponds and lagoons in both mountain and lowland areas.

A perennial, wintergreen aquatic plant native to temperate Europe, especially southern and western Europe. It roots in shallow water and bears broad floating leaves alongside finely divided, hairlike submerged leaves. Its flowers are pure white, and the plant is poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant is poisonous when eaten.

sources.title: Ranunculus ololeucos J.Lloyd
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to the central and southern coast of mainland Portugal. It is an uncommon plant of coastal sands and secondary dunes, particularly near limestone areas or on lime-rich sandstone sands. It is protected under Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.
A flowering plant found in the southern Iberian Peninsula, including mainland Portugal but not the Azores or Madeira. It favours uncultivated and disturbed ground and flowers from April to September.
A flowering wetland plant native to mainland Portugal and the Azores.
Annual herb native to the western Mediterranean Basin. It has a self-supporting growth form and flowers visited by several kinds of flies and a butterfly.

Flowering plant whose two listed subspecies are native to mainland Portugal. Unlike the marsh thistle used for comparison, it has well-developed stem leaves rather than especially developed basal leaves.
An aquatic rush native to the Mediterranean. In Portugal, it inhabits seasonally flooded meadows around ponds, reservoirs, lagoons and waterways.
A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal. It grows in clearings among coastal dune scrub, between dunes and sometimes beneath open pine woodland.

An annual plant native to southwestern Europe and Morocco, French groundsel is widespread across southern France and the Iberian Peninsula. It colonizes isolated, harsh habitats such as deserts, steppes, dry shrublands and salty coastal plains.
A climbing plant of unspecified native origin, Mediterranean asparagus is visited by Western honey bees and several kinds of flies and bees.

A deciduous shrub native to inland Portugal and central-western to southwestern Spain. It branches densely from the base and has spiny stems; male flowers are upright or spreading, while female flowers are somewhat hanging.
An Iberian-endemic flowering plant. It grows on stony ground, rock faces and fissures, walls, scree and sometimes roadsides, avoiding lime-rich ground.
Flowering plant; the subspecies Bufonia macropetala subsp. willkommiana is native to mainland Portugal.
An Iberian-endemic flowering plant. In Portugal, it grows in dry meadows, pastures and open scrub clearings on acidic ground.

A flowering plant whose listed subspecies are native to mainland Portugal. The typical subspecies grows in dry, sandy scrub clearings, pinewoods, cork-oak woodland and pasture; subspecies tuberculata occurs on acidic coastal sands beneath pine and cork-oak woodland.

Perennial flowering herb found in southwestern Europe and North Africa; the variety represented in Portugal is endemic to mainland Portugal. A 1913 account describes large, nearly spherical clusters with up to 50 or more flowers, blooming from June to September in wet places and ditches in central and southern Portugal. The species is classed as Near Threatened.
An erect deciduous shrub native to central and southern Europe and southwestern Asia. Its narrow grey-green leaves turn yellow in autumn, while green catkins appear with the new leaves in spring.

A perennial flowering rush native to Europe and southwest Asia, including the British Isles, great woodrush forms clumps of glossy, bright green leaves that stay greenish through winter. Scattered white hairs along the leaf edges help distinguish it from similar plants, and its tiny chestnut-brown flowers appear from mid-spring to summer.
A highly branched shrub found across much of the Iberian Peninsula, with clusters of yellow flowers from May to July. It favours dry, acidic, nutrient-poor soils in woodland clearings and heathland.
An Iberian-endemic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in meadows beside waterways, along riverside woodland edges and on damp, shaded banks, usually over acidic sand or shale.
An Iberian-endemic flowering plant. It grows in scrub along woodland edges and in open plantations, favouring rocky shale or granite and occurring rarely on limestone.
A perennial herb native to mainland Portugal. It has yellow flower heads on upright, sometimes hollow stems and grows in damp meadows, pastures, woodland edges and deciduous woods.

sources.title: Crepis lampsanoides (Gouan) Tausch
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An evergreen dwarf shrub native to eastern England, France, Spain and Portugal, dwarf gorse is restricted to lowland heathland. It forms low bushes among heather, with small scales or spines instead of typical leaves and soft, crowded green spines on its shoots. Yellow flowers appear mainly in late summer and autumn, rarely before July.
Flowering plant native exclusively to the Iberian Peninsula. It belongs to the legume family and occurs in mainland Portugal.

A perennial flowering plant whose native origin is not specified. Its spreading branches form mats, with narrow rolled-edged leaves and whitish flowers; it inhabits maritime sands, shingle and dry salt marshes.
A flowering wetland perennial native to Europe, North Africa and western Asia, tubular water-dropwort has brittle, inflated hollow stems and forms distinctive pink fruiting balls after flowering.
stories.edibilityNote: In parts of southern Italy and Turkey, the basal leaves have traditionally been cooked as a meal.

stories.summary: An aquatic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in shallow, temperate standing water, including lakes, ponds, pools and quiet backwaters, generally where the water is nutrient-rich and neutral.
Tussock-forming perennial sedge native to the Mediterranean. It favours wet, non-saline bogs, ditches and marshes, and bears unusually long female flower spikes.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s central-west limestone region. It has fleshy, scalloped leaves, white flowers and dense glandular hairs, and grows mainly in limestone rock crevices and walls.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Saxifraga cintrana
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A perennial flowering plant native to Brazil, purple allamanda is grown as an ornamental and bears purple, bell-shaped flowers. Its stems can yield very strong, silky white fibre after chemical treatment.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in dry, often stony clearings among open scrub, thickets and holm-oak woods, especially on limestone, gypsum or clay soils.

sources.title: Cleonia lusitanica (L.) L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An annual native to the Mediterranean, Middle East, India, Pakistan and Central Asia. Its woolly growth bears conspicuous three-part fruits that twist open and propel their seeds. Fruit-coat and leaf-sap extracts yielded a blue-purple dye historically used in manuscripts and as a food colorant, although consuming the plant may cause digestive illness.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit-coat or leaf-sap colorant was used in Dutch cheese and liquors, although consuming the plant may cause digestive illness.

stories.summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It is found in sparse grasslands and meadows on dry, acidic, sandy or stony ground.

Evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand, pūriri has glossy leaves usually divided into five leaflets and large tubular flowers ranging from pink or red to occasional white. Some flowers and ripe fruit occur year-round, with flowering heaviest in winter and fruit more common in summer.
stories.edibilityNote: The bitter fruit is not a traditional Māori food.

stories.summary: A small evergreen tree endemic to Macaronesia, it is found in the Azores, Madeira and the Canary Islands and is an important part of high-altitude laurel forest. It has leathery dark-green leaves, white to pink flowers and red toxic berries.
stories.edibilityNote: The red berries are toxic.

stories.summary: A spurge-family plant native to southern Africa.

An agave native to the Mexican states of Hidalgo, Tamaulipas and San Luis Potosí, it forms clusters of fleshy blue-green to yellow-green leaves with relatively soft brown spines. Its tall flowering stalk bears green flowers packed closely against the stem in a narrow column.
A succulent subshrub or shrub native from Mali to Djibouti, growing mainly in seasonally dry tropical habitats.

sources.title: Aloe macrocarpa Tod. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An evergreen tree native to Australia, with rough bark, waxy leaves and flushes of pink new growth. Its cream-white flowers are followed in winter by edible berries ranging from white to maroon.
stories.edibilityNote: An 1889 account says Aboriginal people and children ate the mildly acidic fruit and called it wholesome; it has also been described as rather tasteless.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native only to coastal New South Wales near Sydney. Its rosette of long, sword-shaped leaves produces a towering stalk topped with bright red, trumpet-shaped flowers visited by bees and nectar-feeding birds.
stories.edibilityNote: Aboriginal people roasted young stems for eating and roasted roots to make a kind of cake.

stories.summary: An annual herb with native subspecies in mainland Portugal and Madeira. It commonly branches from the base, bears white or lilac flowers, and grows in dry, stony grasslands, scrub clearings and beside temporary waterways.

sources.title: Convolvulus siculus L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An aquatic or emergent flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It inhabits very wet, acidic places such as pools, lakes, springs, streams and peat bogs.

A bulbous herbaceous perennial native across much of Europe, northern Africa and western Asia. Its tall stems carry tightly packed, spherical or egg-shaped heads containing many reddish-purple flowers; small bulblets and occasional bulbils can make it potentially invasive in gardens.
A wild onion native to Spain, Portugal and Morocco. Its flowers are yellow, and in Portugal it grows in generally damp perennial meadows within alder, oak and pine woods.

sources.title: Allium scorzonerifolium Desf. ex Redouté
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). English Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/c3kkgh accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A bulb-forming perennial herb found across southern and central Europe. It bears rounded clusters of white, bell-shaped flowers with stamens projecting beyond the petals.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Allium ericetorum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A perennial herb recorded in western Iberia and western France. It grows in peat bogs, wet meadows and riverside forests on acidic soils, flowering from September to October and fruiting in November.

A stemless perennial flowering plant native to the western Mediterranean Basin, particularly the Iberian Peninsula and northwestern Maghreb. Its leaves rise directly from a tuber, while its flower cluster is enclosed by a purple-spotted tube with a curved, forward-tilting helmet shape.

A bulbous perennial bluebell endemic to the northwestern Iberian Peninsula. It grows chiefly in shady woodland and produces clusters of pale-blue spring flowers, usually in March and April but sometimes as late as June in upland areas.

A bulbous perennial strictly endemic to the western and central-western Iberian Peninsula. Its narrow leaves and upright flower stalk emerge from a single underground bulb. Between March and July it typically bears white flowers, often with a green stripe, in rocky crevices, mountain scrub and other open ground on acidic soils.

A bulbous perennial endemic to mountains of northern Portugal, southern Galicia and the westernmost Spanish Central System, paradise lily grows sporadically in cool, shady woods. It bears loose clusters of white, broadly bell-shaped or star-shaped flowers in spring.

A flowering plant of unspecified overall native origin, it has two documented subspecies in mainland Portugal. The typical subspecies is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, while subspecies alpestris is endemic to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant native across Europe to western Siberia and Turkey.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Myosotis welwitschii belongs to the borage family. It is protected under Portuguese or European Community law, including Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows on rocky ground and in woodland or scrub clearings, favouring acidic soils in mountain areas.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in rock crevices and open grassland on acidic, stony soils.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It inhabits acidic sandy grassland, rock crevices and rocky slopes, and sometimes occurs on dunes.

A sedge native to Atlantic Europe from Fennoscandia to the Iberian Peninsula, it grows in damp, acidic habitats such as heaths and moorland. Its fruiting structures bear two conspicuous green veins, while aging leaves develop wine-red patches.
Sedge native to the lowlands of Western and Central Europe, where it grows in moist, shady places, particularly alder–ash woodland. Tiny red dots on its utricles distinguish it from similar species.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It usually grows in shade beneath woodland or on rocky outcrops and is not restricted to a particular substrate.

Deciduous fern endemic to Macaronesia and the Iberian Peninsula. It has thick, scaly creeping stems and broad, finely divided fronds, and grows on tree trunks, branches and mossy rocks in cool, humid places influenced by the ocean.

Large herbaceous flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows mainly in hay meadows and along stream banks in the mountains of northern Portugal, where it is considered Vulnerable, with only seven known locations and an estimated population of fewer than 2,500 mature plants.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Knautia nevadensis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Flowering plant native to Europe. It is less acrid than other spurges, while the purple-leaved cultivar 'Chameleon' is the form most commonly planted in gardens.

sources.title: Euphorbia dulcis L.
sources.attribution: Info Flora, plazi (2021). Info Flora Schweiz - Euphorbiaceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/2m8qx3 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in scrub on cleared or neglected land, field edges, slopes and roadsides, mainly on disturbed acidic soils in Atlantic-influenced areas.

A herbaceous perennial native to western Europe and northern Africa. It has characteristically wavy-edged leaves, winged stems with black glands, and bright-yellow flowers whose petals are tinged red on the back.
Iris native to Europe, mainly Spain and Portugal. It normally carries one blue-purple or deep-purple flower per stem in June, marked by a yellow or orange beard.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It occurs in generally moist grassland and scrub, cultivated fields and roadsides, preferring stony, silica-rich soils.

sources.title: Malva tournefortiana L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Woody flowering subshrub native to mainland Portugal. It has slender branches, small deciduous leaves and blue flowers in clusters near the upper branches, flowering from February to June.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in dry grassland, pine clearings and open scrub, usually on dry, stony, silica-rich soils.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It occurs in clearings among heathland and pine woods on silica-rich ground.

A meadow-rue native to Portugal and Spain on the Iberian Peninsula and to Morocco and Algeria in northwestern Africa. It belongs to the Betic-Rifan flora shared by southern Spain and northern Morocco.

Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal but introduced in the Azores and Madeira. It frequents fallow fields, pasture, scrub clearings and slopes, often on moist, acidic sandy soils enriched by human or animal activity.

A rare wild pear shrub or small deciduous tree of Atlantic western Europe, occurring in France, Spain and Portugal, with a small British presence believed to be anciently introduced. It grows in hedgerows and woodland edges and bears pale cream blossom tinged pink, with an unpleasant smell.

A perennial herb found in Western Europe, meadow bastard toadflax has narrow, three-veined leaves arranged alternately on upright stems. Its tube-shaped flowers bloom in June and July, with petal tips rolling inward as the fruit develops.

A perennial plant of unstated native origin, commonly found in Western Europe and North Africa beside rivers, ponds and other damp places. Its greenish-purple square stems have conspicuous corner wings, and it bears small, rounded maroon-brown flowers.

A flowering plant with a native range described as oceanic western Europe, from the British Isles and Atlantic France to northwestern Spain and Portugal near the Tagus. Its single flowers range from milky violet to greyish pink, with deep purple veins on the lower petal and green spurs behind.
Fern native to mainland Portugal and the Azores and Madeira archipelagos. It favors rocky habitats and also occurs elsewhere in Europe, Africa, and Central and South America.

Small salt-tolerant shrub found mainly along Mediterranean coasts and northward along Atlantic coasts to southeastern England; its native origin is not explicitly stated. Its appearance varies widely, and it grows in salt flats, salt marshes and similar dry or semi-dry salty habitats.
A daffodil native to Spain, Portugal and Morocco. It has solitary yellow flowers that range from horizontal to upright and grows on rocky cliffs, dunes and meadows in either lime-rich or acidic soil.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows on coastal sandy soils in pine woods and clearings among dune scrub.
A flowering plant of unspecified native origin, sea pearlwort is found throughout Europe, Southwest Asia, North Africa, the Canary Islands and the Azores.

An annual flowering herb native to mainland Portugal. In Portugal, it grows in grasslands on sand and acidic ground; its flowers are reported as usually four-parted, though this feature needs confirmation.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. In Portugal, it grows on coastal sands, rocks and cliffs, sometimes in grassland on stabilized dunes.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira, but introduced in the Azores. It belongs to the pea family.

An annual herb whose native origin is not stated. It is extremely short-stemmed, with upright three-part leaves and small white flower clusters tucked into the leaf axils. Its heavy fruits press the clusters to the ground, where the seeds germinate.

sources.title: Trifolium suffocatum L.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A parasitic flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa, from the Canary Islands and Madeira to Morocco and Algeria. In Portugal, it grows in disturbed grassy or agricultural places and parasitizes herbs, mainly daisies and their relatives; in Tunisia it was collected on Calendula suffruticosa.

sources.title: Orobanche calendulae Pomel
sources.attribution: Mokni R E, Domina G, Barone G, felipe (2023). New records of the genus Orobanche L. (Orobanchaceae) to the Tunisian flora with lectotypification of the name O. rapum-genistae Thuill.. Adansonia. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/k8tygy accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An annual grass native to parts of Europe, western Asia and North Africa. It has simple, broad leaves and a self-supporting growth form.

An annual herb native to the Azores and found throughout much of the Mediterranean. Its upright stems bear sparse stinging hairs, coarse-toothed leaves and tail-like male flower spikes near the top. In Sicily, its cooked leaves are eaten as a spinach-like vegetable or in soup.
stories.edibilityNote: In Sicily, cooked leaves are eaten as nettle spinach or soup; the plant was also eaten in 19th-century Greece.

sources.title: Urtica membranacea Poir.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A bulbous plant endemic to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula. In mainland Portugal it occurs only in the Algarve, on rocky limestone ground and outcrops, usually in small scattered groups. There it was assessed as Vulnerable, with fewer than 10,000 mature plants estimated and a continuing national decline inferred.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Narcissus gaditanus
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A tiny fern whose native origin is not stated in the supplied information. Its short fronds are densely hairy and gland-bearing, and it produces spores through most of the year. During hot, dry summers its fronds dehydrate and appear dead, then quickly become green again after autumn rain.
A flowering plant native to southern Europe and North Africa.
