stories.summary: A moss endemic to the mountains of Europe, icy rock-moss grows in humid, rocky alpine and subalpine habitats. In Britain it typically occurs on rocks in streams fed by snow patches.

A deciduous tree native to the eastern Mediterranean, Oriental sweetgum occurs mainly in floodplain stands in southwestern Turkey and on Rhodes. Its colourful autumn leaves are especially valued, and sap obtained from June to September is softened, pressed and made into an aromatic balsam or distilled oil.

An amphibious annual plant native to the Mediterranean Basin. It produces grass-like submerged leaves, spoon-shaped floating leaves or lance-shaped emergent leaves depending on water depth, and in Portugal it is now restricted to two areas.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Damasonium bourgaei
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A deciduous tree originating around the Yangtze River in southern China. Its strongly fragrant white, pink or red flowers open in mid-winter, before the leaves. Across East Asian cuisines, the fruit is used in juices, sauces and alcohol, or prepared by pickling or drying.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is used in East Asian juices, sauces and alcoholic drinks, and may be pickled or dried.

stories.summary: A flowering plant whose range extends from eastern South Africa and Madagascar through tropical Africa to western Arabia. It produces tall spikes of yellow to scarlet flowers, often red-streaked over yellow, and is the principal parent of large-flowered grandiflora hybrids.

Shrub or small tree native to China, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, the Himalayan region of India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines. It bears fragrant white flower clusters in spring, followed by red berries that mature to black.

A shrub occurring widely from eastern and southeastern Asia through New Guinea to northern Australia and the Solomon Islands, it sheds its leaves during the dry season. Its slender, straggling branches bear small white flowers and fruits that ripen brownish orange.

A perennial subshrub native to the western and central Mediterranean, it occurs mainly on cliffs and rocky coasts. Its stiff, branched stems and deeply lobed leaves are coated in grey-white woolly hairs, while its flowers are yellow and daisy-like.

An annual herb native to western Asia and southern Europe, yellow pheasant's-eye has finely divided foliage and red flowers with black centres. In mainland Portugal it grows among traditional dryland crops and was assessed as Vulnerable because of its limited range, few locations and continuing decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Adonis microcarpa
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An Arctic–alpine rosette-forming plant distributed from eastern Canada to Russia and in southern European mountains, it grows in damp places such as stream edges and wet rock ledges. Its loose flower clusters have white petals marked near the base with yellow or red spots.
An Asian fig tree native from Assam to Taiwan, through Southeast Asia, Malesia and New Guinea. Male and female flowers grow on separate trees, and its fruit becomes greenish yellow when ripe.

A flowering plant native to northeastern Spain, southern France and Italy, Crimean iris grows on rocky or sandy hillsides and in woodland. It produces yellow or violet flowers in March and April and prefers dry conditions during its summer dormancy.

An orchid native to Mediterranean southern Europe and northern Africa, with its range extending east to Iran and Turkmenistan. Its three recognized subspecies occupy distinct western Mediterranean, central and eastern Mediterranean, and Turkey-to-Central Asian ranges.
A flowering plant with no stated native origin, goat pea belongs to the pea family and is introduced in mainland Portugal.
A perennial bulb native to Spain and France and naturalised in Turkey. It is low-growing, with yellow flowers that have a slightly lemony fragrance.
Fast-growing deciduous climbing plant native to East Asia. It bears large orange trumpet-shaped flowers in summer and attaches to porous surfaces using scattered aerial roots.

An annual flowering herb native to the desert southwest of North America and northern and central Mexico. Its foliage is hairy, and its bright purple, lavender or pink bell-shaped flowers grow alone or in small clusters.
A fast-growing tree native to Africa. It has dark grey to grey-brown bark, reddish-brown heartwood, spirally arranged leaves clustered at branch ends, and sweet-scented white flowers.

Annual herb native to Africa, southern Europe, and parts of Asia from East Asia to India and Central Asia. Its leaves, stems and seeds can be eaten raw or cooked, though leaves may concentrate nitrates when grown on nitrogen-rich soil.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves, stems and seeds are eaten raw or cooked; leaves are widely used as a vegetable, often in sauces and stews.

stories.summary: An ornamental tree native to parts of Asia, including Korea, Taiwan, mid-southern China and Japan’s Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu, Ilex integra has light-yellow flowers. Its bark is used in birdlime, and it is sometimes planted as a sacred tree.

A perennial flowering plant native to Europe and parts of North Africa, parsley water-dropwort inhabits mainly coastal wetlands and some inland freshwater marshes. Its lower leaves are parsley-like, its leaf stalks smell of celery, and it bears white flowers from June to September in northern Europe. No part is edible by humans.
stories.edibilityNote: No part of the plant is edible by humans.

stories.summary: A perennial flowering plant found across western, central and southeastern Europe, including the British Isles. It grows mainly in damp, neutral grasslands and has stout woody roots and small yellowish flowers.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. There it grows in heath and other acid-loving scrub or beneath deciduous woodland, usually on siliceous ground.

sources.title: Physospermum cornubiense (L.) DC.
sources.attribution: Jeanmonod D, Schlüssel A, carolina (2012). Notes et contributions à la flore de Corse, XXIV. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15553/c2012v672a11 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An annual plant distributed from central Europe to western Asia, mostly near coasts. It is delicate and often much-branched, with blue-green narrow leaves and tiny yellowish to orange flowers, and favors damp or disturbed salty ground.

sources.title: Bupleurum tenuissimum L.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A herbaceous perennial native to the UK and found mainly in Central and Southern Europe, hog's fennel is rare in Britain and now limited to parts of Essex and Kent. Its greenish-yellow flower clusters rise above dark green leaves, while its stout root releases strongly sulphur-scented latex when cut in spring.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It belongs to the family Apiaceae and is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

An annual or biennial flowering plant native to southern and south-central Europe, though probably not native in northern parts of its range. It is hairy or bristly, with a hollow ridged stem and flat clusters of white flowers whose outer petals are conspicuously longer.
A fern found locally along Europe's Atlantic seaboard. It was first recorded in Britain in February 2000 beside Cornwall's River Camel.
A perennial fern confined to Atlantic coastal western Europe and Macaronesia. Its pale yellow-green, often arching fronds have a characteristically crisped appearance and a hay-like scent.

A robust deciduous or partly evergreen fern native mainly to western and central Europe, broad buckler-fern occurs chiefly in mountains in southern Europe and also between the Black and Caspian seas. Its dark green, finely divided fronds have ribs covered with brown scales.

A perennial flowering plant occurring across western Europe. It has spear-shaped, widely toothed leaves and white flowers that fade to pink, blooming from June to August; it is easily confused with two other willowherbs.
A flowering plant native from Europe to China. It is common in moist, disturbed lowland sites and can be difficult to distinguish from several other willowherbs.

A wild rose native to Western, Central and Southern Europe, the field rose is a vigorous, thorny, rambling shrub with long, arching or scrambling purple stems. It bears slightly fragrant, creamy-white flowers in a single midsummer flush, followed by oval orange-red hips.

Perennial mint-family herb native to Western Europe and North Africa. The nominate subspecies is tufted, hairy and mint-scented, with dark green leaves and relatively large, dark flowers. The leaves can be infused for aromatic tea or added to cooked foods for a pungent flavour likened to marjoram and mint.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves can be infused as aromatic tea or added to cooked food for a pungent, marjoram-and-mint-like flavour.

stories.summary: A dense, upright flowering shrub endemic to near-coastal southwestern Western Australia. It has narrow elliptical leaves and head-like clusters of pale to deep pink tubular flowers, blooming mainly from August to February. It grows on coastal dunes and rocky headlands.
A plant of unspecified native origin, found in Sicily, Greece and Turkey. It has a flavor similar to common oregano and is reported to have antimicrobial activity.

A perennial plant of unspecified native origin, bush basil is valued in Portugal for its pleasant smell. Known there as manjerico, it is traditionally sold in small decorated pots during June’s Santos Populares celebrations and was given by men to their lovers.
A short-stemmed South African plant, Goat's-foot has bluish flowers.
A perennial plant with underground storage organs, endemic to South Africa’s Eastern and Western Cape and associated with fynbos. It bears red-purple flowers from April to July.

sources.title: Chasmanthe aethiopica (L.) N.E.Br.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A perennial flowering plant whose native origin is not stated, falling stars is widely distributed across southern and eastern Africa from South Africa to Sudan. It forms large colonies in moist, shady forests and along riverbanks, producing bright orange-to-red flowers from June through August.
A flowering plant native to the temperate and subtropical Northern Hemisphere and Southern Africa, carpet cinquefoil belongs to the rose family.
A red seaweed found in European waters.

A herbaceous perennial native to Mexico, the Caribbean, West Africa, Central America and much of South America. It has broad, fleshy leaves and small pink flowers, and is widely grown in tropical regions as a leaf vegetable. In India’s Mithila region, the leaves are prepared as vegetables and fritters.
stories.edibilityNote: The leaves are widely grown as a vegetable and are prepared as vegetables and fritters in the Mithila region.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to East and Southeast Asia, Asian taro has large, light-green, diamond- to teardrop-shaped leaves. Its flowers produce a sweet scent that is strongest at night.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves and stems are eaten cooked as vegetables; the corm is sometimes boiled and mashed. No part should be eaten raw or undercooked.

stories.summary: A deciduous flowering shrub native to dense forests from the Himalayas through southern China to Taiwan. It has coarse, broadly oval leaves and large, flat flower heads in late summer, typically pale blue or pink with white or pale pink florets around the edges.

An evergreen coastal tree native to southern and eastern Africa, white milkwood has dense foliage and small, foul-smelling greenish flowers. Its purplish-black berries are edible, and both the berries and leathery leaves contain milky latex.
stories.edibilityNote: The purplish-black berries are edible.

stories.summary: Upright perennial herb native to the Mediterranean, including Algeria, Morocco, Portugal, Spain and Sicily. It has a woody base, oval leaves and dense cushions of violet-purple summer flowers; cultivated forms also flower in white, red, pink or dark purple.

A herbaceous perennial in the bedstraw and coffee family. Tiny hooks on its leaves and stems let it climb. Its long roots, harvested after two years, have supplied red textile dyes since ancient times.
stories.edibilityNote: Root-derived dyes have been used as food ingredients.

stories.summary: A fern species in the family Pteridaceae.

Grass thought to have originated in China, although genomic evidence suggests separate domestication of naked and hulled oats in China and Europe. Its edible seeds readily shed their hulls when threshed.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds are edible; naked oats have long been used as food, while Cornish grain was sprouted, dried and crushed for porridge, puddings and ale.

stories.summary: Fast-growing shrub or small tree endemic to eastern Australia. It has pale green, narrowly oval leaves and white to pale-yellow flower clusters; its egg-shaped fruits are covered with black, blister-like warts.
Flowering plant native to southwestern Europe and northwestern Africa, including the Iberian Peninsula, Balearic Islands, parts of North Africa, Sardinia, and northern and central Italy.

A flowering plant found around much of the central Mediterranean Basin, Mediterranean meadow saffron produces abundant small pink-to-purple flowers and foliage in autumn. Its variable flowers may open flat like stars or remain cup-shaped.
A subshrub native to Portugal, Spain and France. It usually has several stems and pale lilac to whitish petals that are fringed only halfway.

sources.title: Dianthus hyssopifolius L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A poisonous nightshade native to several African countries, including Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Mozambique, it has tomato-like fruits that are green when raw and yellow when ripe. In eastern Kenya, village children cautiously use the poisonous yellow fruits as footballs.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant and its yellow fruits are described as poisonous; no qualified human food use is given.

stories.summary: A fast-growing, branching cactus found in Bolivia, Paraguay, southern Brazil, northern Argentina and Uruguay. It may bear straight white spines, orange-to-yellow flowers from late spring into summer, and club-shaped fruit that ripens purple-red.
Succulent flowering plant native to South Africa. It forms a dense scrambling or climbing growth with glossy, fleshy, coarsely toothed leaves and clusters of honey-scented yellow flowers.

Perennial climber native to southern Africa, from South Africa’s coastal Eastern Cape to eastern Zimbabwe. It has bright green, fleshy, ivy-like leaves with purple veins and produces cinnamon-scented, bright yellow, daisy-like flowers, generally from mid-autumn to winter.

A perennial grass native to most of Europe, southwestern Asia and northwestern Africa. It has densely packed flowerheads and is much smaller than Timothy grass, with which it is often confused; it flowers from June to August.

A perennial fern native across much of Asia, Australia, New Zealand and Polynesia. Gray hairs mark the undersides of its leaves, while long rhizomes help it form thick ground cover; outside its native range it is invasive in several regions.
A very large palm native to peninsular Thailand, it has exceptionally long, twice-divided fronds bearing thousands of fan- or wedge-shaped leaflets.

A palm native to southern Brazil, Uruguay and northern Argentina. Its solitary trunk often leans and commonly retains old leaf bases for years. The ripe fruit may be yellow, orange, red or purple, with sweet, juicy, slightly fibrous flesh that is edible.
stories.edibilityNote: The sweet fruit is edible; ripe flesh is described as juicy and slightly fibrous.

stories.summary: Slow-growing palm native to southernmost Brazil and Uruguay. Its feather-like leaves arch toward a thick, stout trunk. The highly aromatic fruit varies in colour and sweet-sour flavour, and the larger-fruited pulposa type is commonly cultivated locally for food.
stories.edibilityNote: The aromatic ripe fruit is eaten; larger-fruited pulposa-type palms are cultivated in Brazilian and Uruguayan orchards.

stories.summary: A small palm endemic to the highlands of southern Brazil. Its flower-bearing woody sheath is densely covered with distinctive rust-coloured woolly hairs, and its leaves arch back toward the trunk. Locally, the fruit pulp is used to make beverages, wine, juice, jellies and jams.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit pulp is used locally to make beverages, wine, juice, jellies and jams.

stories.summary: A palm native to the Mascarene Islands. It has a solitary ringed trunk and a swollen, white-waxy crown base, while its oval fruits ripen purple or black.
A tall, slender palm native to Central and South America and Trinidad and Tobago. It produces edible açaí fruit and hearts of palm, although taking the heart kills this usually single-stemmed tree.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is edible and used for beverages; the heart of palm is also eaten, but harvesting it kills the single-stemmed tree.

stories.summary: Palm endemic to Lord Howe Island, Australia. Mature crowns contain roughly 36 leaves, and the species is restricted to the island's volcanic soils.

A fan palm native to parts of South and Southeast Asia and Yunnan, China. It has large fan-shaped leaves with downward-curving spines on their stalks, and leaden-blue fruits that are broader than long.

A flowering palm indigenous to southern Asia, Phoenix loureiroi grows in forests and open terrain from sea level to high elevations. Its sharply pointed leaflets form stiff, feathery leaves, while its ripe fruit is bluish-black and usually hidden within the leaf crown.

A palm native to the eastern Mediterranean, particularly the southernmost parts of Greece and Turkey, Phoenix theophrasti usually has several slender stems. Its thin, fibrous, acrid fruits are usually inedible, although local people sometimes eat them.
stories.edibilityNote: The usually inedible fruits have thin, fibrous, acrid pulp but are sometimes eaten by local people.

stories.summary: A palm native to southern Pakistan, most of India, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and Bangladesh, it bears single-seeded fruit that ripens purple-red. The fruit is made into wine and jelly, while tapped sap is drunk fresh or fermented into toddy and, in West Bengal and Bangladesh, boiled into palm jaggery.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit is made into wine and jelly; sap is drunk fresh, fermented into toddy or boiled into jaggery in West Bengal and Bangladesh.

stories.summary: A palm native to Norfolk Island and New Zealand’s Kermadec Islands, it has long feather-like leaves and bright red ripe fruit. Early Norfolk Island settlers used its growing tip as a vegetable, raw or boiled.
stories.edibilityNote: Early Norfolk Island settlers ate the growing tip as a vegetable, either raw or boiled.

stories.summary: A palm tree known from two distinct populations in the Khasia Hills of northeast India and central northern Nepal, with others reported in Assam, Sikkim, Burma and southern China. Its leaves split regularly about halfway, and its coffee-bean-shaped seeds grow above a bare rather than fibrous trunk.

A corm-forming flowering perennial native to eastern Africa from Ethiopia to Mozambique. In late summer it bears numerous fragrant white flowers with maroon, or occasionally orange, throat markings on slender nodding stems.

A flowering plant endemic to South Africa and southern Namibia, Stapelia hirsuta has grooved, roughly four-angled stems. Its flat, very hairy dark-red flowers resemble rotting meat and produce a carrion smell that attracts flies.

A rhizomatous flowering perennial native to Brazil’s tropical forests. Its striking oval leaves lie flat by day and fold upright at night, while its spreading stems root at leaf nodes and carpet the forest floor.

An evergreen broadleaf tree endemic to New Zealand. Its inconspicuous flowers are followed by dark-purple fruit; Māori traditionally ate both the flesh and kernels after lengthy steaming, washing and further preparation.
stories.edibilityNote: Māori traditionally ate the flesh and kernels; berries were steamed for two days, washed, and the dried kernels later soaked and pounded.

stories.summary: A climbing plant endemic to New Zealand, Parsonsia heterophylla has leaves whose shapes vary greatly, especially in young plants. Its usually white, scented tubular flowers grow in compact clusters and may be noticed more readily by smell than sight.

An epiphytic orchid endemic to Madagascar, it bears star-shaped, waxy flowers with remarkably long nectar spurs. The flowers release an intense spicy scent only at night and change from green to white before yellowing as they wilt.

Single-celled alga found in tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide. One of the largest known unicellular organisms, it forms a smooth, glassy bubble that can appear green, silver, teal or nearly black.

A compact evergreen shrub native to southern Argentina and Chile. It has glossy leaves, solitary white spring flowers, and showy autumn berries ranging from deep purple through pink to white; male and female plants must grow together for fruit. The ripe fruit is edible, sweet, juicy, and somewhat tasteless.
stories.edibilityNote: The ripe fruit is edible, sweet, and juicy but somewhat tasteless, and is described as useful survival food.

stories.summary: A flowering grass whose variety duriotagana is endemic to mainland Portugal and variety barbata is native there. Both varieties are protected under Portuguese or European legislation.

Evergreen perennial shrub endemic to central coastal Portugal. It grows on coastal dunes and cliffs, with many branches covered in dry leaves and flowers ranging from pink or white to sometimes purple. Flowering occurs from February to May.

A perennial plant from central and south-central Madagascar, it grows in rocky, sunny places and is the only runner-forming member of its genus. Its few, very thick fleshy leaves form terminal rosettes, and its flowers range from white through pink to purple.

A flowering plant with underground stems, native to Algeria, Greece, Turkey, western Syria and Tunisia. Its evergreen, grass-like leaves accompany fragrant pale lilac or purple flowers marked with a central yellow band. The flowers appear in winter and early spring.
Semievergreen flowering perennial native to Southern Africa and Zimbabwe. It has slender, lance-shaped leaves and spikes of red flowers, occasionally pink or white, from late summer to autumn.

A tropical herbaceous plant native to eastern Africa, from southern Kenya to northeastern South Africa. It has a succulent tuber and glossy dark-green leaves, and may shed its normally evergreen foliage during drought. All parts are poisonous if eaten.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts of the plant are poisonous if ingested.

stories.summary: A deciduous broad-leaved tree whose native origin is not stated, it is common along Himalayan lowlands from Kashmir to western Nepal. It has abundant white flowers and forms a rounded canopy. Its seeds are dried and ground into bitter flour, with the saponins thoroughly washed out before cooking.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds are dried and ground; bitter saponins are thoroughly washed out before the flour is used in chapatis, halwa or porridge.

stories.summary: A bulbous perennial native to South Africa’s eastern Cape. It has narrow, grasslike, nearly evergreen leaves and autumn clusters of slender pink flowers with crinkled petals.
A corm-forming flowering plant endemic to South Africa’s Western Cape. It grows beside waterfalls in the region’s south-western mountains.

A bulbous flowering plant native to South Africa, pregnant onion may also be native or introduced in tropical East Africa. Its largely exposed bulb produces small bulblets, while tall flower stalks carry many fragrant, green-striped white flowers; most parts are considered toxic to humans.
Flowering plant; the subspecies lowei is native only to Madeira.

A perennial succulent native to Tanzania in eastern Africa, the red dragon flower forms clumps of smooth, square green-to-reddish stems with soft tooth-like bumps. Its small, velvety crimson or burgundy flowers are funnel-shaped and notably lack the rotting-meat smell associated with many other Huernia species.

An evergreen shrub native to Korea, Japan and Taiwan. It has glossy oval leaves and scented white flowers, sometimes tinged pink, in early summer; unlike most Rhaphiolepis species, its fruits are inedible.
stories.edibilityNote: Its fruits are explicitly described as inedible.

stories.summary: A large hazel tree native to the Balkan Peninsula and western Asia, with thick, corky bark. Its small nuts have very hard shells and grow in clusters surrounded by bristly husks.
stories.edibilityNote: The nuts are edible and sometimes gathered, but are small and enclosed in very hard, thick shells.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub or small tree native to Malesia, Papuasia, the Northern Territory and Queensland. Its young twigs, leaves and flowers have dense rusty-brown hairs, while its yellow or orange capsules contain red seeds held in a sticky ball.
Aquatic fern found mostly in Australia and nearby New Caledonia. It has broad, clover-like fronds and floats in deeper freshwater than other ferns in its genus.

A small fig tree native to eastern Australia, where it grows mainly along waterways and gullies. Its leaves feel like sandpaper, while its succulent oval fruit is densely hairy and was eaten by local Aboriginal people.
stories.edibilityNote: The palatable fruit was eaten by local Aboriginal people.

stories.summary: A spreading woodland tree native to Africa south of the Zambezi River, the weeping boer-bean occurs mainly at middle altitudes. Its bright-red new leaves fade through bronze to dark green, followed by deep-red flowers that may release enough nectar to drip when shaken.

Medium-sized fruit-bearing tree native to Malesia, Australia and the Pacific Islands. Its ripe fruit is edible but tart and may be eaten raw, cooked or preserved; Indigenous Australians buried it underground to ripen.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe fruit is tart and eaten raw, cooked or preserved; Indigenous Australians buried it underground to ripen.

stories.summary: Perennial grass native to parts of Africa, Arabia and Sri Lanka. It grows in stiff, upright tufts with olive-green leaves and densely packed grey-brown flower heads. Its many seeds become sticky when wet and can attach to animals, clothing and machinery.

Small fern widespread across Australia and South Pacific islands. It grows beside streams and along rainforest margins or in other moist forests, with round spore clusters under hairy closed coverings. In Hawaii, it was first recorded as naturalised on Oahu in 1887 and now occurs on all major islands.
stories.edibilityNote: Described as an edible fern; no part or preparation is specified.

stories.summary: A rainforest and woodland tree native to Queensland and New South Wales, Australia, it produces fragrant flower clusters in spring. The cream flowers turn yellow with age and are followed by long, pear-shaped seed capsules.

A flowering plant native to the Arabian Peninsula and much of tropical and subtropical Asia, bearded knotweed is usually described as an erect or sometimes prostrate annual herb with hairless, grooved stems and lance-shaped leaves. Some descriptions instead call it a perennial growing from a creeping rootstock.

A trailing flowering plant native to Australia and Asia. Its stems begin horizontally before turning upright, and it dies back in winter but regenerates after rain. In Africa it is eaten locally during famines.
stories.edibilityNote: Eaten locally in Africa during times of famine.

stories.summary: A tropical tree whose precise native origin is unclear because people spread it early. It bears fruit containing a soft, white, oily kernel inside a hard shell. The nut is mildly toxic raw but is eaten cooked or toasted in many cultures, including in Southeast Asian curries and Hawaiian ʻinamona.
stories.edibilityNote: The nut is mildly toxic raw; cooking or toasting reduces toxicity, after which it is used in Southeast Asian and Hawaiian foods.

stories.summary: An annual or biennial plant native from South America to Mexico, tall fleabane has rather hairy stems and many small flower heads in loose, branching clusters that widen toward the top. Its ray petals are inconspicuous and sometimes tinged purple.

A small fern endemic to Australia, Adiantum atroviride occurs in the Northern Territory, Queensland and New South Wales. Its loosely clustered fronds have shiny black stalks and fan-shaped divisions with shallow lobes.

A perennial tropical grass native to African grasslands, Napier grass forms tall, robust, bamboo-like clumps. Its seeds rarely develop fully, so it usually spreads through horizontal shoots, and its young leaves and shoots are cooked in soups and stews.
stories.edibilityNote: Young leaves and shoots are edible when cooked in soups and stews.

stories.summary: A flowering plant with no explicitly stated native origin, it occurs in Spain, the Canary Islands, Algeria, Morocco, Mauritania and Cape Verde.
A plant species native to southern Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina.

An evergreen shrub or small tree native to Assam, Cambodia, China, the Himalayas, Hainan, Japan, Myanmar, Taiwan, Nepal, Thailand and Vietnam, sweet olive bears strongly fragrant white, yellow or orange-yellow flowers in late summer and autumn. In Chinese cuisine, the flowers may be infused with tea and are also used in jams, cakes, dumplings, soups, liquor and traditional desserts.
stories.edibilityNote: In Chinese cuisine, the flowers may be infused with tea and are used in jams, cakes, dumplings, soups, liquor and traditional desserts.

stories.summary: A strongly aromatic shrub native to the western Mediterranean basin, it has a more pungent, camphor-rich scent than English lavender. Pale lilac flower spikes appear from June to September, depending on the weather.

A perennial herb native to Europe and western Asia, water dock grows beside fresh or coastal waters. It is the tallest dock species, with tough flowering stems that redden with age and large, tapering leaves.
A flowering plant native to Atlantic Europe, St. Dabeoc's heath is abundant in western Ireland and has become naturalised in parts of Great Britain and the Iberian Peninsula.
A tree native to the Caucasian region. It forms a rounded crown of widely spreading branches and bears long, feather-like leaves and green winged nuts in hanging clusters.

Shrub or small tree endemic to the upper Amazon region at the eastern base of the Andes in Peru. It has large, fragrant, nodding, funnel-shaped flowers in shades of white and pink, with a very narrow, unusually long tube at the base.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub native to the Atlantic coasts of western Europe. Its green, spiny stems largely take over the work of its reduced leaves, and yellow flowers appear mainly in late summer and autumn. It can regrow from its roots after fire, while slight scorching encourages seed germination.

An upright annual clover native to mainland Portugal. It has glossy, toothed leaflets and pink flowers in small rounded heads, and grows in temporarily waterlogged pastures and meadows on siliceous ground.

sources.title: Trifolium strictum L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An annual clover native to mainland Portugal and introduced to Madeira. It grows in annual grasslands, generally on poor, dry, siliceous soils.

An annual flowering herb native across parts of Europe, western and Central Asia, and northern and eastern Africa, this sandwort has a low, spreading habit. It produces white flowers from late winter to spring.

Slender annual herb native to Eurasia and introduced into North America. Its leaves usually have three conspicuous lengthwise veins, sometimes as many as five, and its sepals are longer than its petals.
Flowering plant in the carnation family; only its robusta subspecies is explicitly described here as native to mainland Portugal.

A rhizomatous perennial grass native to southern Europe and North Africa. Its stiff, threadlike leaves are distinctive, and its strong, flexible fibres are used for ropes, sandals, baskets, mats and paper.
A short-lived coastal herb, sea stock grows on shores and new sand dunes without spreading vegetatively. It is seldom seen in the British Isles and was assessed as vulnerable in 2001.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira. It grows in abandoned fields, along roads and in cracks or at the bases of walls and rocks, especially on limestone. It has small rounded white petals and oval seedpods whose stalks eventually spread horizontally.

sources.title: Draba muralis L.
sources.attribution: Info Flora, plazi (2021). Info Flora Schweiz - Brassicaceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ahvrx3 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A mustard-family plant of unstated native origin, found mostly in the Mediterranean region. It closely resembles common shepherd's-purse and is used with Capsella grandiflora to study changes in plant reproduction.

A bulbous flowering plant native from the Balearic Islands through the Mediterranean and western Asia to Tajikistan. It retreats to its bulb in summer, then produces glossy green leaves and deep yellow flowers in autumn. The leaves remain through winter.
Epiphytic climbing plant native to India, China, Southeast Asia and Australia. It has tiny, opposite, lens-shaped leaves and often grows on tree trunks.
A moss of unspecified native origin, it has a cosmopolitan distribution.
A flowering plant of unspecified native origin, it is recorded as introduced in the Azores.

An orchid whose lineage derives from Europe or North Africa, it likely reached the Azores in a single seed migration from mainland Europe. It has exceptionally large flowers compared with the other two Azorean butterfly orchids. Exceptionally rare, it was known from one small upland area of São Jorge when rediscovered, with a flowering specimen later found on Faial.

Orchid endemic to the Azores, where it survives in small, scattered populations in laurisilva scrub across eight islands. This endangered species is a strong indicator of the islands’ remaining semi-natural laurisilva habitats.
A sea-lavender native only to central-western Portugal, where it grows on coastal cliffs and in rocky or sandy places. Its flowers have purplish-red petals.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Limonium multiflorum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A waterwort-family plant distributed across Europe and North Africa, it is also recorded in Turkey’s Çanakkale Province. In Portugal it is confined to the far northeast, where it inhabits small permanent ponds and slow-flowing streams and is assessed as Vulnerable.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Elatine alsinastrum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Flowering plant occurring in North Africa and southwestern Europe. Its two recorded mainland Portuguese subspecies are endemic there: one occurs in west-central Portugal, while the Sintra Mountains subspecies is protected under the Habitats Directive.
Green alga that prefers nutrient-rich environments.

A green seaweed with no native origin specified, thread weed is widespread in the Atlantic and Pacific and lives along coasts from exposed shores to sheltered shallows, tide pools, rocks and sand. It is eaten by humans and animals and is widely produced in China, Japan and Korea.
stories.edibilityNote: The seaweed is edible and widely produced in China, Japan and Korea.

stories.summary: True ginger native to Maritime Southeast Asia. Its beehive-like flower spikes have white, yellow, orange or red bracts that often darken as they mature, surrounding small purple-and-yellow flowers with a papery texture.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in summer-developing meadows on waterlogged or sandy ground beside reservoirs and watercourses, sometimes occupying disturbed areas that flood temporarily.
A herbaceous perennial native to China, Japan, Korea and Siberia, it grows from a short rhizome. At least two varieties are recognized.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in nutrient-enriched meadows beside or within clearings of open pine and holm-oak woods, as well as along roadsides, on lime-rich marl or sandy ground.
A perennial herb, Brazilian woodsorrel has a very long, simple root and tiny stems. Its flowers are yellow or vivid crimson-purple.

An evergreen shrub native to coastal dunes and hills in South Africa’s Western, Eastern and Northern Cape. Its paired, parrot-beak-shaped flowers open bright yellow, turn rusty, and leave dark rusty calyxes that persist after fruiting begins.

An alga widespread in tropical and subtropical regions that infects many trees and shrubs. It typically forms fuzzy, orange-brown spots on leaves and thrives in warm, humid conditions; severe infections can damage foliage and fruit.

A fern found in Australia and New Zealand, the giant maidenhair has striking black stems and triangular fronds divided into rectangular segments. Its underground stem grows unusually deep in the soil.

Evergreen succulent subshrub native and endemic to Gran Canaria. It usually carries a large glossy green rosette on a single unbranched stem, with new rosettes growing from the base. The flowering stem normally dies after producing its yellow flower cluster, usually after about five years.
Flowering succulent endemic to Tenerife in the Canary Islands. It is confined to the island’s north, from Teno Point to the Anaga Peninsula.
Annual herb native to southern Europe, North Africa and the Canary Islands. It is a small, self-supporting grass with simple, broad leaves and has been introduced to Australia.
A flowering plant native to northern Africa and many parts of Europe. It is naturalized in parts of Asia, Africa and Europe.

A large flowering megaherb endemic to New Zealand's subantarctic Auckland and Campbell Islands, Ross lily has fleshy, strap-like dark-green leaves and densely crowded golden-yellow flowers. It favours cold, wet ground and is classified as At Risk—Naturally Uncommon because its range is confined to those island groups.

A flowering sedge occurring across Europe, Central Asia, West Siberia and Xinjiang, China. It favours lowland wetlands on heavy soils near lakes, rivers, reservoirs and coasts, and bears pale-green or orange-brown fruiting structures.

A tussock-forming perennial sedge native to Macaronesia, northwest Africa, much of Europe and Turkey. Its lowest leaf-like bract extends beyond the flower cluster, and its flower spikes appear from March to May. It favours sheltered sea-cliff crevices, salt marshes and coastal river mouths.

A sedge found across Europe and Western and Central Asia, with isolated occurrences in North Africa, greater pond-sedge grows in wet habitats and can dominate swamps. It is Britain’s largest Carex and has glaucous leaves; its closely grouped male spikes help distinguish it from lesser pond-sedge.
An evergreen shrub native to South Africa, it grows 0.7–1.3 metres tall and occurs at elevations of 300–1,400 metres.

An annual succulent herb native to the Mediterranean basin. It produces white flowers during Southern Hemisphere spring, from August to October, and is now also found in southern Australia and New Zealand.

A creeping succulent native to eastern and southern Africa, ranging from Kenya and Angola to South Africa. Its small, faintly toothed leaves have barely visible or absent stalks, while pink-white star-shaped flowers appear in late summer or autumn.

A creeping succulent ground cover indigenous to South Africa’s Eastern Cape, Crassula spathulata grows among leaf litter on rocky ridges, often near forest edges. It has stalked, spoon-shaped leaves with rounded bumps along their edges and tiny pink-white, star-shaped autumn flowers.

A perennial succulent native to southern Africa, particularly the east coast of South Africa. Its long branches trail, climb or hang from rocks and form mats, bearing green or yellow-green leaves often edged red and white or cream star-shaped flowers from winter into spring.

A succulent evergreen subshrub endemic to Southern Africa. It has thick, greyish-teal, sickle-shaped leaves, often marked red and arranged in opposing rows. Dense clusters of brilliant scarlet, pink or nearly white tubular flowers appear in summer.
A sedge native to southern Africa, ranging from Mozambique and Zambia to South Africa.
Bulbous flowering plant originating in South Africa’s Cape Province. Its cultivars flower in late summer or early autumn, most often in bright red, orange or yellow, but occasionally pink or white.
An epiphytic fern native to Japan and eastern Asia. It is deciduous, with brown-scaled rhizomes and finely divided, flat triangular fronds.
An evergreen fern native to Australia and New Zealand. Its fertile fronds form upright clusters, and it has been introduced to the Azores, Madeira and Sri Lanka.
Evergreen shrub or small tree native to Brazil and Uruguay. It has shiny dark-green leaves and pure white flowers that open from tubes and spread in summer.

A tall tree native to Victoria and eastern New South Wales, growing in cool, wet forests and rainforest margins. It has smooth pale bark shed in long ribbons, glossy lance-shaped adult leaves, white flowers and woody cup-shaped to cylindrical fruit.

Deciduous bulbous perennial endemic to South Africa's eastern Cape Provinces and KwaZulu-Natal. Its summer flower spike ranges from white to purple, is topped by leafy bracts like a miniature pineapple, and in most plants has a coconut-like scent.
Climbing, twining flowering plant native to Central Asia. Its dense white or greenish flower clusters develop red floral parts as glossy black fruits form.

sources.title: Fallopia aubertii (L.Henry) Holub
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and assessed as native in Hungary. It inhabits wet meadows, rush beds, marshes and the edges of wetlands and waterways. Easily confused with marsh bedstraw, it is best distinguished when its diagnostic fruits are ripe.

sources.title: Galium debile Desv.
sources.attribution: Raab-Straube E V, Raus T, felipe (2024). Euro + Med-Checklist Notulae, 17. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/g5r5d9 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Flowering plant whose native origin is not supplied. In Portugal it inhabits wet meadows on sandy soil near the coast.

A small evergreen tree indigenous to Southern Africa, it has glossy foliage on arching, drooping branches. Its orange or purple flowers and fleshy fruit grow directly from the trunk; the fruit is edible but reportedly not very tasty.
stories.edibilityNote: The small, fleshy fruits are edible but reportedly do not taste particularly good.

stories.summary: A hairy perennial flowering plant native to Europe and northern Asia. It forms basal leaf rosettes and solitary lemon-yellow flower heads, while runners can produce new rosettes and dense mats.

An evergreen tree or shrub endemic to New Zealand, narrow-leaved lacebark has a weeping form. Young plants have dense, interlacing branches and small leaves; adults develop narrow, coarsely toothed leaves and bear white flowers from December to February.
A flowering plant native to Eurasia and Morocco in North Africa, it has five-petalled flowers that appear from July to August.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira. It grows in scrub clearings on poor, acidic soils. Downward-rolled leaf margins are reported as a feature needing confirmation.

An evergreen perennial flowering plant from tropical Africa, Congo cockatoo grows in moist, shaded bushland from Cameroon across tropical Africa to Sudan and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Its bright bird-shaped flowers have long curled nectar spurs; the commonly cultivated ‘African Princess’ clone usually has scarlet-and-yellow flowers.

A deciduous, spreading shrub native to China and Japan. It bears compound dark-green leaves and clusters of light pink or purple, pea-like flowers in summer. Although mainly ornamental, it has also been used to make indigo dye.
A compact succulent shrub native to South Africa. It bears masses of orange to yellow flowers from August to October; the flowers open fully in sunlight.
A flowering plant native to South Africa’s Cape Provinces. This trailing iceplant is sold both in its wild form and as numerous cultivated varieties.

A flowering mint-family plant found across eastern Africa from Sudan to South Africa. It is reasonably resistant to drought and wind, and its bold tubular flowers are larger than those of the similar Leonotis leonurus.

An upright herbaceous perennial occurring across Eurasia, mostly Europe, and North America, this oxeye daisy grows in meadows, along forest edges and roads, and in urban areas. Its conspicuous flower heads combine whitish outer florets with numerous tiny yellow central florets and appear from May to October.

An evergreen shrub native to South Africa and Eswatini, it has glossy dark-green leaves with wavy edges. Profuse pale lilac to lavender, trumpet-shaped flowers marked by deep purple veins appear in spring and early summer.

An ornamental vine native to southern Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia and northern Argentina, Chilean jasmine produces masses of strongly scented white flowers in summer. It becomes deciduous in cool climates and cannot survive freezing.

A perennial grass found across the Mediterranean Basin from Portugal and Morocco to the eastern Mediterranean, it has slender stems and open, nodding flower heads. Their spreading branches carry 7–30 fertile flowering units.

A fern indigenous to the Hawaiian Islands and native across other tropical and subtropical areas, including India and Malaysia. Its coarse, light- to medium-green fronds can exceed three feet, and early Hawaiians used them for hula altars and leis.
stories.edibilityNote: Early Hawaiians reportedly fed young fronds to babies, but the passage does not identify this as food or medicine.

stories.summary: A flowering plant in the borage family, native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant recorded in North and South America. It occurs on coastal dunes and sandy shores, cultivated land and market gardens, and around settlements.

sources.title: Oenothera indecora Cambess.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub or small tree native to eastern Asia, specifically central and southern Japan and Taiwan, holly olive bears very fragrant white flowers in autumn. Spiny leaves predominate on young plants, while unspined leaves predominate higher on mature plants; dark purple fruit ripens the following summer.

Evergreen flowering shrub or small tree native to southern Africa, from South Africa and Lesotho to Mozambique and Zimbabwe. It has showy bright yellow flowers and berry-like fruits that darken to brown or black around a pale, bone-coloured seed. Most varieties have woolly, dull, toothed oval leaves, while the rotundatum variety has glossy, round leaves.

A succulent subshrub native to the Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, Norfolk Island, the southwestern Pacific and warmer parts of New Zealand, where its South Island range is limited to specified northwestern areas. It grows on forest floors and occasionally as a low trunk epiphyte.
Flowering plant native to South Africa and Eswatini. Its foliage resembles that of Coleus; the ornamental cultivar ‘Easy Gold’ is especially noted for this feature.
A flowering grass native to Portugal's Madeira Archipelago.

A perennial native to the Himalayas, Assam, Myanmar, and south-central and southeastern China. It usually has purple flowers, though red, white and bright-pink forms occur, together with hairy, pale-green leaves.

An erect annual or short-lived perennial herb native to Australia; its status in parts of New Zealand is uncertain. It has a bristly main stem, narrow lobed lower leaves and many small yellow or pale-yellow flower heads.

A perennial flowering herb native to central and eastern Russia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia and northwestern China, Maltese-cross has unbranched stems and opposite leaves. It bears clusters of bright red flowers with deeply cleft lobes forming a Maltese-cross shape; cultivated varieties may instead be orange-red, pink or white.
A flowering plant native to Algeria, Morocco, Portugal, Spain and Tunisia. It mainly grows in subtropical regions and was introduced to Corsica in 1967.
A bulb-forming perennial native to Cape Province in South Africa. It bears white to cream flowers and grows in sandy, waterlogged soils.

Flowering shrub native to southern Africa, with sticky, aromatic, heart-shaped leaves that smell of ginger when crushed. Its abundant white, lilac or pink flowers form large clusters at the ends of otherwise bare branches in winter in subtropical or temperate climates.
Perennial climbing vine native across South and Southeast Asia. It has tuberous roots and produces red tubular flowers from January to April.

A flowering plant native to an area extending from southeastern Brazil to northeastern Argentina. Its pink-tipped white flowers and green-purple foliage make it attractive to gardeners, but it can become invasive where grown as an ornamental.
A tuber-growing plant native to the south-southwestern and southern Cape Provinces. It grows mainly in subtropical environments.

sources.title: Tritonia crocata (L.) Ker Gawl. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A flowering plant whose native origin is not given, the spotted calla lily has slender, pointed leaves attractively speckled with white. Its flowers have a white, funnel-shaped outer part surrounding a yellowish centre.
A flowering parasitic plant found in Madeira, where it is introduced. It attacks various herbs and shrubs in dry, sunny, low-altitude sites.

A small to medium-sized tree endemic to New South Wales, Australia. It has thick, rough fibrous bark, narrow greyish-green adult leaves, white flowers and small woody fruit; fewer than 40 localities are known.
An evergreen shrub or small tree endemic to New Zealand. It commonly grows on another plant and sends grooved roots toward the forest floor, and it has large, thick, glossy leaves.

A moss of unstated native origin, recorded across Europe, Asia, the Americas, Africa, Australia and Antarctica. It forms loose brown-green mats; dry shoots look dark brown and bud-like, while wet upper leaves spread into rosettes. In Europe only female plants have been found, and spore capsules are known only from Australia, Tasmania and New Zealand.

A herbaceous perennial endemic to New Zealand, naturally occurring near the sea on rocks north of Greymouth and Kaikōura. Its tall flower stalk bears many white flowers with purple, white and yellow stamens. Māori historically ate its rhizomes after cooking them in a hāngī.
stories.edibilityNote: Rhizomes are edible when cooked and were historically cooked in a hāngī and eaten by Māori.

stories.summary: A shrub endemic to New Zealand, shrubby tororaro has small, heart-shaped leaves among wiry, interlocking branches. It is usually leafless in winter and forms a dense, tangled shape.

Perennial or biennial plant endemic to Europe, though absent from Finland and Eastern Europe, with small populations in European Turkey and Svalbard. Young plants form ground-level rosettes before producing taller shoots bearing many bright yellow flower heads, typically in damp, grazed or disturbed grassland.
An evergreen or semi-evergreen shrub native to East Asia. Its flowers range from white to dark red, and some varieties are poisonous because they contain grayanotoxin.

Herbaceous perennial native to Chile and Argentina, with brittle, fleshy roots and erect, narrow-leaved stems. Its orchid-like yellow or orange flowers appear in early to midsummer and may be heavily spotted or striped with red or brown.

A bulbous plant native to South Africa, this frost-resistant evergreen perennial grows in the Drakensberg grasslands. Its rust-coloured stems carry cream to coral-pink flowers that turn yellow from late summer into mid-autumn, above narrow blue-green leaves.
A cactus native to Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, it can form more than 100 jointed stem segments. It is considered invasive in Africa and Australia.

A woody climbing vine native to woodlands in Japan, the Korean peninsula and Sakhalin. It climbs with small aerial roots and produces flat summer flower clusters with peripheral sterile white flowers around numerous fertile off-white flowers. Its young leaves are edible when cooked and are sometimes added to miso in Japan.
stories.edibilityNote: Young leaves are eaten cooked, sometimes in Japanese miso, and are described as tasting like cucumber.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to New Zealand’s Chatham Islands. It is grown as a garden tree and used for firewood, including in other mild oceanic climates such as Scotland.

A large upright shrub or small tree native to South Africa, the oleander-leaf protea has green or blue-grey leaves that curve upward directly from its stems. Its cone-like flower heads have pink, carmine, creamy-green or whitish outer bracts, typically edged with a distinctive hairy black fringe.
A flowering shrub or small tree found from the central Himalayas to northern Indo-China. It has pointed, ribbed leaves and clusters of fragrant, pale pink flowers in autumn and winter.
Bromeliad endemic to southern Brazil, commonly grown as an ornamental plant. Recognized varieties occur from São Paulo south to Rio Grande do Sul, with one reported specifically from Santa Catarina.
A flowering bromeliad native to the Atlantic Forest of southern Brazil and Misiones province in eastern Argentina.
A succulent perennial endemic to eastern Australia, the giant spear lily forms a rosette of long, sword-shaped leaves. In spring, its flowers rise on a very tall stalk.

A low-growing evergreen shrub native to China, Afghanistan, northeastern India, Bhutan and Nepal. It bears fragrant white flowers throughout winter, followed by black berries; its varieties can differ greatly in appearance.

A deciduous flowering shrub native to northeastern Asia. Its three-lobed, maple-like leaves often turn red in autumn; flat white flower heads appear in early summer, followed by round red berries in autumn.

An evergreen shrub found in the high Andean Yungas valleys of western South America, it bears clusters of brilliant pink, narrow tubular flowers in early spring. It is Peru’s national flower and one of Bolivia’s two national flowers.

Evergreen flowering shrub native to Nepal, the eastern Himalaya, Assam, Myanmar, Vietnam, Tibet, and central and southern China, but not Taiwan. Its leaves emerge red in early spring before turning green, while clusters of creamy-white flowers open alongside the young leaves.

An evergreen terrestrial bromeliad endemic to central Chile. It forms dense rosettes of grey-green leaves armed with hooked spines, while its green or yellow flower spikes resemble medieval maces. Growth is slow, and flowering may take 20 years or more.
Bromeliad native to Brazil, northern Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay. It is typical of Brazil’s Cerrado vegetation and is often grown as an ornamental.

Deciduous tree native to the Caucasus, Kaçkar and Alborz mountains of eastern Europe and southwest Asia. It has a distinctive vase-shaped crown, with a short, broad trunk splitting low into many nearly upright branches, and small greenish flowers without petals.

An evergreen subshrub native to Argentina and Chile, bush slipperwort has highly veined, slightly sticky, puckered leaves. Clusters of lemon-yellow, snapdragon-shaped flowers appear throughout spring and summer.

Groundcover violet native to Australia's east coast from near Brisbane to Batemans Bay. It has striking purple-and-white flowers and bright-green, nearly circular mature leaves with a deep, narrow V-shaped notch at the base.

A bulbous perennial native to Southern Africa, it grows across the region’s winter-rainfall zone in fynbos and renosterveld. Its red flower heads appear before the broad, strap-shaped leaves and are followed by translucent white-to-red fleshy berries.

A large evergreen shrub native to Tibet and south-central China, late cotoneaster bears clusters of white flowers followed by masses of small red fruit in autumn. Birds unusually avoid the fruit, which can remain on the plant through winter.

A compact evergreen shrub reported native to Ireland, southwestern France, Spain, Portugal and Tangier, though its isolated Irish occurrence may be a garden escape. Its brittle foliage stays green, and deep pink, honey-scented flowers open in winter and spring.

Tree or shrub native to French Polynesia, the Cook Islands and the Pitcairn Islands. It commonly forms part of the canopy in montane and cloud forests, sometimes becoming a shrub on windswept mountaintops.

A spreading shrub or tree endemic to New Zealand, rawirinui is widespread on the North and South Islands, mainly near coasts, lowlands and forest margins. Its rough bark peels upward in long strips, and its small white flowers form compact groups.
Perennial cactus native to Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina. It has fleshy, cylindrical, trailing stems and white flowers.
A shrub endemic to southeastern Australia. Its gland-dotted, oblong to egg-shaped leaves accompany white to pink flowers borne singly or in small groups from the leaf axils.

A perennial herb endemic to the western Mediterranean Basin. Its saxophone-shaped flowers lure small flies, temporarily trapping them before releasing them with pollen. Long-term consumption of its roots or rhizomes can cause irreversible kidney damage, and their aristolochic acids may be carcinogenic when taken internally.
stories.edibilityNote: Roots or rhizomes consumed over long periods can cause irreversible kidney damage; internal aristolochic acids may be carcinogenic.

stories.summary: Plant species in the nettle family; its native origin is not specified.

A large deciduous tree common on the plains and lower hills of South and Southeast Asia. Its leaves crowd toward branch tips, and its rounded nuts have five flatter sides. The kernels are eaten by the Lodha people of the Indian subcontinent for their mind-altering qualities.
stories.edibilityNote: The Lodha people of the Indian subcontinent eat the kernels for their mind-altering qualities.

stories.summary: Flowering bromeliad native to Brazil. Its robust, sharp-edged leaves form a vase-like rosette whose funnels often collect water. It bears long-lasting flower heads with striking pink bracts and blue petals that turn red and white as they wilt.

An erect shrub or small tree native to the southwest coast of Western Australia, it has prominent red-and-white flower spikes, mainly in spring. Fire kills the plant but opens seed-storing pods, allowing it to regenerate from seed.
A slowly spreading evergreen perennial native to northern Iran. It has oval, hairy leaves and bright yellow, spurred flowers in late spring and early summer.

Flowering plant in the rose family endemic to southwestern continental Europe. In Portugal it occurs only in rocky habitats above 1,800 metres on Serra da Estrela’s upper plateau; a 2020 mainland assessment classified it as Critically Endangered there.

stories.summary: A deciduous shrub native to China and Japan, it bears yellow flowers marked with dark red flecks. Though rarely cultivated, it is a parent of many yellow-flowered hybrids.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows along the edges and in clearings of deciduous woodland, and also colonizes roadside banks and rocky outcrops in forest settings. It is protected under Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.

A prickly shrub native to eastern New South Wales and southeastern Queensland, Australia. Its crowded, stiff leaves accompany spider-like flower heads in red, pink, orange, yellow or greenish shades. Bushfires kill the plants, which regenerate afterward from seed.
An annual or biennial herb native to parts of Europe and western Asia. It grows in grassland, disturbed ground and roadsides, and its tough taproot can make it difficult to remove from gardens.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves and seeds are eaten in salads; the source also records use as famine food.

stories.summary: A cactus native to central and eastern Brazil. It develops a woody trunk and large crown, while its white flowers open at dusk and last only one night.

Rainforest tree native to eastern Australia, where it grows along streams from New South Wales to central eastern Queensland. It has thin, wavy-edged leaves and produces white summer flowers followed by pale pink or greenish berries.
A shrub endemic to South Africa, it has grey to bluish-green leaves with hard margins. Its woody fruits remain on the plant, and seeds are released from dry flower heads after wildfire.

A perennial herb native to Europe and North Africa, including most Mediterranean islands. Its basal, round-toothed leaves accompany one or two scented yellow flowers, which appear from October to December and may cover large areas.

An evergreen twining vine native to the Portuguese island of Madeira. Deep pink buds open into fragrant, white, star-shaped summer flowers, and the species is critically endangered in its native range.

An evergreen shrub or tree with aromatic, glossy dark-green leaves, native to Madeira and the Canary Islands. It grows in humid cloud-zone forests and bears male and female flowers on separate plants.

A flowering plant introduced in mainland Portugal, the Azores and Madeira; its native origin is not stated. It is naturalized in fields and dunes, especially disturbed coastal sites with sandy, nitrogen-enriched soil.

An evergreen succulent vine native to South Africa, Eswatini and Zimbabwe, it trails for several metres and bears heart-shaped leaves. Older plants develop a woody base, while tubers often form on the roots and sometimes along the stems, creating its rosary-like appearance.
An evergreen shrub native to Madeira. It is rare there, growing on exposed coastal and inland rocky slopes, and has separate male and female plants with similar flower clusters.
A fern native to Madeira, where it grows in subtropical moist lowland forest. It is threatened by habitat loss.
Flowering plant endemic to Madeira, Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation, including the Habitats Directive and the Convention on European Wildlife and Natural Habitats.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira, Sedum brissemoretii grows on the island’s coastal sea cliffs. It is protected under Annex II of the Habitats Directive.
Flowering plant endemic to Madeira and belonging to the mustard family.
A flowering plant in the mustard family, Sinapidendron frutescens has two listed subspecies, both endemic to Madeira.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal's Madeira archipelago. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation, including Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira, Portugal, Sinapidendron gymnocalyx belongs to the mustard family.
A rowan species endemic to Madeira, Sorbus maderensis is threatened by habitat loss.
Flowering plant endemic to Portugal's Madeira Archipelago.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Chaenorhinum serpyllifolium subsp. lusitanicum is endemic to mainland Portugal. That subspecies is protected under Portuguese and European Union law.

Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and Portugal's Berlengas archipelago, growing in dry fields, paths and disturbed ground. The Iberian subspecies is annual, while the Berlengas subspecies is described as biannual or perennial; both have highly branched stems and dense flower clusters.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows on coastal sands, mainly primary dunes and openings in secondary-dune scrub, including somewhat disturbed sites.
A prostrate to ascending perennial herb endemic to eastern Australia, white fanflower has pale blue or white fan-shaped flowers and bright green, slightly hairy leaves with smooth or toothed edges.
Shrub or tree endemic to Madagascar, it is widespread across the island. It grows in habitats ranging from humid coastal and lowland forests to dry deciduous and montane forests.
An orchid occurring in southern Brazil, northeastern Argentina and Paraguay, and reported from eastern Peru.

Terrestrial slipper orchid native to the Khasi Hills of Assam and Meghalaya and adjoining Sylhet in Bangladesh, where it may now be extinct; it is also reported from northwest Yunnan. It bears one large, variably coloured flower with a helmet-shaped lip and is very rare in the wild.
A succulent plant native to South Africa, it is also known as the pickle plant.
Succulent endemic to South Africa’s southern Cape Provinces around Makhanda. It forms clumps of fleshy triangular leaves and produces yellow, daisy-like flowers in autumn.
A perennial herb of unspecified native origin, it is recorded in Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Paraguay, Bolivia and Brazil. It is grown in gardens for its flowers and blooms profusely in late summer.
A rare annual flowering plant endemic to southern Portugal, especially inland Alentejo. It has thick, linear leaves with slightly curled tips and small violet flowers, blooming from February to June.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A mustard-family flowering plant endemic to the central and northern mountains of mainland Portugal, it grows in rock cracks, cliffs and path embankments, mainly on siliceous rock such as schist.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it has a very restricted mainland Portuguese range in the Algarve between Algoz and Faro. It grows in sparse grassland on iron-rich clay soils that flood temporarily in winter and early spring, and its Portuguese population is assessed as Endangered amid continuing habitat and population decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Plantago algarbiensis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Coastal plant endemic to southwestern mainland Portugal, growing on consolidated sandy cliff soils with some iron and surface moisture. In the 2016–2019 assessment, only three subpopulations were known, two created by reintroduction at historical sites, while habitat and population declines continued.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Plantago almogravensis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal, Silene rothmaleri is protected as a priority species under European habitat and wildlife agreements.

A flowering subshrub endemic to southwest Portugal, especially coastal heath and scrub on stabilized limestone-sand dunes. It has pink or purple flowers, often pale pink or reddish bracts, and leaves densely dotted with yellowish glands.

A flowering plant endemic to central Algarve in southern Portugal. It grows both on the coast, in pine clearings and dry scrub on sandy acidic ground, and inland, in thyme vegetation and scrub clearings on marginal or calcareous ground.
A small epiphytic orchid found in Madagascar’s humid evergreen forests. It has leathery, wavy-edged leaves and produces hanging clusters of large pure-white flowers that open successively in autumn.

A flowering plant endemic to southwestern Portugal between Setúbal and Sines. It grows in scrub on stabilized dunes, sometimes beneath pine forests, and can become abundant in disturbed areas with acidic sandy soil.

A robust perennial herb endemic to mainland Portugal, restricted to fragmented populations in the country's west. It grows in heath, gorse scrub and pinewoods on somewhat moist sandy soils, and was assessed as Vulnerable for mainland Portugal during 2016–2019 amid continuing decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Rhaponticum longifolium
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An aquatic flowering plant native to the Azores. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment found its historical distribution uncertain because of repeated confusion with a similar species; it was then known only from Algarve and Baixo Alentejo and assessed as Vulnerable.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Potamogeton schweinfurthii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A dandelion endemic to Portugal's Monchique range. Its current presence is known only around Foia, and the mainland Portuguese assessment classifies it as Vulnerable because of its very small occupied area and single known location.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Taraxacum triforme
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Plant endemic to southwestern mainland Portugal, growing in scrub clearings on sandy soils. Its current distribution and population are highly uncertain because it has repeatedly been confused with a close relative; seven locations are identified, and suitable habitat has declined in recent decades.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Klasea algarbiensis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Flowering plant native to Portugal, Spain and France. Its 'Grace Ward' and 'Heavenly Blue' cultivars have received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

A flowering shrub or small tree native to northern Vietnam, southern China, Hainan, Taiwan, the Ryukyu Islands and southern Kyushu. It is grown in hedges, containers and bonsai, and serves as a street tree in several southern Chinese cities.

A flowering plant endemic to southern mainland Portugal and restricted to the Algarve’s Barrocal. It grows along edges and clearings of lime-loving scrub and was assessed as Vulnerable in the 2020 mainland Portugal Red List, with only six or seven current locations identified.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Centaurea occasus
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A shrub endemic to Cape Verde, where it grows on rocky ground and escarpments across several climate zones. It has milky sap, elliptical leaves arranged in rosettes and yellow flowers.
A flowering plant native to Southern Africa, Ceropegia linearis has received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

A tree native to Indochina, southern India and parts of Malesia, sea fig can begin life growing on another plant and later develop a strangling habit. This is not obligatory, and it also grows as a single-stemmed forest tree.
A climbing shrub widespread in South-East Asia and Australoceania, Salacia chinensis has yellow or yellowish-green flowers with five petals. Its fruit contains a single seed.

Tree-like aloe indigenous to southern Africa. Its thin, recurved pale-green leaves form a distinctive spiral and have many small pink-white marginal teeth; its cone-shaped flower clusters are pink or dull scarlet.

A flowering plant endemic to central Portugal, it inhabits scrub clearings on rocky slopes exposed to Atlantic influence. During mainland Portugal's 2016–2019 assessment, it was classed as Endangered, with an estimated 350–370 mature plants and uncertainty over whether two historical populations had disappeared.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Arabis beirana
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Stemless thistle endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in scrub clearings and traditional dry olive groves on basic, non-calcareous soils. A 2016–2019 mainland Portuguese assessment classified it as Vulnerable, with most populations small and isolated and intensive irrigated olive farming its gravest threat.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Cynara tournefortii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Cynara algarbiensis occurs in southern Portugal and southwestern Spain. It belongs to the artichoke genus.

Perennial grass native to Australia, New Zealand, New Caledonia and Tonga. Its horizontal runners spread across coastal dunes and bind loose sand. Mature female seed heads detach and roll like tumbleweeds.

Evergreen shrub from the southern mountains and coastal provinces of South Africa. Its lower branches are uniquely covered in pustules, while its wedge-shaped leaves and yellow flower heads that turn orange create a pincushion effect with their long projecting styles. After fire kills the growth above ground, multiple branches can sprout from its woody rootstock.

A flowering plant native to Central and South America, the friendship plant is bushy and trailing, with bright green, quilted leaves that often have bronze or reddish undersides. Its small pink-white flowers appear infrequently indoors, and it is primarily grown as a houseplant.

A shrub or tree from southern Africa, mainly South Africa and neighbouring countries. Usually evergreen, it grows as a shrub in dry areas but can become a tree where water is sufficient. Its leathery brown pods contain smooth seeds, each bearing a yellowish cup-shaped covering.
stories.edibilityNote: The seeds are edible; no preparation or historical context is given.

stories.summary: A rainforest plant native to Brazil. Commonly grown indoors in temperate climates, it is valued for striking variegated leaves with purple undersides. Outdoors it suits humid tropical conditions but needs afternoon shade and protection from high winds.

A climbing plant native to Southeast Asia, including southern China, mainland Indochina and Java, heart hoya has thick, heart-shaped leaves. Mature plants bear clusters of flowers that produce red-to-brown nectar droplets and release their scent at night.
Bulb-forming perennial native to the Caribbean islands and northern South America. It bears striking white flowers in clusters, with narrow flower parts that usually droop while blooming.

A terrestrial orchid native to humid forests of southern China, northeastern India, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia and Myanmar. Its velvety wine-red to dark-green leaves are striped, with pink undersides, while annual late-winter to early-spring spikes carry many small white flowers.
