A cereal hybrid of wheat and rye, first bred in laboratories in late-19th-century Scotland and Germany. It combines wheat's yield and grain quality with rye's tolerance of disease and difficult growing conditions. Although grown mainly for animal feed, its grain is also used in some breakfast cereals and other foods.
stories.edibilityNote: The grain is used less often for human food than animal feed; products include breakfast cereals and foods sold in health-food shops.

stories.summary: A flowering-plant genus native to western and southwestern Europe and Morocco. It contains only one species, Trocdaris verticillata.

A genus of tropical and subtropical woody flowering plants whose ten species range from southeastern Mexico through Central America to northwestern South America and several Caribbean islands. Some species are grown for their ornamental flowers.

A natural pitcher-plant hybrid known only from Mount Kinabalu and nearby Mount Tambuyukon on Borneo. Its pitchers vary from yellow to scarlet and combine features of both parents, with raised inner ribs ending in elongated teeth.
A shrubby hybrid of unstated native origin, arising between Cistus albidus and Cistus crispus. It has grey-green leaves and pink to purple flowers.

A semideciduous hybrid tree arising naturally in southwestern Europe where its parents, Turkey oak and cork oak, occur together. Named cultivars are widely grown in gardens, parks and tree collections.

An evergreen hybrid subshrub of unstated native origin, derived from Pavonia makoyana and Pavonia multiflora. Its unusual purple-grey flowers sit within bright red outer floral structures and appear in late summer.
A cactus genus native to Bolivia and Argentina. Its plants are usually solitary, with rounded to oblong stems and flowers ranging from golden yellow and orange to reddish yellow near the stem tips.

A group of hybrid evergreen shrubs first bred in Cornwall from Camellia saluenensis and Camellia japonica, with no wild native origin stated. The group flowers abundantly, and nearly all crosses have translucent petals; some varieties bloom for several months.

An artificial flowering-plant hybrid of unstated geographic origin, derived from Begonia socotrana and the hybrid Begonia × tuberhybrida. It typically has doubled flowers in every colour except blue and can bloom through autumn and winter, sometimes nearly year-round.

A genus of flowering plants native across Southeast Asia, the Indian Subcontinent, southern China, Tibet, Taiwan, Japan, Papuasia and Australia. Its members commonly range from scrambling subshrubs to small trees, with many growing on other plants or as vines.

A naturally occurring terrestrial orchid hybrid distributed in Sardinia and Mallorca, in moist, partly shaded woodland. It flowers early in March and has a large dark brown, sometimes nearly black, lip marked centrally with a silver H and edged with lighter velvety hairs.
A flowering-plant species native to western and southwestern Europe and Morocco. It is the sole species in the genus Trocdaris.

A perennial succulent hybrid developed in France, it forms basal offsets and may have little or no stem. Its blue-green, paddle-shaped leaves develop orange or pink edges in strong sunlight, while numerous small flowers are bright yellow and pink.

A thorny citrus hybrid probably originating in India, it bears irregular fruit with orange flesh and peel at maturity. Its abundant juice is very acidic and used for seasoning or drinks, while the aromatic leaves are also used as seasoning.
stories.edibilityNote: The acidic juice is used for seasoning and drinks; the aromatic leaves are also used as seasoning.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub or small tree native mainly to highland Colombia, southern Brazil and northeastern Uruguay, and also found in eastern Paraguay and northern Argentina. Its green autumn fruit has juicy, sweet-tart, strongly aromatic flesh; the edible pulp is commonly scooped from the halved fruit, and the flower petals are edible too.
stories.edibilityNote: The skin and flower petals are edible; fruit pulp is eaten raw and used in desserts or salads.

stories.summary: A deciduous large shrub or small tree native to the southeastern Balkans, Asia Minor, the Caucasus, Crimea and northern Iran, and possibly Turkmenistan. Its reddish-brown fruit becomes edible after frost or storage softens it through “bletting,” producing wrinkled dark skin and an interior resembling apple sauce.
stories.edibilityNote: Bletted fruit is eaten raw, sometimes with sugar and cream, or made into jelly and medlar cheese.

stories.summary: An annual legume domesticated in the Fertile Crescent of the Near East, it is grown for its edible, lens-shaped seeds. The pods usually contain two seeds, which are eaten worldwide, especially in soups, stews and thick curries such as dal.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds are commonly boiled for soups, stews and curries, but may also be soaked, sprouted, fried or baked.

stories.summary: An artificial perennial aquatic hybrid naturalised in Indian lakes in Meghalaya and Jammu and Kashmir, it grows from a horizontal underground stem. Its unmottled leaves are bronze when young, and it produces small red flowers but is sterile.
A commonly cultivated aloe hybrid probably developed in Europe from cultivated plants, rather than arising in its South African parents’ wild habitat. It has become naturalised in parts of Portugal.

A section of grasses native mainly to Atlantic coasts in Europe, Africa, the Americas and southern Atlantic islands, with limited occurrences on western North American coasts and inland American freshwater habitats. Its species often form large, dense, fast-growing colonies in coastal salt marshes, and many can hybridise when they meet.

An artificial perennial aquatic hybrid naturalised in Australia, New Zealand, North America and Europe, it grows in ponds, lakes and canals. Its floating leaves have reddish-brown marbling above and purple spots below, while its large daytime flowers are often fragrant and white, faintly pink or yellow. It is generally sterile but spreads through creeping stems and can densely cover ponds.
A small genus of flowering cacti native to southern Brazil. Its species grow as epiphytes on trees and have flowers with a short tube where the petals join at the base.

A cultivar group of flowering hybrids derived from three species from Chile and Argentina. These soft-stemmed plants bear yellow to red flowers, dislike summer heat and rarely bloom again indoors without greenhouse-like humidity.

A flowering hybrid between Viola cornuta and the hybrid pansy Viola × wittrockiana. It has wider, slightly overlapping petals, while perennial growth, scented flowers or a longer spur may distinguish it from the latter parent.
A leggy hybrid shrub or small tree developed from cherry plum and sand cherry. Its strong-tasting fruit is eaten and made into jams or preserves, but eating the pits is not advised.
stories.edibilityNote: Strong-tasting fruits are eaten or made into jams and preserves; eating the pits is not advised.

stories.summary: An evergreen hybrid shrub with no native origin supplied. Its dark green leaves have silvery, scaly undersides, and small fragrant white flowers appear in autumn.

A cultivated deciduous hybrid shrub, absent from the wild and probably originating in the foothills of central Asia or Iran. Its fragrant pink to light-red flowers are harvested for rose oil and rose water; the edible petals flavor foods, garnish dishes, make tea and are preserved in sugar.
stories.edibilityNote: Petals are used as flavoring, garnish and herbal tea, or preserved in sugar; rose water and powdered roses also feature in cooking.

stories.summary: A terrestrial natural orchid hybrid found in Italy, especially Tuscany. It grows in meadows and open ground in sun or partial shade, producing dense cones of small pink, spotted flowers from April to June.
An artificial flowering-plant hybrid between Freesia corymbosa and Freesia leichtlinii subsp. alba; no native origin or other features are supplied.
A genus of 73 flowering-plant species distributed across Europe, northern Africa, the Middle East and central Asia.

A genus of 43 flowering plants in the pea family, native across the Americas from the United States to southern Argentina and Uruguay. Some species are called mesquites, and tannins occur mainly in their bark and wood, with low concentrations in the pods.
An ornamental small-tree hybrid that arose between cultivated hawthorns. It has glossy, dark green, unlobed leaves.

A succulent flowering plant native to the Sierra Madre Oriental of northeastern Mexico. Its long green leaves tend to curl and have minute edge teeth but no pointed terminal spine; white or pale-yellow flowers crowd the upper part of a short spike.

A perennial group of flowering hybrids of garden origin, created by crosses between Heuchera and Tiarella. Its plants are notable for colourful, patterned leaves and white, pink or cream flowers that usually appear in spring.

An annual flowering plant native to North Africa, Europe and parts of Asia. It has four-petalled yellow flowers followed by beaked pods, while its dark brown to black seeds are commonly used as a spice.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds are used as a spice; young leaves, buds and flowers are edible, and shoots and leaves are eaten cooked in Ethiopia.

stories.summary: A flowering grass hybrid native to mainland Portugal.
A group of small hybrid succulents produced by crossing Pachyphytum and Echeveria. The plants can develop compact, low forms in sunny conditions and can be propagated from detached top rosettes.

A tropical tree native to the Indian subcontinent, southern China and mainland Southeast Asia. Its aromatic leaves season many South and Southeast Asian dishes; its shiny black fruits have sweet edible pulp, but the seeds may be toxic.
stories.edibilityNote: Fresh leaves are used in South and Southeast Asian cooking; berry pulp is edible, but the seeds may be toxic to humans.

stories.summary: A flowering plant in the asparagus family, recorded from Portugal's Madeira Archipelago.
An evergreen tree from South Africa and Mozambique, with male and female reproductive structures on separate trees. Its fruit is edible.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is edible.

stories.summary: A shrubby hybrid rose of cultivated Dutch origin, developed between the 17th and 19th centuries, possibly earlier. Its highly scented flowers are round and densely packed with thin overlapping petals, usually pink but sometimes white or dark red-purple.

A citrus tree whose wild form evolved in a restricted region of southern China and Vietnam. Its small, flattened fruits have thin, loose, pebbly skin and separate easily into segments; most commercial strains are sweeter than the bitter ancestral mandarin.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten fresh or used in salads, desserts and main dishes; peel is used fresh, as zest, dried, or as flavouring.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub or small tree of cultivated west Pacific origin, created by Polynesians from parent species originating in Vanuatu and French Polynesia. Its typically red, five-petalled flowers have prominent orange-tipped structures, while cultivated forms range from white and yellow to blue and purple and may be double-flowered.
stories.edibilityNote: Flowers are eaten in salads in the Pacific Islands and are dried for beverages in several countries.

stories.summary: A rosette-forming flowering plant endemic to Puebla and Oaxaca, Mexico. Its thick, pointed oval leaves are olive, grey or whitish green with red-brown markings, and its late-spring flowers are scarlet with yellow tips.
A grass native to the Pyrenees of France and Spain, Portugal and Morocco. It is the only species in its genus and has blunt to squared-off outer flower bracts, with florets about half their length.
A genus of four grass species native to Mediterranean Europe, North Africa and western Asia from the Levant to Turkmenistan.

An annual or perennial herb or woody-based subshrub, likely native to West Africa. Its pale flowers have a dark red spot, while the calyx becomes fleshy and deep crimson as the fruit matures. The calyces are commonly steeped for an infusion, and the stems yield fibre.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves, young stems and fruits are cooked; calyces and fruits make drinks, and the fruits can be made into jam.

stories.summary: A moss of unstated native origin, frequently recorded at numerous Algerian localities, including Algiers, Kabylie, Constantine and Tlemcen.

sources.title: Orthotrichum tenellum Brid.
sources.attribution: Ros R M, Olaf S R, Eloy O W, Cerón E, plazi (2024). Revisiting the Bryophyte Checklist of Algeria: Exploring Diversity and Distribution. Cryptogamie, Bryologie. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/6xu7ry accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A moss of unstated native origin, commonly recorded across numerous Algerian localities and settings, from Skikda beach to mountain forests.

sources.title: Scleropodium touretii (Brid.) L.F.Koch
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A moss of unstated native origin, widespread in Europe and also reported from parts of Asia, the Americas and Tristan da Cunha, but rare around the Mediterranean. It usually grows in acidic forests on soil near tree bases, sheltered banks or rocks. In Tunisia it was sterile and confined to a tiny patch in the Oued Zen Valley.

sources.title: Pseudotaxiphyllum elegans (Brid.) Z. Iwats.
sources.attribution: Osman I B, Hugonnot V, Muller S D, Daoud-Bouattour A, felipe (2021). Four bryophytes collected in Tunisia, new for mainland Africa. Cryptogamie, Bryologie. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4uzwrs accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A long-lived epiphytic plant recorded across Europe, temperate Asia, northern America, Africa, Australasia and the Pacific. It occurs in woodlands and on shrubs, but also inhabits rock outcrops, rural mosaics and buildings; documented Algerian populations are rare.

sources.title: Dicranoweisia cirrata (Hedw.) Lindb.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A tiny annual herb native to Macaronesia and the Mediterranean region. Its grey, felted growth branches from the base, with spreading spoon-shaped leaves forming rosettes above inconspicuous flower heads; it occurs near coasts in grassland and garrigue.

sources.title: Filago pygmaea L. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A winter annual grass native to Europe, North Africa and western Asia. In Portugal it occurs in dry meadows, pastures and roadside verges.

An annual tuft-forming grass widespread in Eurasia, although the sources do not explicitly identify its native range. Its narrow flower head usually arches downward, with its lower part often enclosed by the uppermost leaf sheath; the blue-green plant soon turns straw-yellow.

sources.title: Festuca myuros L.
sources.attribution: Döring M (2022). German Wikipedia - Species Pages. Wikimedia Foundation. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/4wn9dt accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.title: Festuca myuros L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A perennial native from Ecuador to southern South America. It grows mainly in temperate regions.

sources.title: Geranium core-core Steud. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial native from southern Haida Gwaii to western California, it grows mainly in temperate regions.

sources.title: Juncus hesperius (Piper) Lint — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A short-lived plant originally from the western European–Mediterranean region. Its narrow, elongated fruit has four angles, a deep groove along one side and only a tiny calyx tooth.

sources.title: Valerianella carinata Loisel.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Plant of unstated growth form and with no explicitly stated native origin, recorded from Canada to Colombia and the Caribbean. It occurs in wet pine flatwoods and wet pine savannas.

sources.title: Morella cerifera (L.) Small
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: Bulbous herb native to west-central Portugal, southern Spain and northwestern Africa. It bears dense, rounded flower heads with numerous whitish or pink flowers and grows in places including rocky crevices, fields and sandy ground.

sources.title: Allium baeticum Boiss. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: Evergreen tree native to the Andean valleys of Chile, Peru and Ecuador. Its fruit ripens after falling, developing soft, very sweet, dry and floury orange-yellow flesh around large hard seeds. The ripe fruit is eaten raw or used in Peru to flavour drinks and ice cream, and its flesh can be dried into powder.
stories.edibilityNote: The ripe fruit is eaten raw, used in Peruvian drinks and ice cream, and dried into powder; it was also food in Inca times.

stories.summary: Leafy moss with no explicitly stated native origin, distributed across a northern range extending south to North Africa and from southwestern Asia to North America; it was introduced to Australia and New Zealand. Its slender whitish-green shoots remain tightly leafy and threadlike even when wet, and it fruits rarely.

A liverwort native to Europe, Macaronesia, North America and Asia. It forms green to reddish-brown or nearly black mats and has two-lobed leaves. It favours wet, lime-free sites, often submerged on rocks in streams or beside waterfalls.

A moss native to Europe, Africa, North and South America, Asia, Australia and New Zealand. It grows on soil in woodland and on slopes beside streams, with branched or unbranched stems bearing about 20 pairs of toothed leaves.
A bulbous flowering plant native to the southeastern United States. It has glossy green leaves and slightly nodding flowers that are mostly white, sometimes pink-tinged or veined.

sources.title: Zephyranthes atamasco (L.) Herb. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A moss native to Europe, Macaronesia, North America and New Zealand. It colonises hummocks on open disturbed soil, old fields, railway and roadside ground, and sandy banks; its leaves taper to long points and are toothed toward the tip.

A genus of more than 500 mostly tree-dwelling or rock-growing vines of unspecified native origin, wax plants have leathery, often fleshy leaves and white latex. Their waxy or fleshy flowers grow in rounded or elongated clusters, and their fruits contain flattened seeds with a tuft of hairs.
A moss species of unspecified native origin, it is documented reproducing in Sweden.

A medium-sized tree native to Japan and China. It develops a broad rounded crown, long green to yellowish leaves, and spring flowers that are white with yellow spots; its elongated fruit turns from green to brown before falling.
A flowering shrub recorded from China.
A tree native from Kenya to southern tropical Africa. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical areas.

sources.title: Fernandoa magnifica Seem. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial fern native to Macaronesia and the western Mediterranean. It has a sturdy, dark-scaled underground stem and large upright fronds that arch near their tips, growing beside streams in damp, shady coastal woodland.

sources.title: Pteris incompleta Cav. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A fern native from Mexico through tropical America. It grows mainly in wet tropical areas and has recorded environmental and medicinal uses.

sources.title: Anemia phyllitidis (L.) Sw. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A very spiny cactus endemic to the Americas, ranging from central Canada and the northern United States to northern Mexico. Its small, nearly spherical or barrel-shaped stem bears dense spine clusters; flowers vary from pink and red to yellow-green, while the ripe fleshy fruits remain green.

A photosynthetic species of unspecified native origin. After 14 days of cultivation in seawater, its growth, photosynthetic performance and chlorophyll content were statistically similar across the tested germanium dioxide concentrations.

sources.title: Ulva fenestrata
sources.attribution: Rautenberger R, felipe (2024). Germanium dioxide as agent to control the biofouling diatom Fragilariopsis oceanica for the cultivation of Ulva fenestrata (Chlorophyta). Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ejdynn accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: An annual herb native to Mexico, with its range possibly extending into northern Central America. Its yellow or orange flower heads carry distinctive red or orange V- or W-shaped marks, and its flowers decorate Mexican Day of the Dead altars. It is also used by the food industry as an artificial colorant.
stories.edibilityNote: Used by the food industry as an artificial colorant.

stories.summary: A herbaceous plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it grows in wet meadows and around temporary pools on acidic soils.

A moss with no native origin supplied, found across most of the world but mainly in the Northern Hemisphere. It forms glossy yellow-green to pale-green mats with upright, often tree-like branching. It favours streams, springs and other damp habitats.

A moss with no native origin supplied, found nearly worldwide and commonly throughout Europe. Its green to golden-green mats have broad, finely toothed leaves ending in short sharp points. It grows on wood, bark, rock and soil, including in city centres.

sources.title: Brachythecium rutabulum (Hedw.) Schimp.
sources.attribution: Ros R M, Olaf S R, Eloy O W, Cerón E, plazi (2024). Revisiting the Bryophyte Checklist of Algeria: Exploring Diversity and Distribution. Cryptogamie, Bryologie. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/6xu7ry accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A moss with no native origin supplied. It occurs across temperate regions of both hemispheres and extends into Antarctic tundra.

A moss with no native origin supplied, described as Mediterranean–Atlantic and occurring in Europe, North Africa, southwestern Asia and North America. Several shiny, budlike bulbils in each leaf joint make it immediately recognizable. It forms cushions on wet rocks beside watercourses and on river-flooded sandstone.

sources.title: Bryum gemmiparum De Not.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A moss with no native origin supplied, with an oceanic, mountain-associated distribution and a European stronghold in western Europe. It forms green to yellow-green mats with pale leaf bases. Crowded reproductive leaves at the shoot tips resemble cauliflower and make it especially recognizable.

A moss with no native origin supplied, distributed through tropical and warm-temperate parts of the Americas, Africa, India and Europe. It forms dense cushions and often has clear, spreading tufts at the stem tips. Its transparent, toothed leaf-tip hair is distinctive but may be short or absent on older leaves.

sources.title: Campylopus pilifer Brid.
sources.attribution: J. Florschutz-de Waard, H. R. Zielman, M. A. Bruggeman- Nannenga, sylvia (2011). Flora of the Guianas, Series C, fascicle 2.. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/7x5z7g accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A plant of unstated native origin, found in wet pine savannas and along adjacent roadsides. It is described as occasional in the cited local account.

sources.title: Chasmanthium laxum (L.) H.O.Yates
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A rare plant of unstated native origin, recorded near Algiers and Constantine and at Akfadou, Tiaret, Tlemcen, Réghaïa and La Rassauta.

sources.title: Corsinia coriandrina (Spreng.) Lindb.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A common epiphytic moss with a circumboreal distribution. It forms dense fresh-green to yellowish-green cushions, with leaves that twist when dry. It usually colonises beech, pine and birch bark, favouring acidic, nutrient-poor and lime-poor surfaces.

A moss distributed across the Northern Hemisphere, including Europe, parts of Asia and North to Central America. Its unusually large spore-bearing structures dwarf the small plants. Pressure on ripe capsules, including from raindrops, can propel spores several metres.

A cushion-forming moss distributed through most of Europe and parts of Asia, Africa, North America, New Zealand and Tasmania. It grows in dry, sunny places on lime-rich or otherwise base-rich soil, rocks and walls. Its spore capsule is wrapped by a hood extending below the capsule’s base.
A moss recorded frequently at numerous Algerian localities, including Kabylie, Constantine and the Algerian Sahara.

sources.title: Entosthodon attenuatus (Dicks.) Bryhn 1908
sources.attribution: Ros R M, Olaf S R, Eloy O W, Cerón E, plazi (2024). Revisiting the Bryophyte Checklist of Algeria: Exploring Diversity and Distribution. Cryptogamie, Bryologie. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/6xu7ry accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A moss usually distinguished by egg-shaped leaves that narrow abruptly, short leaf cells and short, egg-shaped capsules. Large, multicellular teeth along the leaf edges are characteristic, although eastern plants occurring with Fabronia ciliaris may have smaller teeth and be difficult to identify.

sources.title: Fabronia pusilla
sources.attribution: Ignatova E A, Kuznetsova O I, Milyutina I A, Fedosov V E, Ignatov M S, felipe (2017). The genus Fabronia (Fabroniaceae, Bryophyta) in Russia. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/anm76n accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A frillwort recorded rarely at several Algerian localities, including Blida, Mostaganem, Tlemcen and the Djurdjura region.

sources.title: Fossombronia angulosa (Dicks.) Raddi
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A subshrub native to Arizona, New Mexico, Sonora and Coahuila. It bears clusters of pink to purplish-pink flowers and grows primarily in desert or dry shrubland, with other records from rocky mountain slopes, woodland clearings and subalpine meadows.

sources.title: Glandularia chiricahensis Umber — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A leafy moss of unstated native origin, widespread in Europe and also occurring in parts of Asia, North Africa and North to Central America. It forms glossy dark-green mats with flattened, densely leafy shoots that resemble leafy liverworts. It mainly inhabits shaded, moist deciduous woodland, especially tree bases, but also grows on soil, rocks, stones and walls.
A perennial native to Central America and from southern Brazil to northeastern Argentina. It grows mainly in wet tropical environments.

sources.title: Hydrocotyle bowlesioides Mathias & Constance — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A leafy moss of unstated native origin, occurring in Europe, parts of Asia, North Africa, the Canary Islands and North America. It forms broad, slightly glossy green mats, with arching stems ending in clustered, downward-curving, catkin-like leafy branches. In woods it grows mainly at the bases of deciduous trees and on mineral-rich, mildly acidic rock.

sources.title: Isothecium alopecuroides (Lam. ex Dubois) Isov.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A shrub native from Texas through tropical America. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical environments and is used medicinally and socially.

sources.title: Lantana canescens Kunth — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An annual herb with no supplied native origin, Neapolitan melilot grows upright and branched, with serrated leaflets and long, fairly loose flower clusters. Its mature, straw-coloured fruits are usually hairless and do not normally hang down.

sources.title: Melilotus neapolitanus Ten.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A climbing woody plant native from southern Mexico and southern Florida through tropical America, and from western tropical Africa to Angola, horseeye bean grows mainly in wet tropical regions. It is used for food, medicine and environmental purposes.
stories.edibilityNote: Used for food; the parts and preparation are not specified.

sources.title: Mucuna sloanei Fawc. & Rendle — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An epiphytic fern native to the Philippines, fishtail swordfern grows chiefly in wet tropical areas. Its leaf divisions have conspicuously forked tips, and this unusual form is cultivated in many gardens.

sources.title: Nephrolepis falcata (Cav.) C.Chr. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A flowering tree native to East Africa, Mickey Mouse plant is recorded from Somalia, Kenya and Tanzania. It is cultivated as an ornamental.
A flowering plant recorded from the Buenos Aires countryside, with no native origin supplied. An early description notes lance-shaped, wavy or toothed leaves and flowers arising from mid-stem.

sources.title: Oenothera mollissima L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A shrub or tree native from Florida through the Caribbean. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical environments and is used medicinally.

sources.title: Pavonia spinifex (L.) Cav. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A hydrangea-family plant with no native origin supplied. It has not been recorded in Sweden.
A fern with underground stems, native to tropical and subtropical America. It grows mainly in wet tropical environments and is used medicinally.

sources.title: Phlebodium pseudoaureum (Cav.) Lellinger — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A moss distributed across Europe, North America and Asia, with no native origin specified. It inhabits moist ground from tundra and bogs to meadows, forests and watersides. Its green to yellow-green leaves become crisp and bent when dry but flatten when wet.

A moss with no native origin stated, it is widespread across temperate parts of the Northern Hemisphere. It forms glossy green to golden-brown mats on bark or lightly decayed wood, with abundant small shoots often giving its branch tips a shaggy appearance.
A moss with no native origin stated, it is documented as reproducing in Sweden.
A moss with no native origin stated, it is documented as reproducing in Sweden.
A tuber-rooted perennial native to Mexico and the US states of Arizona and Texas. It bears solitary yellow flowers and grows in wet meadows and along riverbanks, flowering from March to May.

A shrub native from Europe through south-central Siberia and northwestern Iran, and also to Algeria. It has lightly fruity-scented cream-white flowers and round black hips, and its complex roots help stabilize embankments.

sources.title: Rosa spinosissima L. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A stemless succulent whose native origin is not explicitly stated, occurring from eastern South Africa to tropical East Africa. Its upright, dull-green leaves have crowded cross-bands that fade with age, and it often forms dense groups beneath trees or bushes.

A perennial herb with no native origin stated, found beside water in Europe. Its stem has conspicuous wings, while its sharply tipped, saw-toothed leaves lack the ear-like basal lobes seen in a similar figwort; it favors shaded wetlands and damp woods.
A flowering herb with no undisputed native origin supplied. It occupies moist pioneer waste ground, especially salty sites, and was recently introduced to France.
An annual plant recorded in Portugal. It grows in fallow ground, pastures and scrub clearings, especially on dry, acidic soils.

A moss reported from tropical and temperate regions, including the Andes and Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta. Algerian records need reassessment because several taxa once treated within the Trichostomum brachydontium complex are now recognised separately.

sources.title: Trichostomum brachydontium Bruch
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A scrambling annual herb native from the Mediterranean to Central Asia and Afghanistan. Its solitary flowers are pale yellow, sometimes purple-veined, with a densely silky-haired upper petal. It grows in grassland, cultivated ground and along roadsides.

sources.title: Vicia hybrida L. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial horsetail hybrid of field horsetail and water horsetail. Its cones are rare and remain closed, while its spores are sterile. In Central Europe it inhabits wet meadows, ditches, shores and water-seeped banks.
A perennial hybrid native to Europe’s temperate regions. Its parents are Silene dioica and Silene latifolia subsp. alba.

sources.title: Silene × hampeana Meusel & K.Werner — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A shrub native from Mexico to Guatemala. It grows mainly in wet tropical environments.

sources.title: Moussonia deppeana (Schltdl. & Cham.) Klotzsch ex Hanst. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A tuberous plant native to southwestern Cape Province. It grows mainly in the subtropical biome.

sources.title: Ixia polystachia L. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An artificial plant hybrid of unstated geographic origin. Its parentage comprises Glandularia peruviana, G. phlogiflora, G. platensis and G. tweedieana.

sources.title: Glandularia × hybrida (Groenland & Rümpler) G.L.Nesom & Pruski — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial wetland plant native from western Europe to the western and central Mediterranean. It grows in still waters such as ponds and lakes, and less often in slow-moving streams.

sources.title: Helosciadium inundatum (L.) W.D.J.Koch — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A tiny annual aquatic plant native from southwestern France to Spain and from northwestern Africa to Mauritania. It inhabits temporary pools on open sandy or silty ground. In shallow pools it forms dense stands of minute plants and flowers as the water recedes, while deeper-water plants grow larger and may flower submerged.

sources.title: Elatine brochonii Clavaud
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.title: Elatine brochonii Clavaud — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A shrub recorded from the Sierra Madre del Sur in Michoacán, Guanajuato and Mexico State. It has large, sometimes lobed leaves and numerous hanging flower heads with white outer florets and yellow centres, creating a showy display. It occurs in cool pine forest on steep slopes and in drier pine-oak forest along roadsides.

sources.title: Montanoa grandiflora DC.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A succulent perennial native to Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao. It grows mainly in deserts and dry shrubland.

sources.title: Agave vivipara L. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A shrub or tree native from Mexico to El Salvador. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions.

sources.title: Phymosia rosea (DC.) Kearney — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial herb with no explicitly stated native origin, occurring across the Pyrenees and Alps to the northern Balkans. It forms low tufts and bears solitary daisy-like flower heads with white rays and yellow centres in July and August, often on damp, acidic mountain ground near lingering snow.

sources.title: Leucanthemopsis alpina (L.) Heywood
sources.attribution: C. Benedi, A. Buira, E. Rico, M. B. Crespo, A. Quintanar, C. Aedo, S. Castroviejo, plazi (2019). Flora Iberica / Vol. XVI (III): Compositae (partim). Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/28egpw accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

A succulent perennial native to northern and western Mexico, growing mainly in subtropical regions.

sources.title: Agave maximiliana Baker — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An aquatic moss widely distributed south of the Arctic, particularly in Northern Hemisphere flowing freshwater. It is among the largest aquatic mosses and forms loose, sprawling or hanging mats on rocks and tree roots.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A plant species recorded as rare around Blida, Algiers, Michelet and Kabylie du Djurdjura; its native origin is not specified.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A rhizome-forming geophyte native from Mexico through tropical America, growing mainly in wet tropical regions. It is reported as a medicine for unspecified disorders.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A succulent subshrub native to Veracruz, Mexico, growing mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions.

sources.title: Sedum burrito Moran — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A plant with underground stems, native from Mexico to Central America. It grows mainly in wet tropical regions.

sources.title: Begonia plebeja Liebm. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An annual or low woody-based plant native to Mexico, northern Venezuela, southern Bolivia, Brazil and northern Argentina. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions.

sources.title: Ocimum carnosum (Spreng.) Link & Otto ex Benth. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A tree native from southern Mexico to Central America. It grows mainly in wet tropical regions.

sources.title: Casimiroa tetrameria Millsp. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A tree native from Mexico to Central America, growing mainly in seasonally dry tropical areas.

sources.title: Lippia umbellata Cav. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A subshrub native from Veracruz in Mexico to Chile, found mainly in seasonally dry tropical areas. It is used medicinally for infections and unspecified disorders.

sources.title: Alternanthera pubiflora (Benth.) Kuntze — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An annual or perennial grass native from Africa to Indo-China, growing mainly in seasonally dry tropical areas. It is used medicinally, though no particular use is specified.

sources.title: Eragrostis tenuifolia (A.Rich.) Hochst. ex Steud. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A subshrub or climbing shrub native from southern Mexico through tropical America. Across much of seasonally dry South America it is a widespread weed of roadsides and abandoned pastures.

sources.title: Mimosa candollei R.Grether
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.title: Mimosa candollei R.Grether — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial, sometimes rhizomatous plant native from east-central Portugal to northwestern and central Spain. In Portugal it is confined to the upper Serra da Estrela and assessed as Near Threatened, with only two known locations but no evidence of continuing habitat decline.

sources.title: Luzula caespitosa (J.Gay ex E.Mey.) Steud. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A low-growing shrubby cactus recorded across parts of Mexico from Sinaloa to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec and from Tamaulipas to Veracruz. It has thick, fuzzy, mostly oval green pads with spreading white spines, yellow flowers, and fuzzy spherical fruits.

A Begonia hybrid created in 1845 by crossing Begonia hydrocotylifolia with Begonia manicata. It has long flower stalks, white to pink flowers, and broad dark-green leaves with red undersides and pale-green veins.

A bulb-growing perennial native from Italy and Greece through southwestern Türkiye to southeastern Syria. It grows mainly in temperate regions; in Portugal it occurs in sunny meadows, pastures and woodland clearings, often on stony ground.

sources.title: Ornithogalum gussonei Ten. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A tiny annual rush native to the Mediterranean region and Atlantic seaboard of Europe and North Africa. Its extremely slender upright stems bear small clusters of greenish or reddish flowers, and it grows in seasonally flooded grassland on siliceous ground.

A rose-family flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in cool, somewhat shaded and moist woodland, sometimes near waterways. Its stems may have gland-tipped hairs, but this feature needs confirmation.

A perennial herb native from northeastern Türkiye to Transcaucasia. Its leafy, short-haired stems carry divided leaves and dense clusters of many small white-and-yellow flower heads, giving it the appearance of a luxuriant yarrow. It is cultivated as an ornamental.

sources.title: Tanacetum macrophyllum (Waldst. & Kit.) Sch.Bip. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A shrubby cactus found across several states of Mexico. It often forms thickets of climbing or creeping, spiny stems with tuber-like roots, and its large white, pink-tinged flowers open at night. The red fruits are edible.
stories.edibilityNote: The red fruits are edible.

stories.summary: An annual bellflower native from eastern and southern Portugal to southwestern and south-central Spain. It grows mainly in temperate regions.

sources.title: Campanula transtagana R.Fern. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A flowering plant in the legume family; its native origin is not supplied. In Portugal, it grows in sparse meadows, somewhat degraded pasture, banks and rocky outcrops, favouring acidic, sandy or stony ground.

A bulbous plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows near the coast in clearings among pine woods and dry scrub on settled sand; in Portugal it is restricted to the southern Algarve coast and assessed as Near Threatened, although its validity as a species needs study.

A liverwort occurring in parts of the Northern Hemisphere. It forms green to brown-red mats with toothed, two-lobed leaves, and has distinctive brown clusters of tiny one-celled reproductive bodies at the shoot tips.

sources.title: Scapania nemorea (L.) Grolle
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A perennial herb centred in western Europe but ranging from North Africa to Iran and Afghanistan. It is a chlorophyll-free parasite of plants including field eryngo, with an unbranched purple stem and whitish, purple-veined flowers.
A perennial plant with underground stems, native to northern and central Madeira. It grows mainly in the subtropical biome.

sources.title: Goodyera macrophylla Lowe — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A low-growing plant whose native origin is not stated. In Portugal it occurs along salt-marsh edges and among coastal cliff and rock vegetation.
A perennial sedge native to the Azores, growing primarily in temperate environments.

sources.title: Carex hochstetteriana J.Gay ex Seub. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial fern hybrid native to Madeira, where it grows mainly in the subtropical biome. It is a cross between Polystichum falcinellum and P. setiferum.

sources.title: Polystichum × maderense Johns. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial fern native to Madeira. It grows mainly in the subtropical biome.

sources.title: Polystichum falcinellum (Sw.) C.Presl — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An aquatic plant recorded from Swedish lakes around Dannemora and Stockholm.

sources.title: Cladophora aegagropila (Linnaeus 1753) Trevis.
sources.attribution: Jarvis C, admin (2007). Chapter 7: Linnaean Plant Names and their Types (part C). Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.291971 accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A rock-growing fern native from Macaronesia and western Europe to the Mediterranean. In Portugal it occupies cool, shady crevices in rocks, banks and walls, generally on siliceous surfaces.

sources.title: Asplenium obovatum Viv. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial fern, sometimes growing on rock, native to southern tropical America. It is used for food and medicine, although the plant parts and preparations are unspecified.
stories.edibilityNote: Used for food; the source gives no plant part, preparation or cultural context.

sources.title: Blechnum cordatum (Desv.) Hieron. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A flowering palm native to Madagascar’s rainforests, particularly the southeast. Its leaf bases form three vertical columns, giving the trunk a triangular cross-section, while the upright leaves arch near their tips. Yellow-green flowers become round black fruit, and only about 1,000 plants remain in a small part of its native habitat.

sources.title: Dypsis decaryi (Jum.) Beentje & J.Dransf.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A shrub hybrid arising naturally where its naturalised parent species occur; no geographic native origin is given. It grows mainly in subtropical regions and is used medicinally.

sources.title: Lantana × strigocamara R.W.Sanders — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A bulbous plant native to the Edwards Plateau of Texas, growing mainly in the temperate biome.

sources.title: Allium fraseri (Ownbey) Shinners — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: Annual plant native to Madeira and western and southern Europe. It grows mainly in temperate regions.

sources.title: Aira multiculmis Dumort. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: Plant native to southern tropical and southern Africa. It grows mainly in subtropical regions.

sources.title: Blechnum capense Burm.f. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: Shrub native from Brazil to northeastern Argentina, including Misiones. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions.

sources.title: Calliandra selloi (Spreng.) J.F.Macbr. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: Annual flowering plant native from southern Europe to the western Himalaya and Central Asia. Often grown ornamentally, it bears spikes of blue, pink or white flowers. Its aerial parts and seeds contain highly toxic alkaloids, so the plant is considered poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: Documented as used for food, but its aerial parts and seeds contain highly toxic alkaloids and the plant is considered poisonous.

sources.title: Delphinium ajacis L. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: Terrestrial moss whose native origin is not supplied. It is described as long-lived and associated with pioneer vegetation and grasslands.

sources.title: Fissidens viridulus (Sw.) Wahlenb.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A short-lived terrestrial plant associated with pioneer vegetation. It favors moderately nutrient-rich conditions and is reported as frequent across numerous listed localities.

sources.title: Riccia ciliata Hoffm.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

stories.summary: A short-lived terrestrial plant associated with pioneer vegetation and nutrient-rich agricultural settings. One record places it on clay soil in a shallow depression beside a dirt road, and it is reported as frequent across numerous listed localities.

sources.title: Tortula truncata (Hedw.) Mitt.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

sources.title: Kniphofia linearifolia Baker — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A vigorous perennial herb occurring in southern Africa. It grows along streams and on black, clay-rich swamp soil. Its grey-blue, finely toothed leaves accompany dense cylindrical flower clusters bearing pale red to red-green buds and usually white or greenish-white flowers.

A crust-forming red alga occurring in the Mediterranean and northeastern Atlantic. It forms horizontal, fan-shaped blades ranging from dark pink to reddish brown. It favors dim rocky seabeds, often in caves, and may also grow on Posidonia oceanica rhizomes and mats.
Plant native to Honshu, Japan, where it grows mainly in the temperate biome.

sources.title: Ajania pacifica (Nakai) K.Bremer & Humphries — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: Perennial plant native from the Indian subcontinent through central and southern China to Indo-China. It grows mainly in the temperate biome.

sources.title: Ophiopogon intermedius D.Don — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: Woody perennial vine native to Guyana, much of Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, Paraguay, Argentina and Uruguay. It is hairless, with three-lobed leaves, purple flowers and ellipsoid fruits.

Annual or perennial herb native to Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay. Its stems range from trailing to upright, with deeply lobed, rough-haired leaves and dense, headlike spikes of white to purple flowers.
Epiphytic fern native from southern Myanmar to New Guinea.

sources.title: Microsorum musifolium (Blume) Copel. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial fern of unspecified native origin, widespread across Eurasia and North America in the Northern Hemisphere. Its funnel-shaped rosette of yellow-green fronds has a faint lemon scent, with spore clusters arranged in two rows near the leaflet edges.
A succulent shrub native from southern Brazil to northeastern Argentina, growing mainly in the subtropical biome.

sources.title: Opuntia arechavaletae Speg. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A bulb-forming perennial hybrid first produced in Prescot, England, from Hippeastrum reginae and H. vittatum. It has green strap-like leaves and red flowers marked with a white central stripe; several clones exist, but their identities are now uncertain.

A small moss of unstated native origin, occurring in Europe, Macaronesia and North America. Its creeping stems bear tightly folded, sharply toothed leaves, and it grows on vertical tree trunks and rock faces.
An annual plant native to Europe, western Türkiye and western Morocco. It grows mainly in temperate regions.

sources.title: Salicornia procumbens Sm. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A hybrid subshrub native to southern Portugal. It is a cross between Lavandula stoechas subsp. luisieri and Lavandula viridis and grows mainly in subtropical regions.

sources.title: Lavandula × alportelensis P.Silva, Fontes & Myre — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A moss occurring across almost all Europe and in parts of North Africa and North America. Its loosely branched shoots are yellow-green or fresh green, with branches that shine when dry and densely packed, strongly folded leaves.
A plant documented at numerous Algerian sites, including ravines, forests and the Lake Tonga watershed. It was described as frequent.

stories.summary: A large leafy liverwort distributed across the Mediterranean, western Europe including Macaronesia, and southwestern Asia. It forms broad, dense, trailing mats with opposite leaves, typically in shaded, damp banks, ledges and rocky wooded ravines where water seeps.

sources.title: Angraecum elephantinum Schltr. — Plants of the World Online

stories.edibilityNote: Seeds were eaten since prehistory, raw when green or thoroughly cooked; human food use declined by the nineteenth century.

A biennial or perennial herb native from Europe to Iran. It has upright, strongly ribbed stems that branch near the top, hairy divided leaves, and flower heads that may have ray florets or be entirely disc-like. It favours slopes, roadsides and deciduous woodland edges, especially on sandy, siliceous soils.

A commercially valuable red alga whose native origin is not stated. Its firm, cartilage-like branches lie in one plane, and it inhabits wave-battered rocky shores. It is an important source of agar.
A subshrub or shrub native from the eastern United States to eastern Mexico. It grows mainly in subtropical regions.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A parasitic plant growing from underground buds; its native origin is not supplied. It occurs across Europe and North Africa and, in Portugal, is confined mainly to northern coastal dunes. It parasitizes Artemisia species.

A plant growing from underground buds; its native origin is not supplied. In Portugal it inhabits scrub, pinewoods and woodland, usually on limestone soils, and parasitizes rosemary and probably other shrubs.
A parasitic plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in scrub and parasitizes rosemary.

A perennial parasitic plant; its native origin is not supplied. In Portugal it grows in hedges and fallow ground on limestone soils, parasitizing fennel or other perennial members of the carrot family. It is currently known there from only two small population centres, around Lisbon and in the Algarve.

A herbaceous parasitic plant native to the Mediterranean region. It mainly parasitizes members of the legume, daisy and mint families, and bears dense clusters of strongly curved, pale blue-violet flowers.

A parasitic broomrape native to Eurasia and North Africa. It has many slender yellowish stems but no leaves or chlorophyll, drawing nutrients from other plants’ roots. Its tubular flowers are white and blue to purple.
A shrub or low-growing shrub native from southern Ecuador to northern and central Peru. It grows mainly in subtropical regions.

sources.title: Calceolaria pavonii Benth. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to the Canary Islands.

sources.title: Carduus clavulatus Link — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial flowering herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It inhabits scrub clearings and rocky outcrops on basic rocks and green schist, sometimes in flood beds or places that become temporarily waterlogged; its Portuguese population is endangered and severely fragmented.

An annual flowering plant whose native origin is not supplied. In Portugal it is known only from traditional dry-farmed olive groves on basic soils, and bears flowers consistently in threes at each node, with a central male flower between two female flowers.
A geophyte whose native origin is not supplied. In Portugal it is recorded as a parasite of Carlina hispanica, while its habitat remains undocumented.

A subshrub native from southern France and southern Portugal to southwestern Spain. It grows around upper saltmarsh edges and on coastal sands, with some inland populations on slightly salty clay; in mainland Portugal it is endangered and known only from the Algarve coast.

sources.title: Myriolimon diffusum (Pourr.) Lledó, Erben & M.B.Crespo — Plants of the World Online

stories.summary: A subshrub of unspecified native origin, distributed around Mediterranean coasts. Its leafless, prostrate or rising stems carry dense clusters of small lilac flowers, and it grows in coastal salt marshes, salt steppes, cliffs and rocks.
A subshrub native to eastern Spain, growing primarily in the temperate biome.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A tropical plant native to southeastern and southern Brazil. It grows on other plants or rocks, mainly in wet tropical environments.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial plant of unstated native origin, distributed across northwestern Africa, southern Europe and western Asia. It has closely grouped lower leaves, white flowers in umbrella-like clusters and small, nearly spherical fruits.

A perennial grass of unstated native origin, occurring from Hungary and the Mediterranean region to Iran. It spreads by a creeping underground stem and has rolled, threadlike grey-green leaves, with sparse flower clusters bearing straight, rough bristles.
A plant species of unspecified type and native origin. It has been recorded in ravine bottoms, Stora and several Kabylie localities, where it was described as rare.

Its small known range and declining habitat contributed to its Vulnerable assessment in mainland Portugal.
Annual plant of unstated native origin. In Portugal it occurs in dry meadows, fallow fields, pastures and roadsides.
Cactus native to the deserts of Mexico. Its solitary rounded or slightly cylindrical body bears exceptionally numerous thin, wavy ribs, white spines and white-to-purple flowers.

Cactus tribe of unstated native origin, distributed from North America to northeastern South America. Its members form shrubs or cushions with strongly jointed, cylindrical shoots; most have only short-lived leaf remnants, though Pereskiopsis and Quiabentia retain succulent leaves.

An annual or perennial herb found on disturbed saline ground and around saltmarsh scrub in Portugal. In mainland Portugal it is endangered and known only from three locations on the southern Algarve coast, although the assessment is based on limited information.
A tuberous hybrid plant native to the western Mediterranean. It is the cross Ophrys bombyliflora × Ophrys speculum and grows mainly in subtropical regions.

An annual plant found near the Portuguese coast on sandy soils. It grows in annual grasslands on stable dunes, sandy-scrub clearings, forest firebreaks and pinewood margins.
An annual or perennial herb found on sandy ground in Portugal. Its subspecies occupy habitats ranging from coastal dunes and dry scrub clearings to inland sands, stony places and river deposits.
Annual plant native to the western Mediterranean, growing mainly in subtropical regions.

Shrub or tree native from peninsular Thailand to Malesia, growing mainly in wet tropical regions. Its roots and leaves have medicinal uses, but the leaves are reported poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves are reported poisonous; terminal shoots were reportedly eaten by women to induce abortion, not as food.

Members range from dwarf shrubs to small trees and have leaves arranged in four perpendicular rows; alpine forms may have leaves reduced to thick scales.
A shrub hybrid native to New Zealand’s South Island, growing mainly in the temperate biome. It is a cross between Veronica speciosa and Veronica stricta.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A filamentous green alga with no native origin stated; it occurs worldwide and is typical of soil communities. It is common on cultivated soils, often dominating them, and its cylindrical cells become barrel-shaped over time.

A unicellular alga with no native origin stated, recorded in European waters. Its nearly round cell has a central constriction forming two halves, each with one round chloroplast; it usually inhabits neutral, moderately nutrient-rich peat cuttings, bogs, ditches and ponds, but can tolerate slightly alkaline water.
A plant native from the Iberian Peninsula to Morocco. It grows mainly in the temperate biome.

A perennial grass hybrid native to the Azores, it grows mainly in temperate conditions. It is the cross Holcus lanatus × Holcus rigidus.

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

An ecologically diverse species complex of unstated native origin, with wild tetraploid plants widely distributed around the Mediterranean. It gave rise to cultivated forms including the robust-stemmed common leek and slender-leaved kurrat, which remain fully interfertile with the wild plants.

An annual or winter-annual herb of unstated native origin. Its branched, creeping-to-rising stems have a single line of hairs between each pair of leaves, while its flowers have deeply split petals and usually three to five purple-violet anthers.

An annual grass native from western Europe through the Mediterranean to the western Himalayas. It has narrow, pointed leaves and a straight, one-sided flower spike with closely pressed, bristle-tipped flowers.
