sources.title: Salicornia depressa in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: An annual or biennial clover native from southeastern and eastern Europe to Türkiye, growing mainly in temperate regions.

sources.title: Trifolium vessiculosum Savi — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A genus of annual and perennial flowering herbs native to southern Africa, including South Africa and Lesotho. Its flowers usually have two downward-pointing oil-bearing spurs, which are visited by specially adapted Rediviva bees.

A green alga occurring in the Atlantic, Mediterranean, Red Sea and Indian Ocean. It forms glossy, dark olive-green clusters of translucent oval or spherical bladders, usually attached to shallow rocks or coralligenous formations.

A terrestrial fern occurring from southern China and Taiwan through parts of South and Southeast Asia. In mountain forests, it produces very large, broadly triangular, nearly leathery fronds on a creeping woody underground stem.

sources.title: Microlepia platyphylla in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of perennial herbs occurring in East Asia and extending to Japan, the Philippines and Vietnam. The plants have tufted, grasslike basal leaves and mature seeds that are deep blue to purple and resemble berries.

sources.title: Liriope in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: An annual flowering plant native to tropical and subtropical America, growing mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions.
stories.edibilityNote: Documented as used for food, but the source gives no plant part or preparation.

sources.title: Tinantia erecta (Jacq.) Fenzl — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A genus of small mosses occurring across tropical and temperate regions worldwide. Its plants form tufts or loose cushions with keeled leaves, and many species rarely produce spore capsules.

sources.title: Zygodon in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A one-species genus of perennial flowering plants occurring in the southeastern United States. It bears solitary or loosely grouped flower heads, usually blue to purplish blue but occasionally white or lilac, above leaves with smooth or spiny-toothed edges.

sources.title: Stokesia in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of flowering plants found in the Neotropics, with most of its roughly fifteen species concentrated in Brazil and a few elsewhere in Central and South America.
A minute moss of unspecified native origin. It grows on damp soil and silty hummocks near riverbanks, and is recognizable by its loosely arranged leaf cells and finely toothed leaf tips.

sources.title: Pseudephemerum nitidum in Bryophyte Flora of North America @ efloras.org
sources.attribution: Bryophyte Flora of North America, eFloras

stories.summary: A widespread genus of mosses whose native origin is not supplied. Its leaves often become crisped, curled or twisted when dry, while the large, folded capsule hood covers much of the capsule.

sources.title: Ptychomitrium in Moss Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: An almost cosmopolitan genus of mosses whose native origin is not supplied. Its small plants often form dense, lime-encrusted cushions or tufa, with leaves clustered in whorls and distinctively toothed near the base.

sources.title: Eucladium in Bryophyte Flora of North America @ efloras.org
sources.attribution: Bryophyte Flora of North America, eFloras

stories.summary: A genus of very small mosses whose native origin is not supplied. Its stems creep along the surface, bearing usually toothed leaves with long, narrow tips; the genus is notably variable in form.

sources.title: Fabronia in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of small to medium mosses whose native origin is not supplied, occurring mostly in mountain and arctic-alpine regions. It forms thin green to golden-green mats, with leaves strongly folded near the base and toothed toward the tip.

sources.title: Lescuraea in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A slender moss of unspecified native origin, found on rocks and in rock crevices in alpine and subalpine regions. Its leaves lie against the stem when dry and spread when moist; the leaf midrib stops below the tip and the margins are scalloped near the base.

sources.title: Anoectangium aestivum in Moss Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A mat-forming moss of unspecified native origin, found on logs, tree bases, soil and rocks in forests at low to moderate elevations. It has concave leaves, curved nearly upright capsules and short-tapered, sword-shaped branches that are somewhat flattened.

sources.title: Callicladium haldaneanum in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: An annual plant of unspecified native origin. A Catalan account places it in small grasslands dominated by annual plants.

A usually robust moss of unspecified native origin, growing on moist sandstone ledges and in crevices near streams and waterfalls. Its leaves typically curl tightly inward from their tips when dry, and subterranean reproductive bodies have been reported specifically from Macaronesian specimens.

sources.title: Fissidens asplenioides in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A subtropical subshrub native from Bolivia to southern Brazil and northern Argentina. It grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

sources.title: Glandularia peruviana (L.) Small — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A moss recorded from western North America, Mexico, Eurasia, northern Africa and Pacific islands, favouring warm coastal areas and dry rock. It forms olive to brown-black tufts, with leaves pressed straight against the stem when dry but spreading or bending backward when moist.

sources.title: Grimmia lisae in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A moss recorded from western North America, Chile, Europe, Kazakhstan and Atlantic islands, growing on dry rock and occasionally cultivated plum trees. Its leaves spread widely when dry, with broad translucent tips bearing narrow, sharply pointed teeth; capsules mature in spring.

sources.title: Hedwigia stellata in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A small moss recorded across Asia, Europe, the Americas and Oceania, growing on limestone, soil or grassland. Its yellow-green leaves curl inward into narrow tubes when dry, then spread widely when moist; small reproductive buds may also be present.

sources.title: Hyophila involuta in Moss Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A shrub native from Texas through Central America and from Ecuador to northern Argentina. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions.

sources.title: Lantana velutina M.Martens & Galeotti — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A rock-dwelling moss recorded at high elevations in Colorado, South America, Eurasia, Africa, New Zealand and Australia. Its leaves run slightly down the stem and have broadly pointed tips, but the identification of the only known Colorado population remains uncertain.

sources.title: Leptodon smithii in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: An annual or subshrub native to tropical and subtropical America. It has upright, four-angled stems and leafy flower spikes, and occurs around pond margins, wet depressions, sandy ditches and prairies.
stories.edibilityNote: The species is documented as having a food use, but the edible parts and preparation are not specified.

sources.title: Ludwigia erecta in Flora of North America @ efloras.org
Ludwigia erecta (L.) H.Hara — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An annual native to Texas, growing in sandy soils. It usually has gland-tipped hairs throughout its stems and produces flower heads with both ray and disc florets from late summer into fall.

sources.title: Palafoxia hookeriana in Flora of North America @ efloras.org
Palafoxia hookeriana Torr. & A.Gray — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A salt-tolerant moss recorded near sea level around Atlantic and Gulf coasts and in Europe, Syria, northern Africa, Macaronesia and New Zealand. It is usually pale yellow above and yellow-brown below, with leaves tightly curled around the stem when dry; its capsules are rare.

sources.title: Tortella flavovirens in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A shrub or tree native from southern Tanzania to northeastern Mozambique. It grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions.

sources.title: Coffea zanguebariae Lour. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A moss with no native origin supplied. It usually has a single long leaf midrib, although some leaves have shorter or doubled midribs, and it is rarely found above the tree line.

sources.title: Campyliadelphus chrysophyllus in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A green alga with no native origin supplied. Its elongated cells join into a net, usually with five- or six-sided openings; colonies begin as rounded green tubes and may become yellow and torn with age.

An annual seaweed with no native origin supplied. It forms brittle reddish-brown to yellowish-red tufts, with cylindrical branches that shorten towards the tip to create an irregularly pyramidal outline. In the British and Irish account it is usually attached to other plants in the lower intertidal zone.

sources.title: Laurencia obtusa (Hudson) J.V. Lamouroux — Seaweed.ie, Michael D. Guiry

stories.summary: A shrub native to southern tropical Africa, growing mainly in seasonally dry tropical habitats.

sources.title: Podranea brycei (N.E.Br.) Sprague — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A frond-forming plant with no native origin supplied. Its flattened branches repeatedly fork from a small attachment disc, and reproductive structures often form an interrupted midrib. It grows on rocks and shells below the shore, recorded to 13 metres deep.
A subshrub native from Portugal to western Spain, growing mainly in temperate habitats.

sources.title: Biscutella lusitanica Jord. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A green alga with no native origin supplied. It forms dense, dark-green turf from tightly packed, elongated and branching bladders. It inhabits shaded rock crevices in shallow surf-zone waters.

A moss with no native origin supplied. In Britain and Ireland it is associated with very wet districts and consistently humid places with little temperature variation. Its upper leaf edges can be toothed, so that feature alone may cause confusion with similar mosses.

A small moss whose native origin is not stated, recorded across several continents and Pacific islands. It grows mainly on tree bark and has leaves that twist when dry, each ending in a conspicuous smooth hair-point. Leaf-like reproductive structures occur at stem tips and in upper leaf axils.

sources.title: Syntrichia laevipila in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A creeping perennial herb endemic to New Zealand, although also recorded from Sardinia in Europe. It forms loose mats, rooting beyond where its nodding white flowers appear, and can become an aggressive weed in urban areas, wasteland and plant nurseries.

sources.title: Epilobium nummulariifolium • New Zealand Plant Conservation Network

stories.summary: A feather moss whose native origin is not stated. It has dense branches with crowded, narrow pointed leaves; some leaf tips twist halfway around, and some stems creep underground.

A small red seaweed whose native origin is not stated in this British and Irish account. Its compressed crimson fronds arise from creeping cylindrical runners and have flattened upper branches, blunt tips, hollow interiors and pinched nodes. It grows on rocks and kelp holdfasts in silty pools and below low tide on exposed shores.

sources.title: Lomentaria orcadensis (Harvey) F.S. Collins ex W.R. Taylor — Seaweed.ie, Michael D. Guiry

stories.summary: An upright, spreading annual herb whose native origin is not stated. It bears numerous showy flower spikes above dense, narrow green foliage; the blooms last into autumn and can be used fresh or dried.

sources.title: Deeringia spicata 'Flamingo Feather' (Celosia Spicata, Cockscomb, Wheat Celosia) | North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
sources.attribution: North Carolina State University Extension Plant Toolbox

stories.summary: A red alga whose native origin is not stated, distributed in the English Channel, Atlantic and Mediterranean. Its firm body grades from dark red at the base to bright carmine tips, with upper branches ending in spiny branchlets. It grows on rocky seabeds from shallow water to 70 metres deep.

A bright-green moss whose native origin is not stated, recorded in the Americas, southern and western Europe, Turkey and Macaronesia. It is distinguished by several interrupted leaf rosettes along each stem and slender hair-points that curve back when dry. It also reproduces through small red tubers.

sources.title: Rosulabryum canariense in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of about 65 perennial herb species, sometimes low shrubs, distributed across North Africa, Asia and southern Europe; its native origin is not explicitly stated. Members have alternate simple leaves, flower clusters at stem tips, five petals and usually dry capsules.

sources.title: Haplophyllum in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A much-branched perennial subshrub native to temperate Asia. It has terminal rounded flower clusters with white, pink or mauve flowers, while its stems and leaves range from nearly hairless to densely hairy. The species is extremely variable across southwestern Asia, and the two subspecies recognized in Pakistan may not be distinct.

sources.title: Ziziphora clinopodioides in Flora of Pakistan @ efloras.org
Ziziphora clinopodioides Lam. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A biennial or subshrub native to the western and southern Balkan Peninsula, growing mainly in the temperate biome.

sources.title: Verbascum undulatum Lam. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A genus of relatively large plants forming coarse mats, with no native origin supplied. Its yellow-green to brown growth has feather-like stems and broad, pointed, finely toothed leaves with either no central vein or a short, double one.

sources.title: Nogopterium in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A tuberous perennial native from Zimbabwe to South Africa, primarily growing in subtropical environments.

sources.title: Gloriosa modesta (Hook.) J.C.Manning & Vinn. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A succulent perennial native to southern tropical and southern Africa, primarily found in deserts or dry shrubland.

sources.title: Bulbine latifolia (L.f.) Spreng. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A moss of unspecified native origin, usually dark red to red-green and sometimes purple-black. Its tightly overlapping leaves and stems have a metallic sheen, and it grows on damp or wet silica-rich rock and nearby soil, often around waterfalls or springs.

sources.title: Imbribryum miniatum in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A deciduous shrub of unspecified native origin that may grow upright or climb. Its non-fragrant white flowers appear after the leaves, followed by compressed, egg-shaped fruit that ripens red.

sources.title: Viburnum foetidum in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A red seaweed of unspecified native origin, forming leathery tufts that range from brownish red to dark purple or black and may bleach brown in summer. Its highly variable branches arise above a tough, flexible, branch-free base, and it tolerates substrates ranging from pebbles and bedrock to marina pontoons.

sources.title: Black siphon weed (Vertebrata fucoides) - MarLIN - The Marine Life Information Network

stories.summary: A shrub or tree native from Bolivia to Brazil and northern Argentina, primarily growing in seasonally dry tropical environments.

sources.title: Vassobia breviflora (Sendtn.) Hunz. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An aquatic perennial native to Cambodia, the Philippines, New Guinea through northern Australia, and New Caledonia, primarily growing in wet tropical environments.

sources.title: Vallisneria nana R.Br. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A seaweed of unspecified native origin, with a thin blade rising from a disc-shaped attachment and dividing irregularly into forks, often from the margins. It grows on rocks or other plants and is rarely found on the shore but occurs below low tide to depths of 30 metres.
A shrub native to Daitojima in the Nansei Islands and the Ogasawara Islands, primarily growing in subtropical environments.

sources.title: Zanthoxylum beecheyanum K.Koch — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A shrub found in mountain forests of central Taiwan. Its young shoots have dense, coarse red-brown hairs, while its pink, funnel-shaped flowers bear darker pink flecks.

sources.title: Rhododendron rubropilosum in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A low deciduous shrub found in Taiwan’s open grasslands. It has small, stiff leaves and red to dark purple funnel-shaped flowers with protruding stamens; the account’s authors had seen no specimens themselves.

sources.title: Rhododendron noriakianum in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A climbing shrub native to Taiwan, including forests and mountain slopes on the Hengchun Peninsula. Its four-sided branches have rings of long hairs at the nodes, and it produces nearly spherical berries.

sources.title: Medinilla formosana in Flora of China @ efloras.org
Medinilla formosana Hayata — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A low, spreading, semi-evergreen shrub native to Taiwan. It has thick, leathery leaves, solitary white flowers and red oval fruits, and grows in sunny rocky high-mountain habitats.

sources.title: Cotoneaster morrisonensis in Flora of China @ efloras.org
Cotoneaster morrisonensis Hayata — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A temperate plant native to the northwestern North Island of New Zealand.

sources.title: Veronica macrocarpa Vahl — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A shrub found in Taiwan’s mountain forests and slopes. Its young branches are densely hairy, its leaves have pale, hairy undersides and sharply toothed edges, and its upright leafy shoots carry large, many-flowered terminal clusters.

sources.title: Spiraea formosana in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A seaweed with no native origin supplied. It grows around the high-water mark on muddy British and Irish shores, often attached to the lower stems of saltmarsh flowering plants, and can be locally abundant.

sources.title: Bostrychia scorpioides (Hudson) Montagne ex Kützing — Seaweed.ie, Michael D. Guiry

stories.summary: A seaweed with no native origin supplied. Its thin, single-layered fronds range from olive-green to brown-purple or blackish and hang from rocks on sandy, semi-exposed shores; it is most common in spring and early summer.
A perennial plant with underground stems, native to Madeira. It grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

sources.title: Semele menezesii J.G.Costa — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A seaweed with no native origin supplied. It has firm, fleshy, flattened dark-red fronds with repeated forks, often paler blunt tips and irregularly sculpted edges; reproductive growths resemble external warts.

sources.title: Gymnogongrus crenulatus J. Agardh — Seaweed.ie, Michael D. Guiry

stories.summary: A plant species native to Mozambique, growing mainly in seasonally dry tropical areas.

sources.title: Aloe ribauensis T.A.McCoy, Rulkens & O.J.Baptista — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A liverwort of unspecified native origin, associated locally with sheltered, acidic places in rainy areas and oceanic oakwoods. It is relatively large, yellow-brown and untidy-looking, with loose leaf lobes and an often recurved upper lobe.

A seaweed of unspecified native origin that forms dense, brownish-red, tassel-like tufts of lightly branched hair-like filaments. It grows on limpets along exposed shores and sometimes on Codium fragile in the lower intertidal zone.

sources.title: Colaconema caespitosum (J. Agardh) Jackelman, Stegenga & Bolton — Seaweed.ie, Michael D. Guiry

stories.summary: An annual or perennial plant native to central and eastern Spain, growing mainly in the temperate biome.

sources.title: Ionopsidium glastifolium (L.) M.Koch — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A plant of unspecified native origin, found locally in humid western woodlands and sheltered, north-facing rocky places. It has conspicuous, relatively sparse teeth along the leaf margins and can be difficult to distinguish from Plagiochila bifaria without microscopic examination.
A perennial plant native to Madeira, growing mainly in the temperate biome.

sources.title: Viola sequeirae Capelo, R.Jardim, J.C.Costa, Lousã & Rivas Mart. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial plant native to the Mediterranean region, growing mainly in the subtropical biome.

sources.title: Oloptum thomasii (Duby) Banfi & Galasso — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A fern of unspecified native origin, recorded in lower mountain areas of southeastern Taiwan and parts of southern Asia, Japan, Africa and Indonesia. It has a short upright rhizome with brown hairy scales and clustered, lance-shaped fronds that are deep green when dry and hairy on both surfaces.

sources.title: Leptogramma pozoi in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: An annual plant native from Macaronesia and the Mediterranean region eastward to the Caucasus, growing mainly in the temperate biome.

sources.title: Vicia lentoides (Ten.) Coss. & Germ. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A winter annual or biennial native to South America and introduced widely elsewhere. It has basal leaves that remain as a rosette during flowering, with white-felted undersides, and dense flower-head arrays that later become branched and interrupted.

sources.title: Gamochaeta impatiens in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A small alga whose native origin is not supplied. It grows in upright tufts with whorled branches and lives attached to animals or other plants from the lower shore to shallow water.
A shrub or tree native from western South America to Venezuela. It grows mainly in wet tropical environments and is used medicinally.

sources.title: Varronia cylindristachya Ruiz & Pav. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An annual plant native from Portugal to southern Italy and northwestern Africa. It grows mainly in temperate environments.

sources.title: Avena castellana (Romero Zarco) Romero Zarco & L.Sáez — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: An annual plant native to the Mediterranean and La Gomera in the Canary Islands. It grows mainly in subtropical environments.

sources.title: Avena hirtula Lag. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A red-to-brown alga native to Asia and the Indo-Pacific and introduced in Europe and northwestern North America. Its fine, irregularly branching stems intertwine into pom-poms and can form dense mats on rocks, mussels, other algae or gravel.

A genus of three annual plants from the western Mediterranean basin. Its flowers have two stamens, making the genus easy to recognize within its group. Fruit shape varies markedly within each species, while flower colour and shape help distinguish the three species.

A perennial succulent native to the Tehuacán-Cuicatlán region of Puebla in southern Mexico, where it grows in semi-desert. Its creeping or cascading fleshy stems carry rosettes of thick, waxy green to grey-green leaves, often tinged purple. Small pale pink to purple star-shaped flowers appear in spring or summer.
A scrambling shrub native to western Europe, growing mainly in the temperate biome.

sources.title: Rubus elegantispinosus (A.Schumach.) H.E.Weber — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A temperate plant native from the Cape Province through Lesotho to KwaZulu-Natal.

sources.title: Cotula lineariloba (DC.) Hilliard — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A genus of flowering plants native from Mozambique to southern Africa. It contains only one known species, Helichrysopsis septentrionalis.

sources.title: Helichrysopsis Kirp. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A section of plants within the genus Dendrobium, found from India east to New Guinea and Australia and north to Japan and Korea. Its plants have slender, moderately long pseudobulbs, with leaves along their upper two-thirds.

An evergreen hybrid shrub of garden origin, derived from Holantarctic Veronica elliptica and New Zealand Veronica speciosa. It has glossy dark-green leaves and dense clusters of blue-violet flowers with white throats. It tolerates salt spray and wind but is vulnerable to hard frost, especially inland.

sources.title: VERONICA ×FRANCISCANA  (Eastw.) J. T. Howell, P. H. Raven et P. Rubtzoff – rozrazil / veronika | BOTANY.cz

stories.summary: A dark red seaweed native to the northwestern Pacific. It may form large mats, growing either as bushy clumps or long, irregularly branched strands whose hollow sections can feel elastic. It favours sheltered muddy waters such as bays, harbours and estuaries.

sources.title: Gracilaria vermiculophylla (Ohmi) Papenfuss, 1967 — National Museums Northern Ireland, Habitas

stories.summary: A marine alga with no native origin stated. Its upright growth forms dense tufts, with rootlike filaments creating a thick outer layer. It grows on other plants, animals or rock along the lower shore.

sources.title: Callithamnion granulatum (Ducluzeau) C Agardh — National Museums Northern Ireland, Habitas

stories.summary: An evergreen tree native to central China, chiefly along the Yangtze River. Its crown has strongly drooping branches: young trees are narrow and pointed, while older trees develop a broader, eventually flattened crown. The brown bark becomes divided into short, irregular yellow-brown strips.
stories.edibilityNote: In its homeland, branches are used to smoke pork and the ash to pickle duck eggs.

stories.summary: A succulent with no explicitly stated native origin, occurring in central and southern Europe, especially the Alps and western Balkans. It is a hardy, prolific plant of dry, stony limestone ground, with stronger and less trailing growth than Petrosedum montanum.
A flowering orchid endemic to the island of São Tomé.

A seaweed with no native origin stated. It grows on rock, sending creeping stems through sponges and soft rock from the lower shore into waters about 25 metres deep. Around Britain and Ireland it is widespread but uncommon.

sources.title: Rhodymenia holmesii Ardissone — Seaweed.ie, Michael D. Guiry

stories.summary: A red alga with no native origin stated. Its upright cylindrical fronds branch irregularly at very narrow angles and end in rounded tips; the cells are large enough to see unaided. It is recorded as very rare on submerged rock in shallow water.

sources.title: Bornetia secundiflora (J Agardh) Thuret — National Museums Northern Ireland, Habitas

stories.summary: A marine alga with no native origin stated. It grows upright with a cylindrical form and dense, overlapping rings of divided branches. It occurs on rock in lower-shore pools and underwater.

sources.title: Halurus equisetifolius (Lightfoot) Kützing — National Museums Northern Ireland, Habitas

stories.summary: A calcareous alga with no native origin stated. It forms either a thin hard crust on firm surfaces or loose, fragile branched nodules that can gather into dense gravel-like beds. Living plants are reddish to deep pink with a violet tinge, turning white after death.

sources.title: Boreolithothamnion glaciale nodules amongst pebbles with the sunstar Crossaster papposus, Isle of Lewis. — MarLIN, Marine Biological Association

stories.summary: An epiphytic subshrub native to tropical Africa, growing mainly in wet tropical habitats.

sources.title: Tridactyle tridactylites (Rolfe) Schltr. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A riverside moss with no native origin stated. When wet, its tongue-shaped leaves show thickened, scalloped borders; older leaves often split neatly into rectangular fragments.
An annual plant native to the Canary Islands and from the western Mediterranean east to western Italy, growing mainly in subtropical regions.

sources.title: Festuca alopecuros Schousb. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A temperate plant native to Portugal.

sources.title: Centaurea francoi Figueiredo & Gideon F.Sm. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A herbaceous perennial hybrid with no native origin stated. It forms fast-growing arching clumps and has flowers in many solid or two-toned colors, sometimes with ruffled or patterned edges.

sources.title: Daylily - Hemerocallis hybrida | North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
sources.attribution: North Carolina State University Extension Plant Toolbox

stories.summary: A tuber-forming plant native from western Portugal to western and southwestern Spain, growing mainly in temperate regions.

sources.title: Crocus clusii J.Gay — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A climbing, tuber-forming plant native to Madeira and the Canary Islands, growing mainly in subtropical regions.

sources.title: Dioscorea edulis (Lowe) M.Campos, Wilkin & Viruel — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A fully parasitic plant native to the Canary Islands and western Mediterranean, growing mainly in subtropical regions.

sources.title: Orobanche castellana Reut. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A short-rhizomed plant recorded from western and central Europe east to central Siberia, with no explicitly stated native origin. Its much-branched, deeply grooved solid stem bears twice-divided basal leaves whose lowest leaflet pair is conspicuously unequal.

sources.title: LIBANOTIS PYRENAICA (L.) Bourgeau – žebřice pyrenejská / rebrica pyrenejská | BOTANY.cz

stories.summary: A genus of herbs, undershrubs and shrubs widely distributed across the Old and New Worlds. Its leaves range from a single leaflet to feather-like arrangements, while flowers may stand alone or form varied clusters and range from violet or purple to white or pale yellow.

sources.title: Astragalus in Flora of Pakistan @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of shrubs, sometimes trees or vines, occurring in the southeastern United States, Cuba and eastern Asia. Its evergreen or deciduous leaves are often toothed, and its clustered white, urn-shaped flowers are followed by dry capsules containing many seeds.

sources.title: Pieris in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A perennial evergreen genus native to the southeastern United States and introduced elsewhere. Its leaves have two hinged lobes edged with stout bristles; three trigger hairs on each inner surface cause the trap to snap shut when properly stimulated.

sources.title: Dionaea in Flora of North America @ efloras.org
Dionaea J.Ellis — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A genus of aromatic, gland-covered herbs, subshrubs and shrubs, widely distributed and especially associated with western North America. Male and female flower heads are separate but often occur on the same plant, with female heads developing spiny-tipped coverings around the fruits.

sources.title: Ambrosia in Trees and shrubs of the Andes of Ecuador @ efloras.org
sources.attribution: Trees and shrubs of the Andes of Ecuador, eFloras

stories.summary: A genus of mostly perennial herbs found mainly in Asia and Europe, with one species in North America and a few in East Africa. Many species are robust and tall, bearing broad-based compound leaves and spreading umbrella-shaped clusters of mostly white flowers.

sources.title: Heracleum in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of annual, occasionally perennial herbs from Eurasia and northern Africa, introduced nearly worldwide. Its yellow flowers form clusters that lengthen as fruits develop, and its pods have a seed-bearing section plus a terminal section that may be seedless or hold one or two seeds.

sources.title: Sinapis in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of perennial evergreen, mat-forming herbs from tropical Africa, Asia, Australia and Polynesia, introduced in North America. Stout creeping underground stems produce crowded, firm basal leaves, while the flowers are followed by long-lasting blue to bluish-purple berries.

sources.title: Dianella in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of annual or perennial herbs, subshrubs and shrubs distributed through the tropics and subtropics of both hemispheres, with about two-thirds of its species restricted to the Americas. Most are hairy, with alternate leaves and flowers ranging from yellow or white to pink or orange.

sources.title: Sida in Flora of Pakistan @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A very small moss found in China, India, Japan and Africa, where it grows on rocks. It forms dense tufts containing both fertile and sterile stems, with narrow pointed leaves and upright cylindrical capsules.

sources.title: Fissidens curvatus in Moss Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A moss species recorded reproducing in Sweden and classified as endangered in Finland. It inhabits limestone cliffs and limestone quarries.
A liverwort species of unstated native origin, blue crystalwort is recorded across Europe, Africa, Australia and both North and South America.
A tree genus native to Africa, Tamarindus has one species and is widely cultivated across the tropics. It has paired leaflets, small flower clusters and pods with thick pulp surrounding the seeds.

sources.title: Tamarindus in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A moss genus of unstated native origin, Ditrichum occurs on every continent, including maritime Antarctica, from near sea level to mountain regions. Its plants form green to yellow-green tufts, and their capsules typically have 16 teeth split into threadlike segments.

sources.title: Ditrichum in Bryophyte Flora of North America @ efloras.org
sources.attribution: Bryophyte Flora of North America, eFloras

stories.summary: A mostly perennial herb genus of unstated native origin, Cota occurs in Europe, southwestern Asia and northern Africa; its North American representative is introduced. It typically has upright stems, deeply divided leaves and flower heads with yellow rays surrounding many small central flowers.

sources.title: Cota in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A moss genus of unstated native origin, Racomitrium occurs across much of the world, including Antarctica. Its coarse, rigid plants are usually greyish or brownish, with many short side branches and leaves ending in long, pale, rough-edged points. The fruiting stalks have a uniquely roughened surface among upright mosses.

sources.title: Racomitrium in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of annual or perennial herbs of unstated native origin, Glycine occurs across tropical, subtropical and temperate parts of the Eastern Hemisphere. Its members may twine, climb, creep or stand erect, usually bearing root nodules and leaves divided into three leaflets. Their pods split open and the valves coil afterward.

sources.title: Glycine in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A genus of perennial herbs of unstated native origin, Gloriosa occurs in southern and tropical Africa and tropical Asia. Its elongated stems often climb using tendrils at the leaf tips, while the large, showy flowers have six spreading or swept-back segments. The seeds have bright red, spongy coats.

sources.title: Gloriosa in Flora of China @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A moss genus of unstated native origin, Gymnostomum occurs worldwide except Antarctica and favors moist, lime-rich environments. It forms green turf or cushions, with leaves that spread outward when moist but draw inward when dry. Its capsules lack teeth around their openings.

sources.title: Gymnostomum in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A shrub native to tropical and subtropical America, shrubby Indian mallow grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical areas and open, arid habitats. It has roughly hairy stems and leaves, with orange-yellow flowers appearing throughout the year.

sources.title: Abutilon abutiloides in Flora of North America @ efloras.org
Abutilon abutiloides (Jacq.) Garcke ex Hochr. — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A climbing shrub or liana native to southwestern Texas, sevenleaf creeper is endemic to the Edwards Plateau and Lampasas Cut Plain. Its leaves usually have seven thick, glossy leaflets, while its branched tendrils lack adhesive discs. It bears greenish to reddish-green flowers followed by rounded berries.

sources.title: Parthenocissus heptaphylla in Flora of North America @ efloras.org
Parthenocissus heptaphylla (Planch.) Britton — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A leafy moss species of unspecified native origin, Small Twisted Moss is usually dull dark green or yellow-green above and brown to black below. Its leaves curl or twist when dry and spread when moist, while its well-developed reproductive teeth are conspicuously twisted.

sources.title: Tortella humilis in Flora of North America @ efloras.org

stories.summary: A shrub or tree native from Mexico to Honduras, the Caribbean to Venezuela, and eastern Brazil, desert senna grows mainly in wet tropical regions.

sources.title: Senna polyphylla (Jacq.) H.S.Irwin & Barneby — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A tree genus distributed chiefly in the Old World tropics, Pterygota has usually unlobed, heart-shaped leaves. Its flowers lack petals, and its woody, nearly spherical fruits contain numerous seeds, each with a long or broad blade-shaped wing.

sources.title: Pterygota in Flora of Pakistan @ efloras.org

stories.summary: An annual native to Madeira and the Canary Islands, Luzula elegans is restricted there to Madeira Island and the islands of Gran Canaria, Tenerife, La Gomera, El Hierro and La Palma.

sources.title: Luzula elegans Lowe — Plants of the World Online
sources.attribution: Plants of the World Online, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

stories.summary: A perennial hybrid native from the Caucasus through Central Asia and Iran, Sand Lucerne grows mainly in temperate regions. It is the hybrid of Medicago falcata and Medicago sativa.

sources.title: Medicago × varia Martyn — Plants of the World Online
